ingredients: 1 kg beef shin or chuck (paleron), in large pieces
600 g beef short rib (plat de côtes)
2 marrow bones (os à moelle), about 400 g
1 onion, halved and studded with 3 cloves
1 bouquet garni (thyme, bay leaf, parsley stalks)
3 leeks, trimmed and tied in a bundle
1 tbsp coarse salt and 10 black peppercorns
steps: Put the beef and short rib in a large pot, cover with 4 litres of cold water, bring slowly to a simmer and skim off the grey foam for 10 minutes.
Add the onion, bouquet garni, salt and peppercorns, then keep at a bare simmer, lid ajar, for 2 hours.
Add the carrots, leeks and turnips and simmer 45 minutes; wrap the marrow bones' ends in foil and add them for the last 20 minutes.
Boil the potatoes separately in a ladle of the broth and salted water for 20 minutes until tender.
Serve the clear broth first as a soup, then the sliced meat and vegetables with coarse salt (gros sel), cornichons and Dijon mustard, spreading the marrow on toasted bread.

ingredients: 1.2 kg veal shoulder or breast, in 5 cm pieces
250 g button mushrooms (champignons de Paris), quartered
steps: Cover the veal with cold water, bring to the boil, drain and rinse, then return to the pot with 1.5 litres fresh water, the onion, carrots and bouquet garni.
Simmer gently, partly covered, for 1 hour 30 minutes until the veal is fork-tender; meanwhile cook the mushrooms and pearl onions in a knob of butter and a splash of water for 10 minutes.
Strain off 750 ml of the cooking stock; melt the butter, stir in the flour for 2 minutes without colouring, then whisk in the stock and simmer 10 minutes to a velvety sauce.
Whisk the yolks with the crème fraîche and lemon juice, stir into the sauce off the heat and warm gently without boiling.
Fold in the veal, mushrooms and onions, check the seasoning and serve with white rice.

ingredients: 1.2 kg floury potatoes, peeled and cubed
700 g minced beef (or leftover pot-au-feu beef, chopped)
1 tsp thyme and a handful of chopped parsley
steps: Boil the potatoes in salted water for 20 minutes until soft, drain and mash with the milk, 40 g butter, salt and a pinch of nutmeg.
Soften the onions in the oil over medium heat for 8 minutes, add the garlic and beef and cook, breaking it up, until no pink remains, about 10 minutes.
Stir in the tomato paste, thyme, parsley, salt and pepper and cook 5 minutes more.
Spread the meat in a buttered baking dish, cover with the mash, ridge with a fork, scatter with cheese and dot with the remaining butter.
Bake at 200°C for 25 minutes until the top is golden and bubbling; serve with a green salad.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 2 entrecôte (rib-eye) or bavette steaks, about 250 g each
1.5 litres sunflower or peanut oil, for frying
fleur de sel and black pepper
steps: Cut the potatoes into 1 cm sticks, rinse and dry thoroughly; fry at 150°C for 6 minutes until soft but pale, then drain.
Bring the steaks to room temperature and season; heat a heavy pan until very hot and sear them 2–3 minutes per side for medium-rare (internal 54°C), adding the butter for the last minute and basting.
Rest the steaks 5 minutes; in the same pan soften the shallot for 1 minute and stir in the parsley.
Refry the chips at 180°C for 2–3 minutes until crisp and golden, drain and salt immediately.
Serve the steaks with the shallot butter spooned over, the frites alongside, and Dijon mustard or béarnaise.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 2 beef fillet or sirloin steaks, 3 cm thick
120 ml crème fraîche or double cream
steps: Press the crushed pepper firmly into both sides of the steaks and salt them lightly.
Heat the oil in a heavy pan over high heat and sear the steaks 3–4 minutes per side for medium-rare, adding the butter in the last minute; rest them on a warm plate.
Lower the heat, soften the shallot in the pan for 1 minute, then add the Cognac and carefully flambé or let it bubble away.
Add the stock and reduce by half, stir in the cream and simmer 2 minutes until it coats a spoon.
Pour the sauce over the steaks and serve with frites or sautéed potatoes.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 1 tsp fine salt and black pepper
steps: Take the chicken out of the fridge 30 minutes ahead and heat the oven to 210°C.
Rub the bird all over with butter, salt and pepper and stuff the cavity with lemon, a few garlic cloves and thyme.
Set it on its side in a roasting dish with the remaining garlic and roast 25 minutes, turn onto the other side for 25 minutes, then breast-up for 25 minutes more, basting each time.
Check the thigh juices run clear (74°C at the thickest part), then rest the chicken 10 minutes.
Deglaze the dish with the water over heat, scraping up the juices, and serve the jus with the carved chicken, frites or a green salad.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 1 chicken, about 1.5 kg, cut into 8 pieces
2 tbsp sunflower oil and 20 g butter
3 tomatoes, peeled and diced (or 200 g canned)
steps: Season the chicken and brown it in the oil and butter in a casserole over medium-high heat, about 10 minutes, then set aside.
Cook the shallots and mushrooms in the fat for 5 minutes, sprinkle over the flour and stir 1 minute.
Add the wine and boil 2 minutes, then the tomatoes, stock and bouquet garni.
Return the chicken, cover and simmer gently for 35–40 minutes until cooked through.
Stir in the tarragon and parsley and serve with boiled potatoes or tagliatelle.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 1 chicken, about 1.5 kg, cut into 8 pieces
2 eggs, fried, and 4 slices fried bread (croûtons), to serve
steps: Season the chicken and brown it in the olive oil in a sauté pan over medium-high heat for 10 minutes.
Add the onion and garlic for 3 minutes, pour in the brandy and wine and boil 2 minutes.
Add the tomatoes and mushrooms, cover and simmer 35 minutes until the chicken is cooked through.
Lay the prawns on top for the last 5 minutes until pink and opaque.
Serve in the classic style, with croûtons and a fried egg alongside each portion.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 1 leg of lamb, about 2 kg, bone in
6 garlic cloves, 3 cut in slivers and 3 whole
800 g flageolet beans, cooked (canned is fine), to serve
steps: Make small cuts all over the lamb and push in the garlic slivers and a few rosemary needles; rub with oil, salt and pepper.
Roast at 220°C for 15 minutes, then lower to 180°C and roast about 15 minutes per 500 g for pink meat (internal 57°C), basting twice.
Rest the lamb under foil for 15 minutes.
Deglaze the roasting tin with the water and butter over heat, scraping well, and warm the flageolets with the whole garlic and thyme in some of this jus.
Carve into thin slices and serve with the flageolets and jus.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 1.5 kg beef topside or chuck in one piece, tied
1 calf's foot or 2 pig's trotters, split (optional, for body)
steps: Marinate the beef overnight in the fridge with the wine, Cognac, onions, bouquet garni and cloves.
Drain and dry the beef, keeping the marinade; brown it all over in the oil in a heavy casserole, about 10 minutes.
Add the marinade, stock and calf's foot, bring to a simmer and cook covered in a 150°C oven for 2 hours 30 minutes.
Add the carrots and cook 1 hour more until the beef is very tender; skim off the fat and reduce the sauce a little on the hob.
Slice the beef and serve hot with the carrots and sauce, or chill it overnight in its jelly to serve cold.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 1 rabbit, about 1.4 kg, cut into pieces (or 4 chicken legs)
2 tbsp sunflower oil and 20 g butter
steps: Season the rabbit and brush it all over with 3 tbsp mustard.
Brown the pieces in the oil and butter in a casserole over medium heat for 10 minutes; add the lardons and shallots for 5 minutes.
Pour in the wine, add the thyme, cover and simmer gently 45–50 minutes until the meat comes easily off the bone.
Stir in the crème fraîche and remaining mustard and simmer 5 minutes without boiling hard.
Serve with tagliatelle or steamed potatoes.

ingredients: 2 large duck breasts (magrets), about 400 g each
3 oranges, juiced, plus zest of 1 in fine strips
2 tbsp sherry or red wine vinegar
steps: Score the duck skin in a criss-cross and season; place skin-down in a cold pan and cook over medium heat for 10–12 minutes until the fat renders and the skin is crisp, pouring off fat as you go.
Turn and cook 4 minutes for pink meat (internal 57°C), then rest 8 minutes.
Blanch the zest strips in boiling water 2 minutes; in a small pan melt the sugar to a light caramel, add the vinegar (gastrique), then the orange juice and stock and reduce by half.
Add the liqueur and zest, then whisk in the cold butter off the heat.
Slice the duck and spoon over the sauce; serve with pommes purée or gratin.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 2 Dover soles, about 400 g each, skinned and trimmed (or plaice)
steps: Season the soles and dust them in flour, shaking off the excess.
Heat the oil and 20 g butter in a large pan over medium-high heat and cook the fish 4–5 minutes per side until golden and the flesh lifts from the bone.
Transfer to warm plates, wipe the pan and melt the remaining butter until it foams and turns nut-brown (beurre noisette).
Off the heat add the lemon juice and parsley, then pour the sizzling butter over the fish.
Serve at once with lemon wedges and steamed potatoes.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 12 king scallops with coral, plus 4 cleaned scallop shells or gratin dishes
40 g grated Gruyère and 2 tbsp breadcrumbs
steps: Poach the scallops gently in the wine with the shallot for 2 minutes, lift out and slice each in half; keep the liquor.
Cook the mushrooms in 15 g butter for 5 minutes until their liquid evaporates.
Melt the rest of the butter, stir in the flour for 1 minute, whisk in the poaching liquor and cream and simmer 5 minutes; off the heat stir in the egg yolk and season.
Divide the scallops and mushrooms among the shells, coat with sauce and sprinkle with cheese and breadcrumbs.
Grill under a hot grill for 4–5 minutes until bubbling and golden; serve straight away.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 4 thin veal escalopes, about 120 g each, beaten flat
steps: Mix the sausage meat with the shallot, garlic and parsley and spread a quarter on each escalope.
Roll up, wrap each in bacon and tie with kitchen string like a small parcel.
Brown the paupiettes in the butter and oil in a casserole for 8 minutes, then add the carrots and onion for 5 minutes.
Add the wine, stock and tomato paste, cover and simmer gently for 45 minutes, turning once, until cooked through (72°C in the centre).
Remove the string, reduce the sauce slightly and serve with rice or fresh pasta.

ingredients: 4 boudin noir (French black pudding), about 600 g
4 apples (Reinette or Golden), peeled and cut in eighths
steps: Prick the boudins lightly with a pin so they do not burst.
Melt the butter in a pan, add the apples and sugar and cook over medium heat for 10–12 minutes, turning, until golden and tender; add the cider at the end.
Meanwhile heat the oil in another pan and fry the boudins gently over medium-low heat for 10 minutes, turning, until hot through and the skin is crisp.
Serve the boudin with the caramelised apples and pommes purée.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 400 g sausage meat or mixed pork and veal mince
30 g stale bread soaked in 3 tbsp milk
steps: Cut a lid off each tomato, scoop out the pulp into the base of a baking dish and salt the insides, turning them upside down to drain for 10 minutes.
Mix the meat with the onion, garlic, squeezed bread, egg, parsley, salt and pepper.
Fill the tomatoes generously, replace the lids and set them in the dish; scatter the raw rice into the tomato pulp around them with 200 ml water.
Drizzle with olive oil and bake at 180°C for 50 minutes until the stuffing is cooked through (72°C) and the rice has absorbed the juices.
Serve hot with the rice from the dish.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 4 large ready-made puff pastry cases (vol-au-vent shells)
200 g veal sweetbreads or extra chicken thigh (common substitute)
steps: Poach the chicken (and sweetbreads, if using) in the simmering stock for 15 minutes until cooked through, then cut into small pieces; keep the stock.
Cook the mushrooms in 10 g butter for 5 minutes.
Melt the remaining butter, stir in the flour for 2 minutes, whisk in 400 ml stock and simmer 8 minutes; add the cream, then off the heat the egg yolk and lemon juice.
Fold in the chicken and mushrooms and season with salt, white pepper and nutmeg.
Warm the pastry cases at 180°C for 8 minutes, fill with the hot ragoût, add the lids and serve with a green salad.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 4 thick slices jambon de Paris (cooked ham), diced
steps: Boil the coquillettes in plenty of salted water for 8–9 minutes until just tender, then drain, keeping a few spoonfuls of cooking water.
Return the pasta to the pan over low heat with the butter, crème fraîche and a splash of the water and stir until glossy.
Fold in the ham and half the cheese and heat through for 2 minutes.
Serve topped with the rest of the cheese and plenty of black pepper.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 1 tsp chopped chervil and tarragon (fines herbes)
steps: Beat the eggs lightly with a fork with salt, pepper and most of the herbs.
Melt the butter in a 20 cm non-stick pan over medium-high heat until it foams.
Pour in the eggs and stir quickly with a fork while shaking the pan for about 1 minute until softly set but still creamy (baveuse) on top.
Tilt the pan and fold the omelette into thirds, roll it onto a warm plate seam-down and sprinkle with the remaining herbs.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 40 g butter, plus extra for the dish
2 tbsp grated Parmesan or fine breadcrumbs, for the dish
steps: Butter a 1.5 litre soufflé dish with upward strokes and coat with Parmesan; heat the oven to 200°C with a baking tray inside.
Make a thick béchamel: melt the butter, stir in the flour for 1 minute, whisk in the milk and cook 3 minutes; off the heat beat in the yolks, cheese, mustard, nutmeg, cayenne, salt and pepper.
Whisk the 5 whites with a pinch of salt to firm peaks; stir a quarter into the base, then gently fold in the rest.
Pour into the dish, run a thumb round the inside rim and bake on the hot tray, lowering to 190°C, for 25–28 minutes until risen, golden and just wobbly in the centre.
Serve immediately, before it falls.

ingredients: salt, pepper and a pinch of paprika
steps: Lower the eggs into boiling water and cook 10 minutes, then cool in iced water and peel.
Halve lengthwise and remove the yolks; set aside 2 yolks for garnish.
Mash the remaining yolks with mayonnaise, mustard, salt and pepper and pipe or spoon back into the whites.
Press the reserved yolks through a sieve over the eggs to look like mimosa flowers, then sprinkle with herbs and paprika; chill until serving.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 250 g pork or chicken livers, trimmed and finely chopped
1 tsp quatre-épices (or mix of pepper, nutmeg, clove, ginger)
16 g fine salt and 1 tsp black pepper
150 g caul fat or thin bacon rashers, to line
steps: Mix the meats, livers, shallots, garlic, egg, Cognac, spices, salt and pepper thoroughly; cover and chill overnight so the flavours develop.
Line a 1.2 litre terrine with caul fat or bacon, pack in the mixture firmly, fold over the overhang and top with thyme and bay.
Cover and set in a roasting tin half-filled with hot water; bake at 160°C for about 1 hour 45 minutes to 2 hours until the centre reads 70°C.
Cool, then press with a weight (a board and two cans) and refrigerate at least 24 hours.
Slice and serve with crusty bread, cornichons and pickled onions.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 500 g plain flour, 250 g cold butter, 1 egg, 1 tsp salt and 100 ml cold water (hot-water or shortcrust pastry)
300 g veal or chicken thigh, minced
200 g chicken breast or duck breast, cut in strips
1 tsp quatre-épices, 14 g salt and 1 tsp pepper
300 ml chicken stock with 3 gelatine leaves, for the jelly
steps: Rub the butter into the flour and salt, bind with the egg and water, and chill 1 hour; marinate the strips in Cognac and mix the minced meats with shallot, spices, salt and pepper, then chill everything overnight.
Line a hinged pâté mould or loaf tin with three quarters of the pastry, fill with layers of farce, strips and ham, and cover with a pastry lid, sealing well; cut two chimneys in the top.
Glaze with egg yolk and bake at 200°C for 15 minutes, then 170°C for about 1 hour 30 minutes until the filling reaches 68–70°C.
Cool completely, then pour the warm gelatine stock through the chimneys to fill the gaps and refrigerate 24 hours.
Slice thickly and serve cold with cornichons and a green salad.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 2 live lobsters, about 600 g each (or 1 kg lobster or langoustine shells)
3 tbsp olive oil and 30 g butter
1 onion, 1 carrot and 1 celery stick, finely diced
steps: Plunge the lobsters into boiling salted water for 3 minutes, cool, then remove the tail and claw meat and chop the shells roughly.
Fry the shells in the oil over high heat for 5 minutes, add the vegetables and butter and cook 5 minutes, then the tomato paste for 1 minute.
Add the Cognac and let it bubble, then the wine, stock and rice; simmer 40 minutes.
Blend briefly, then press through a fine sieve, pressing hard on the solids; return to the pan with the cream and cayenne and simmer 5 minutes.
Slice the lobster meat, warm it in the bisque for 2 minutes until cooked through, and serve with croûtons.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 3 leeks, white and pale green parts, sliced
500 g floury potatoes, peeled and diced
steps: Melt the butter in a pot and sweat the leeks over low heat for 10 minutes until soft but not coloured.
Add the potatoes and stock, season and simmer 20–25 minutes until the potatoes collapse.
Blend until smooth (or leave rustic), then stir in the crème fraîche and reheat without boiling.
Serve sprinkled with chervil and black pepper, with crusty bread.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 1 kg pumpkin or butternut squash (potiron), peeled and cubed
150 ml single cream or whole milk
steps: Soften the onion in the butter over medium heat for 5 minutes.
Add the pumpkin, potato and stock, season and simmer 25 minutes until very tender.
Blend until silky, stir in the cream and nutmeg and reheat gently.
Serve topped with a swirl of cream and the pumpkin seeds.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 600 g button or chestnut mushrooms, sliced
steps: Melt the butter and soften the shallots and garlic for 4 minutes over medium heat.
Add the mushrooms and cook 8 minutes until they release and then reabsorb their juices; sprinkle over the flour and stir 1 minute.
Pour in the stock and simmer 15 minutes.
Blend until smooth, stir in the crème fraîche, season and serve with parsley and a few sautéed mushroom slices.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

steps: Peel the celeriac and cut it into fine matchsticks or grate coarsely; toss immediately with the lemon juice and a pinch of salt.
Whisk the egg yolk with the mustard, then add the oil in a thin stream, whisking, until thick; season and add the vinegar.
Fold the sauce through the celeriac and chill 30 minutes.
Serve as a starter with parsley, as part of crudités with grated carrots.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

steps: Grate the carrots finely.
Whisk the lemon juice, mustard, salt and pepper, then whisk in the oil.
Toss the carrots in the dressing and rest 10 minutes; sprinkle with parsley and serve chilled.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 2 small logs goat's cheese (bûche de chèvre), cut in 8 rounds
150 g mixed salad leaves (frisée, lamb's lettuce)
1 tbsp red wine vinegar, 1 tsp Dijon mustard, 3 tbsp walnut or olive oil
steps: Toast the baguette slices lightly, top each with a round of goat's cheese, a drizzle of honey and a few thyme leaves.
Grill under a hot grill for 4–5 minutes until the cheese is soft and golden.
Whisk the vinegar, mustard, oil, salt and pepper and toss with the leaves and walnuts.
Arrange two warm toasts on each plate of salad and serve at once.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 1 kg floury potatoes (Bintje or Russet), peeled
steps: Cook the potatoes in cold salted water brought to the boil, simmering 20–25 minutes until a knife slides in easily.
Drain well, dry them in the pan for 1 minute, then pass through a potato ricer or food mill.
Over low heat beat in the butter a little at a time, then the hot milk until smooth and supple.
Season with salt, pepper and nutmeg and serve at once.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 2 litres sunflower or peanut oil, or beef dripping for frying
steps: Peel and cut the potatoes into 1 cm sticks, rinse in cold water and dry very well on a towel.
Fry in batches at 150°C for 6–7 minutes until cooked through but pale; drain.
Raise the oil to 180°C and fry again 2–3 minutes until crisp and golden.
Drain on paper, salt immediately and serve hot.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

steps: Boil the potatoes for 20 minutes, drain, dry and pass through a ricer.
Make choux paste: bring the water, milk, butter and salt to the boil, add the flour all at once and stir 1 minute until it leaves the pan, then beat in the eggs one at a time.
Mix the choux paste with the potato and season with nutmeg.
Shape into walnut-sized balls with two spoons and fry at 175°C in batches for 3–4 minutes until puffed and golden.
Drain on paper, salt and serve with roast meats.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 2 egg yolks, plus 1 beaten egg to glaze
steps: Boil the potatoes for 20 minutes, drain and dry in the pan, then pass through a ricer.
Beat in the butter and yolks while hot and season with nutmeg, salt and pepper.
Pipe rosettes with a star nozzle onto a lined tray and brush gently with beaten egg.
Bake at 200°C for 15–20 minutes until the ridges are golden; serve with roasts.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 1.2 kg waxy potatoes (Charlotte or Yukon Gold), peeled
steps: Slice the potatoes very thinly (2 mm) on a mandoline; do not rinse.
Brush a 24 cm ovenproof frying pan with butter and arrange overlapping slices in neat circles, brushing each layer with butter and seasoning.
Cook on the hob over medium heat for 8 minutes until the base starts to brown, then press down and cover.
Bake at 200°C for 45–50 minutes until tender in the centre and crisp at the edges.
Rest 5 minutes, then invert onto a plate and cut into wedges.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 500 g fresh or frozen garden peas
1 Little Gem or soft butterhead lettuce, shredded
8 small spring onions or pearl onions
steps: Melt 30 g butter in a pan and soften the onions over low heat for 5 minutes.
Add the peas, lettuce, sugar, water, salt and pepper, cover and simmer gently for 12–15 minutes (8 for frozen peas) until tender.
Uncover and let most of the liquid evaporate, then swirl in the remaining butter.
Sprinkle with herbs and serve with roast chicken or lamb.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 600 g carrots, peeled and sliced in thin rounds
steps: Put the carrots in a wide pan with the butter, sugar, a pinch of salt and the water.
Cover and simmer over medium heat for 15 minutes until almost tender.
Uncover and cook 5–8 minutes more, shaking the pan, until the liquid has reduced to a shiny glaze.
Sprinkle with parsley and serve.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 500 g fine green beans (haricots verts), topped
steps: Cook the beans in a large pan of well-salted boiling water for 5–6 minutes until just tender, then refresh in iced water and drain.
Melt the butter in a pan and soften the shallot for 2 minutes over medium heat.
Toss in the beans and heat through for 2–3 minutes, season and finish with parsley.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

steps: Warm the milk in a small pan.
Melt the butter in a heavy saucepan, add the flour and stir over low heat for 2 minutes to make a pale roux.
Pour in the warm milk gradually, whisking constantly, then simmer 8–10 minutes until thick enough to coat a spoon.
Season with nutmeg, salt and pepper; use for gratins, croque-monsieur or lasagne.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

steps: Put the yolks and water in a heatproof bowl over a pan of barely simmering water.
Whisk continuously for 3–4 minutes until pale, thick and foamy and the mixture reaches about 65°C so the yolks are cooked safely.
Off the heat, whisk in the warm butter drop by drop, then in a thin stream, until thick and glossy.
Season with lemon juice, salt and cayenne and serve warm with asparagus, fish or eggs Benedict.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 2 tbsp chopped tarragon (estragon), plus 1 tbsp to finish
steps: Simmer the vinegar, wine, shallot, tarragon and pepper until reduced to about 2 tablespoons; cool slightly and strain.
Whisk the reduction with the yolks in a bowl over barely simmering water for 3–4 minutes until thick and foamy (about 65°C).
Off the heat whisk in the butter in a thin stream until thick and glossy.
Stir in the fresh tarragon and chervil, season and serve warm with steak frites.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 1 egg yolk, at room temperature (pasteurised if serving to vulnerable people)
1 tsp white wine vinegar or lemon juice
steps: Whisk the yolk with the mustard and a pinch of salt in a bowl set on a damp cloth.
Add the oil drop by drop at first, whisking constantly, then in a thin stream once it thickens.
Whisk in the vinegar, season, and keep chilled; use within 2 days.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 1 tbsp red or white wine vinegar
3 tbsp sunflower, olive or walnut oil
steps: Whisk the vinegar, mustard, salt and pepper until the salt dissolves.
Whisk in the oil gradually until emulsified, then add the shallot.
Toss with salad leaves just before serving.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 1 vanilla pod, split (or 1 tsp vanilla extract)
steps: Heat the milk with the vanilla pod and scraped seeds until steaming, then leave to infuse 10 minutes.
Whisk the yolks and sugar until pale, pour in the hot milk while whisking and return to the pan.
Cook over low heat, stirring constantly with a wooden spoon, until it coats the spoon and a finger drawn across leaves a clear line (82–84°C); do not boil.
Strain into a cold bowl and cool, stirring occasionally; serve with île flottante, cakes or tarts.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 500 g strong white flour or T45 flour
6 eggs, cold, plus 1 yolk for glaze
steps: Mix the flour, yeast, sugar and salt in a stand mixer, add the eggs and knead with the hook on medium for 10 minutes until elastic.
Add the butter a few pieces at a time and knead 8–10 minutes more until the dough is glossy and comes away from the bowl.
Cover and prove 1 hour at room temperature, then knock back and refrigerate overnight.
Shape into 8 balls and place in a buttered loaf tin (or form a brioche à tête), then prove 2 hours until doubled.
Brush with yolk mixed with milk and bake at 180°C for 25–30 minutes until deep golden and hollow-sounding; cool on a rack.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 150 g active sourdough starter (levain), or 3 g dried yeast
steps: Mix the flours and water and rest 30 minutes, then add the starter and salt and squeeze through until combined.
Over the next 2 hours give the dough 4 sets of stretch-and-folds, 30 minutes apart, then leave covered until about 50% risen.
Shape into a tight round, place seam-up in a floured basket (banneton) and refrigerate overnight (8–12 hours).
Heat a lidded cast-iron pot in the oven at 250°C for 45 minutes; turn the loaf in, slash the top and bake covered 20 minutes.
Uncover, lower to 230°C and bake 20–25 minutes more until dark and hollow-sounding; cool at least 1 hour before slicing.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 30 g butter, melted, plus extra for the pan
steps: Whisk the flour, sugar and salt with the eggs, then gradually whisk in the milk until smooth; stir in the melted butter and rum.
Rest the batter at least 1 hour in the fridge.
Heat a crêpe pan over medium-high heat, wipe with butter and pour in a small ladle of batter, swirling to coat thinly.
Cook 1 minute until the edges lift and the base is golden, flip and cook 30 seconds.
Serve warm with sugar and lemon, jam, or chocolate-hazelnut spread.

ingredients: zest of 1 orange and juice of 3 oranges
steps: Melt the butter and sugar in a wide pan over medium heat until lightly caramelised, about 3 minutes.
Add the orange zest and juice and simmer 4–5 minutes until syrupy, then stir in the Grand Marnier.
Dip each crêpe in the sauce, fold into quarters and arrange overlapping in the pan.
Warm the Cognac, pour over and carefully flambé, standing back; serve as soon as the flames die down.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 8 thick slices stale brioche or baguette
50 g caster sugar, plus extra to sprinkle
steps: Whisk the eggs, milk, sugar, vanilla and cinnamon in a shallow dish.
Soak the bread slices 30 seconds per side so they absorb the custard without falling apart.
Fry in the butter over medium heat for 2–3 minutes per side until golden and set in the middle.
Sprinkle with sugar and serve warm with fruit, crème fraîche or salted-butter caramel.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

steps: Melt the chocolate and butter over a pan of barely simmering water, then cool until just warm.
Stir in the egg yolks one at a time.
Whisk the whites with the salt to soft peaks, add the sugar and whisk to firm, glossy peaks.
Fold a third of the whites vigorously into the chocolate, then gently fold in the rest until no streaks remain.
Spoon into ramekins and chill at least 4 hours; note the eggs are raw, so avoid serving to pregnant women or the very young.

ingredients: 6 tbsp demerara or caster sugar, for the topping
steps: Heat the cream with the vanilla seeds and pod until steaming, then infuse 10 minutes and remove the pod.
Whisk the yolks and sugar without frothing, then stir in the warm cream.
Pour into 6 shallow ramekins in a roasting tin, add hot water halfway up and bake at 140°C for 35–45 minutes until set with a slight wobble.
Cool, then chill at least 4 hours.
Sprinkle each with a thin even layer of sugar and caramelise with a blowtorch until amber; serve within 30 minutes.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 150 g caster sugar and 3 tbsp water, for the caramel
steps: Heat the sugar and water without stirring until a deep amber caramel forms, then quickly pour into 6 ramekins and swirl to coat the bases.
Heat the milk with the vanilla until steaming.
Whisk the eggs, yolks and sugar, pour in the milk, strain and divide among the ramekins.
Bake in a water bath at 150°C for 35–40 minutes until just set; cool and chill at least 4 hours.
Run a knife round the edge and turn out onto plates so the caramel flows over.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 750 ml crème anglaise (see Crème Anglaise), chilled
100 g sugar and 3 tbsp water, for caramel
steps: Whisk the egg whites to soft peaks, add the sugar and whisk to stiff, glossy meringue.
Bring the milk to a bare simmer and poach large spoonfuls of meringue 1 minute per side until set; drain on a cloth.
Pour the chilled crème anglaise into shallow bowls and float the meringues on top.
Cook the sugar and water to an amber caramel and drizzle over in thin threads; scatter with almonds and serve.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 1 tsp sugar and a pinch of salt
150 g dark chocolate and 150 ml double cream, for the sauce
steps: Bring the water, milk, butter, sugar and salt to the boil, tip in the flour and beat over the heat for 1 minute until the paste leaves the pan.
Cool 5 minutes, then beat in the eggs one at a time to a smooth, glossy paste that falls from the spoon in a V.
Pipe 24 small balls onto a lined tray and bake at 190°C for 25–30 minutes until puffed and golden; pierce each and cool on a rack.
Heat the cream, pour over the chocolate and stir until smooth.
Split the choux buns, fill with a scoop of ice cream and pour over the hot chocolate sauce at the table.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 250 g plain flour, 125 g cold butter, 1 egg yolk, 40 g sugar and 3 tbsp cold water (pâte brisée)
3 tbsp apricot jam, warmed, for glaze
steps: Rub the butter into the flour and sugar, bind with the yolk and water, and chill 30 minutes.
Cook 2 of the apples, diced, with 20 g butter, 20 g sugar and vanilla for 15 minutes into a chunky compote.
Roll out the pastry to line a 26 cm tart tin, prick the base and spread with the compote.
Slice the remaining apples thinly and arrange in overlapping circles, brush with the rest of the butter, melted, and sprinkle with sugar.
Bake at 190°C for 40–45 minutes until the pastry is crisp and the apples golden; brush with apricot glaze and serve warm or cold.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 1 blind-baked 24 cm sweet pastry case (pâte sucrée)
4 unwaxed lemons, zest of 2 and juice of 4 (about 150 ml)
3 egg whites and 150 g caster sugar, for the Italian meringue
steps: Whisk the lemon zest, juice, eggs and sugar in a pan over low heat, stirring constantly, for 6–8 minutes until thick and just bubbling.
Off the heat whisk in the butter, strain into the tart case and chill 1 hour.
For the meringue, boil the 150 g sugar and water to 118°C while whisking the whites to soft peaks, then pour the syrup in slowly while whisking and continue until cool and glossy.
Pipe or swirl the meringue over the lemon cream.
Colour with a blowtorch or under a hot grill for 1–2 minutes until golden; chill until serving.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 1 blind-baked 24 cm sweet pastry case (pâte sucrée), cooled
steps: Heat the milk with vanilla; whisk the yolks, sugar and cornflour, pour on the hot milk and return to the pan.
Whisk over medium heat until it boils and thickens, then cook 1 minute more to make crème pâtissière; cover with film and chill.
Beat the cold crème pâtissière smooth and spread in the pastry case.
Arrange the strawberries closely on top and brush with the warm jelly; chill and serve the same day.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 4 eggs and 120 g caster sugar, 120 g plain flour (génoise)
500 ml whole milk, 5 egg yolks, 100 g sugar, 40 g cornflour and 1 vanilla pod (crème pâtissière)
200 g soft unsalted butter (for crème mousseline)
80 g sugar and 80 ml water, plus 2 tbsp kirsch (optional), for syrup
150 g pink or white marzipan, rolled thin
steps: Whisk the eggs and sugar over warm water to the ribbon stage, fold in the flour and bake in a 22 cm tin at 180°C for 20–25 minutes; cool and slice into two discs.
Make crème pâtissière with the milk, yolks, sugar, cornflour and vanilla, cooking until thick; cool to room temperature, then beat in the soft butter to make crème mousseline.
Set one sponge disc in a 22 cm ring lined with acetate, brush with syrup, and stand halved strawberries cut-side out around the edge.
Fill with mousseline and whole strawberries, top with the second disc brushed with syrup and a thin layer of cream.
Chill at least 4 hours, cover with the marzipan disc and unmould; decorate with strawberries.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 150 ml sugar syrup (75 g sugar and 75 ml water, boiled and cooled)
250 g fromage blanc or Greek yoghurt
steps: Blend 250 g strawberries with the icing sugar to a coulis; warm a quarter of it, dissolve the soaked, squeezed gelatine in it, then mix back into the rest.
Whip the cream to soft peaks and fold it with the fromage blanc into the strawberry mixture once it is cool and starting to thicken.
Dip the sponge fingers briefly in the syrup and line the base and sides of a charlotte mould or 18 cm springform tin, rounded sides out.
Pour in half the mousse, add a layer of chopped strawberries, then the rest of the mousse and a final layer of soaked fingers.
Chill at least 6 hours, unmould and decorate with the remaining strawberries.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 125 g butter, plus extra for the moulds
1 tbsp cocoa powder, for the moulds
steps: Butter 4 ramekins and dust with cocoa; heat the oven to 200°C.
Melt the chocolate and butter together over gentle heat and cool slightly.
Whisk the eggs and sugar until pale, stir in the chocolate, then fold in the flour.
Fill the moulds three-quarters full and bake 10–12 minutes until the tops are set but the centres still wobble.
Rest 1 minute, turn out and serve warm with crème anglaise or vanilla ice cream.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 60 g caster sugar, plus extra for the ramekins
steps: Brush 4 ramekins with butter using upward strokes and coat with sugar; heat the oven to 200°C with a tray inside.
Bring the milk to the boil, whisk in the cornflour slaked with a little water and cook 1 minute until thick, then stir in the chocolate until melted and beat in the yolks.
Whisk the whites to soft peaks, add the sugar and whisk to firm, shiny peaks; fold into the chocolate base in three stages.
Fill the ramekins to the rim, level the tops and run a thumb round the edge.
Bake on the hot tray for 10–12 minutes until well risen; dust with icing sugar and serve immediately.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 1 pot plain yoghurt (125 g), the pot used as the measure
11 g baking powder (1 sachet levure chimique)
zest of 1 lemon or 1 tsp vanilla extract
steps: Heat the oven to 180°C and butter a 22 cm round tin.
Empty the yoghurt into a bowl, then use the pot to measure in the sugar and whisk with the eggs.
Add the flour and baking powder, then the oil and zest, mixing until smooth.
Pour into the tin and bake 30–35 minutes until golden and a skewer comes out clean; cool on a rack.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 150 g short-grain or round pudding rice
steps: Blanch the rice in boiling water for 2 minutes and drain.
Bring the milk to the boil with the vanilla pod and seeds and the salt, add the rice and lower to a gentle simmer.
Cook uncovered for 40–45 minutes, stirring often, until the rice is very soft and creamy.
Stir in the sugar and butter off the heat, remove the pod and serve warm or chilled, with salted caramel if liked.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 4 firm pears (Williams or Conference), peeled, stalks left on
1 litre water and 200 g caster sugar
1 vanilla pod, split, and juice of 1/2 lemon
steps: Bring the water, sugar, vanilla and lemon juice to a simmer, add the pears and poach gently 20–25 minutes until a knife slides in easily; cool in the syrup.
Heat the cream until steaming, pour over the chocolate and stir until smooth and glossy.
Drain the pears and stand each in a coupe with a scoop of ice cream.
Pour the warm chocolate sauce over at the table and scatter with almonds.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 2 sheets all-butter puff pastry, about 230 g each, rolled into 26 cm discs
1 fève (a small ceramic charm) or a whole dried bean
steps: Beat the butter and sugar until creamy, then add the ground almonds, eggs and rum to make frangipane.
Lay one pastry disc on a lined tray, spread the frangipane over it leaving a 2 cm border, and press in the fève near the edge.
Brush the border with water, cover with the second disc and seal firmly; chill 30 minutes.
Brush with yolk, score a sunburst or leaf pattern with a knife tip and poke a small hole in the centre.
Bake at 190°C for 35–40 minutes until puffed and deep golden; serve warm on Epiphany, with the youngest person deciding who gets each slice — the finder of the fève is king.

ingredients: 80 g plain flour and 20 g cocoa powder
250 ml double cream and 150 g dark chocolate (ganache)
200 g chestnut cream (crème de marrons) or 200 ml whipped cream
steps: Whisk the yolks with 60 g sugar until pale; whisk the whites to soft peaks with the remaining sugar and fold into the yolks with the sifted flour and cocoa.
Spread on a lined 30 x 40 cm tray and bake at 200°C for 8–10 minutes until springy.
Turn out onto a damp tea towel, roll up from the long side while warm and leave to cool.
Heat the cream, pour over the chocolate and stir; chill 30 minutes until spreadable.
Unroll the sponge, spread with the chestnut cream, roll up again and cover with ganache, marking bark lines with a fork; trim an end to make a branch, chill 2 hours and dust with icing sugar as snow.

ingredients: 300 ml strong brewed coffee (French press or filter)
steps: Brew the coffee strong, using about 30 g ground coffee for 300 ml water.
Heat the milk until steaming and lightly frothy, without boiling.
Pour equal amounts of coffee and hot milk together into large bowls (bols) and serve at breakfast with tartines or croissants for dipping.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 100 ml double cream (optional, for a richer chocolat à l'ancienne)
steps: Heat the milk and cream until just simmering.
Whisk in the cocoa, sugar and salt, then the chopped chocolate until fully melted.
Simmer gently, whisking, for 3–4 minutes until slightly thickened and frothy.
Serve hot in cups, with whipped cream (chantilly) if liked.

ingredients: 8 slices pain de mie (soft sandwich bread)
4 slices jambon de Paris (cooked ham), about 200 g
30 g butter, plus extra for spreading
1/2 tsp salt and a pinch of white pepper
steps: Melt the butter in a small pan over medium heat, stir in the flour for 1 minute, then whisk in the milk and simmer 4–5 minutes until a thick béchamel; season with salt, pepper and nutmeg.
Heat the oven grill to high and butter one side of each bread slice.
Lay 4 slices buttered-side down on a tray, spread with a little béchamel, add a slice of ham and a handful of cheese, then close with the remaining bread, buttered side up.
Spread the remaining béchamel over the tops and cover with the rest of the cheese.
Bake at 200°C for 8 minutes, then grill 2–3 minutes until bubbling and golden; serve hot with a green salad.

ingredients: 8 slices pain de mie (soft sandwich bread)
4 slices jambon de Paris (cooked ham), about 200 g
30 g butter, plus extra for spreading and frying
1 pinch nutmeg, salt and white pepper
steps: Make a béchamel: melt the butter over medium heat, cook the flour 1 minute, whisk in the milk and simmer 4–5 minutes until thick; season with nutmeg, salt and pepper.
Assemble 4 sandwiches with buttered bread outside, a little béchamel, ham and cheese inside, then top each with béchamel and the remaining cheese.
Bake at 200°C for 8 minutes, then grill 2–3 minutes until golden and bubbling.
Meanwhile fry the eggs in a little butter over medium-low heat for 3–4 minutes until the whites are set and the yolks still runny.
Slide one egg onto each croque (the egg is the "hat" that makes it a Madame) and serve at once.

ingredients: 60 g good unsalted or demi-sel butter, softened
4 slices jambon de Paris (cooked ham), about 160 g
steps: Cut the baguette in half crosswise, then split each half lengthways without cutting all the way through.
Spread butter generously on both cut faces, right to the edges.
Fold the ham slices to fit and lay them inside, adding sliced cornichons if you like.
Press closed and eat the same hour, ideally with the bread baked that morning.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 1 tsp salt and black pepper to taste
steps: Melt the butter in a heavy pot over medium-low heat, add the onions and a pinch of salt and cook, stirring often, for 40–45 minutes until deep golden brown and jammy.
Sprinkle in the flour and stir 2 minutes, then pour in the wine and scrape up the browned bits.
Add the stock, thyme and bay leaf and simmer gently 20 minutes; season with salt and pepper and discard the herbs.
Ladle into ovenproof bowls, float two toasted baguette slices on each and cover thickly with cheese.
Grill under high heat for 4–5 minutes until the cheese is melted, bubbling and browned at the edges; serve very hot.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 500 g fresh or frozen green peas
1 tsp salt and white pepper to taste
small croutons fried in butter, to serve
steps: Brown the lardons in a pot over medium heat for 5 minutes, then remove half for garnish.
Add the butter and onion and soften 5 minutes without colouring, then add the lettuce and peas and stir 2 minutes.
Pour in the stock, bring to a boil and simmer 12–15 minutes until the peas are very tender.
Blend until smooth, pass through a sieve for a silky finish, then stir in the crème fraîche and season.
Reheat gently and serve topped with the reserved lardons and croutons.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 750 g carrots, sliced (Crécy is famous for its carrots)
1 tsp salt and white pepper to taste
steps: Melt the butter in a pot over medium-low heat and sweat the onion and carrots with the sugar and a pinch of salt for 10 minutes without browning.
Add the potato and stock, bring to a boil and simmer 20 minutes until the carrots crush easily.
Blend until completely smooth, then stir in the cream and adjust the seasoning.
Reheat without boiling and serve sprinkled with chervil and buttered croutons.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 1.2 kg lamb shoulder and neck, cut in 5 cm pieces
12 small new potatoes, 12 baby carrots, 12 baby turnips, 12 pearl onions
steps: Season the lamb and brown it in batches in the oil over high heat, sprinkling the last batch with the sugar to caramelise; return all the meat to the pot.
Stir in the flour and cook 2 minutes, then add tomato paste, garlic, stock and bouquet garni; bring to a simmer.
Cover and cook gently on low heat or at 160°C for 1 hour.
Add the potatoes, carrots, turnips and onions and cook 30 minutes more until the vegetables are tender and the lamb is soft.
Add the peas for the last 8 minutes, skim off the fat, check the seasoning and serve from the pot.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 300 g very fresh beef fillet or rump, from a trusted butcher, kept cold
2 very fresh egg yolks (pasteurised if available)
1 tsp Worcestershire sauce and a few drops of Tabasco
1 tbsp olive oil, salt and black pepper
steps: Use only very fresh, high-quality beef bought the same day for eating raw, and keep it in the fridge until the last moment; pregnant, elderly or immune-compromised people should avoid raw meat and egg.
Trim all sinew and chop the beef finely by hand with a sharp knife (not minced) on a cold board.
Mix the mustard, Worcestershire, Tabasco, oil, salt and pepper in a chilled bowl, then fold in the shallot, capers, cornichons, parsley and beef.
Shape into two rounds on cold plates, make a hollow in each and set a yolk in it.
Serve immediately with frites and a green salad.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 600 g leftover boiled beef (from pot-au-feu), thinly sliced
1 tbsp chopped parsley, salt and pepper
steps: Cook the onions in the butter over medium heat for 15 minutes until soft and golden.
Sprinkle in the flour, stir 1 minute, deglaze with the vinegar, then add the stock and tomato paste and simmer 10 minutes until slightly thickened; season.
Spread half the onion sauce in a gratin dish, arrange the beef slices overlapping on top and cover with the rest of the sauce.
Scatter with breadcrumbs and bake at 180°C for 20–25 minutes until bubbling and the beef is heated through.
Finish with parsley and serve with boiled or mashed potatoes.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 1.5 kg rolled veal head (tête de veau roulée), from a butcher, tied
2 carrots, 1 onion studded with 2 cloves, 1 leek
2 tbsp plain flour and 2 tbsp white wine vinegar (blanc de cuisson)
1 tbsp each capers, cornichons, parsley, chervil and tarragon, chopped
steps: Blanch the veal head and tongue in boiling water 10 minutes, drain and rinse.

Whisk the flour and vinegar with 3 l cold water in a large pot (this keeps the meat white), add the vegetables, bouquet garni, peppercorns and salt, then the meats; simmer gently 2.5–3 hours until very tender.
Peel the tongue while hot and slice it with the head meat into thick pieces; keep warm in some broth.
For the gribiche, mash the egg yolks with mustard, salt and pepper, whisk in the oil drop by drop to a mayonnaise, then add the chopped whites, capers, cornichons and herbs.
Serve the meat hot with boiled potatoes and carrots from the pot and the gribiche on the side.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 40 g Gruyère, grated, plus 1 tbsp Parmesan
1 tsp chopped tarragon, salt and cayenne pepper
steps: Chill the lobsters 30 minutes to sedate them, then plunge them head first into a large pot of boiling salted water and cook 8 minutes; cool in iced water.
Split each lobster lengthways, remove the meat from tails and claws and cut into chunks; clean the shells and keep them.
Soften the shallot in the butter, add the wine and reduce by half, add the fish stock and reduce again by half, then add the cream and simmer 5 minutes until coating a spoon.
Off the heat whisk in the mustard, egg yolk, tarragon, Gruyère, salt and cayenne, then fold in the lobster meat.
Pile the mixture back into the shells, sprinkle with Parmesan and grill 3–4 minutes until golden and bubbling; serve with rice or salad.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 6 eggs (4 to serve, 1 yolk for the mayonnaise)
steps: Lower 4 eggs into boiling water and cook 9 minutes, then cool in iced water and peel.
Whisk 1 raw yolk (use pasteurised if preferred) with the mustard and salt, then add the oil drop by drop, then in a thin stream, until thick and glossy; finish with vinegar and pepper.
Halve the boiled eggs and lay them cut side down on the lettuce.
Coat generously with mayonnaise and sprinkle with chives; serve chilled with bread.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 8 small leeks, trimmed and well washed
steps: Tie the leeks in a bundle and simmer in salted water 12–15 minutes until a knife slides in easily.
Drain well, pressing gently to remove water, and let cool to lukewarm.
Whisk the mustard, vinegar, salt and pepper, then whisk in the oil and add the shallot.
Arrange the leeks on a dish, spoon the vinaigrette over while still warm and finish with the herbs.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 8 fillets smoked herring marinated in oil (harengs fumés doux)
6 tbsp oil from the herring jar or sunflower oil
1 tbsp chopped parsley, salt and pepper
steps: If your herrings are not already marinated, cover them with sunflower oil, the carrot, onion, a bay leaf and peppercorns, and leave in the fridge 480 minutes or overnight.
Boil the potatoes in their skins in salted water 15–20 minutes until tender, then peel and slice while warm.
Whisk the mustard, vinegar, salt and pepper with the oil, then pour over the warm potatoes with the shallot so they absorb the dressing.
Serve the potatoes topped with the herring fillets, some of the marinated carrot and onion, and parsley.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 4 beef marrow bones, cut 6–8 cm long or split lengthways
1 tsp coarse sea salt (fleur de sel)
1 shallot, finely sliced, and 1 tsp lemon juice
steps: Soak the bones in cold salted water for 2 hours if you have time, then pat dry.
Stand them upright (or cut side up) on a tray and roast at 220°C for 15–20 minutes until the marrow is soft, wobbly and starting to separate from the bone.
Toss the parsley and shallot with lemon juice for a quick salad.
Serve hot with toast, fleur de sel and pepper, scooping the marrow onto the bread.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 1 kg floury potatoes (Bintje or Maris Piper)
2 l beef dripping or sunflower oil, for frying
steps: Peel the potatoes and cut into thick sticks about 1.5 cm square and 7 cm long; rinse well and dry thoroughly.
Fry in batches at 150°C for 7–8 minutes until tender but still pale; drain and let cool 10 minutes.
Fry again at 180°C for 3–4 minutes until deep golden and crisp.
Drain, salt immediately and serve stacked like logs, traditionally with grilled steak.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 2 l sunflower oil or beef dripping, split between two pans
steps: Square off the potatoes and cut lengthways into even slices exactly 3 mm thick; dry them well but do not rinse.
Heat one pan of oil to 150°C and the other to 190°C.
Fry the slices in a single layer in the cooler oil for 6–7 minutes, shaking the pan constantly, until they just start to blister.
Transfer them straight into the hot oil, where they puff up into little pillows in a few seconds; fry 1 minute more until golden and crisp.
Drain, salt and serve immediately; slices that don't puff are still delicious crisps.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 500 g French T65 flour (or strong bread flour)
steps: Mix the flour and 330 ml water until shaggy and rest 30 minutes, then add yeast, salt and the remaining water and knead 8–10 minutes until smooth and elastic.
Let rise 1 hour, folding the dough twice, then cover and refrigerate 12–16 hours for flavour.
Divide into 3, pre-shape into loose logs, rest 20 minutes, then roll into tight 35 cm baguettes and proof seam side up in a floured cloth for 45–60 minutes.
Heat the oven to 250°C with a tray below for steam; slash each loaf with 4–5 long diagonal cuts.
Bake 22–25 minutes, pouring a cup of hot water into the tray at the start, until deep golden and hollow-sounding; cool on a rack.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 500 g French T45 flour (or plain flour)
120 ml cold whole milk, plus 2 tbsp for brushing
280 g cold unsalted butter (beurre de tourage, 82% fat) for laminating
40 g soft butter for the dough
steps: Mix flour, sugar, salt, yeast, water, milk and soft butter into a smooth dough, flatten into a rectangle, wrap and chill overnight (about 12 hours).
Pound the cold butter into an 18 cm square; roll the dough into a 20 x 40 cm rectangle, enclose the butter and seal.
Roll to 20 x 60 cm and fold in three; chill 30 minutes, then repeat twice more for three turns.
Roll to 4 mm thick, cut into long triangles about 9 cm wide at the base, and roll up tightly from the base, curving the ends.
Proof at 25°C for 2 hours until wobbly and doubled, brush lightly with milk, and bake at 190°C for 16–20 minutes until deep golden and flaky.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 500 g French T45 flour (or plain flour)
270 ml cold water and milk, half and half, plus 2 tbsp milk for brushing
40 g soft butter for the dough
280 g cold unsalted butter for laminating
24 bâtons de chocolat (baking chocolate sticks) or 150 g dark chocolate cut in strips
steps: Make the dough with flour, sugar, salt, yeast, liquids and soft butter, flatten, wrap and chill overnight.
Laminate with the cold butter as for croissants, giving three single folds with 30 minutes chilling between each.
Roll to 4 mm and cut rectangles about 8 x 14 cm.
Place one chocolate stick at the short end, roll once, add a second stick and roll up, finishing seam side down.
Proof 2 hours at 25°C, brush with milk and bake at 190°C for 16–18 minutes until golden.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 100 ml water and 50 g sugar for syrup, plus 1 tbsp rum or orange-flower water
steps: Boil the water with 50 g sugar for 1 minute, cool and add the rum or orange-flower water.
Beat the butter and sugar until creamy, then beat in the egg and ground almonds to make frangipane.
Split the croissants horizontally, brush the insides with syrup and spread with half the frangipane; close them.
Spread the remaining frangipane on top, press on flaked almonds and bake at 180°C for 15–20 minutes until golden and the filling is set.
Cool slightly and dust with icing sugar.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 1 batch croissant dough (about 1.2 kg), laminated and chilled
150 g raisins, soaked in 2 tbsp rum or hot water for 30 minutes
steps: Make crème pâtissière: heat the milk, whisk the yolks with sugar and cornflour, pour on the hot milk, return to the pan and whisk over medium heat until thick and boiling for 1 minute; add vanilla and chill.
Roll the laminated dough to a 30 x 50 cm rectangle, 4 mm thick.
Spread with the cold crème pâtissière, leaving a 2 cm strip bare on one long edge, and scatter with the drained raisins.
Roll up tightly toward the bare edge, chill 20 minutes, then cut into 2.5 cm slices and lay flat on lined trays.
Proof 1.5–2 hours, brush the dough with beaten egg and bake at 185°C for 18–20 minutes until golden.

ingredients: 4 apples (Golden or Reinette), peeled and diced
2 tbsp milk and 1 tbsp sugar for glazing
steps: Cook the apples with sugar, butter, lemon and vanilla over medium heat for 15 minutes into a chunky compote; cool completely.
Roll the pastry 3 mm thick and cut six 14 cm ovals or rounds.
Spoon compote onto one half of each, wet the edges, fold over and press firmly to seal.
Brush with milk, score a leaf pattern with a knife tip without cutting through, and chill 15 minutes.
Bake at 200°C for 20–25 minutes until puffed and deep golden; brush with a little sugar syrup or sprinkle sugar while hot.

ingredients: 80 g sucre perlé (pearl sugar); substitute crushed sugar cubes
steps: Bring the water, milk, butter, sugar and salt to a boil, tip in the flour all at once and stir over the heat 1–2 minutes until the dough leaves the pan.
Off the heat beat in the eggs one by one until the choux paste is smooth and falls from the spoon in a V.
Pipe walnut-sized mounds on lined trays, brush with beaten egg and cover generously with pearl sugar.
Bake at 190°C for 20–25 minutes, without opening the oven for the first 15 minutes, until puffed, golden and dry.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 1 batch choux paste (125 ml water, 125 ml milk, 100 g butter, 150 g flour, 4 eggs)
steps: Pipe the choux paste into 12 cm fingers on lined trays and bake at 180°C for 30–35 minutes until golden and crisp; cool.
Make chocolate crème pâtissière: whisk yolks, sugar and cornflour, pour on the hot milk, cook while whisking until thick and boiling for 1 minute, then stir in the chocolate; chill.
Pierce three small holes in the base of each éclair and pipe in the cream until full.
Warm the fondant to 37°C with the cocoa and a little water until fluid, dip the tops of the éclairs and smooth with a finger; let set.

ingredients: 1 batch choux paste (125 ml water, 125 ml milk, 100 g butter, 150 g flour, 4 eggs)
4 egg yolks, 80 g sugar and 40 g cornflour
80 g dark chocolate or 2 tsp coffee extract for flavour
200 g fondant icing, coloured to match
80 g butter, softened, and 80 g icing sugar for the collar
steps: Pipe 8 large choux (5 cm) and 8 small ones (2.5 cm), bake at 180°C for 25–35 minutes until golden and dry; cool.
Make crème pâtissière with milk, yolks, sugar and cornflour, flavour with chocolate or coffee and chill.
Fill all the choux through a hole in the base.
Dip the tops in warmed fondant, then set each small choux on a large one like a head on a body.
Beat the butter and icing sugar (with a little flavouring) and pipe small rosettes around the "neck" to form the collar.

ingredients: 1 batch choux paste (125 ml water, 125 ml milk, 100 g butter, 150 g flour, 4 eggs)
250 ml whole milk, 3 egg yolks, 60 g sugar and 25 g cornflour
150 g praliné paste (hazelnut-almond); substitute smooth hazelnut butter plus 2 tbsp sugar
steps: Pipe the choux into a 22 cm ring (two rings side by side, a third on top), sprinkle with almonds and bake at 180°C for 35–40 minutes until deep golden; cool.
Make crème pâtissière with the milk, yolks, sugar and cornflour; cool to room temperature.
Beat the soft butter until fluffy, then beat in the praliné and the crème pâtissière to make crème mousseline.
Split the ring horizontally, pipe generous rosettes of cream over the base and replace the lid.
Chill 30 minutes and dust with icing sugar before serving.

ingredients: 250 ml whole milk, 3 egg yolks, 60 g sugar and 25 g cornflour
300 ml cold double cream and 30 g icing sugar
150 g sugar and 3 tbsp water for caramel
steps: Roll the puff pastry to a 22 cm disc, prick it, pipe a ring of choux around the edge and pipe 14 small choux separately; bake at 190°C for 25–30 minutes until golden.
Make vanilla crème pâtissière with milk, yolks, sugar and cornflour, and chill.
Fill the small choux with some crème pâtissière.
Cook the sugar and water to a light amber caramel; carefully dip the tops of the choux and stick them around the ring with more caramel.
Spread the remaining crème pâtissière in the centre and pipe the cream, whipped with icing sugar to firm peaks, on top with a Saint-Honoré nozzle; serve the same day.

ingredients: 120 g ground almonds and 120 g icing sugar
30 g plain flour and 20 g melted butter
150 ml strong espresso and 50 g sugar for syrup
150 g soft butter, 2 egg yolks, 80 g sugar and 2 tbsp coffee extract for coffee buttercream
150 g dark chocolate and 120 ml cream for ganache
100 g dark chocolate and 1 tbsp oil for glaze
steps: Beat the eggs with almonds and icing sugar 5 minutes, fold in flour, whipped egg whites and butter, spread on two lined trays and bake at 220°C for 6–7 minutes (joconde sponge); cool and cut into three equal rectangles.
Dissolve sugar in the espresso for the soaking syrup; make the buttercream by beating yolks with sugar cooked to a syrup, then beating in butter and coffee extract.
Heat the cream, pour over the chocolate and stir to a smooth ganache.
Layer: sponge soaked with syrup, buttercream, sponge, ganache, sponge, buttercream, smoothing each layer; chill 1 hour.
Pour over the melted chocolate and oil glaze, chill until set, trim the edges and write "Opéra" in chocolate if you like.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 200 g fondant icing or 150 g icing sugar mixed with a little water
steps: Roll the pastry into a thin 30 x 40 cm sheet, prick all over, place between two trays and bake at 190°C for 25–30 minutes until evenly golden and crisp; cool and cut into three equal strips.
Make crème pâtissière with the milk, vanilla, yolks, sugar and cornflour, whisk in the butter and chill until firm.
Pipe half the cream on the first strip, add the second, pipe the rest and top with the flattest strip, base side up.
Spread the fondant over the top, pipe thin lines of chocolate across and drag a knife through for the feathered pattern.
Chill 1 hour and cut with a serrated knife.

ingredients: 110 g egg whites (about 4), aged at room temperature, split in two
150 g caster sugar and 40 ml water
200 g dark chocolate and 200 ml double cream for ganache filling
steps: Sift the almonds and icing sugar, then mix in half the egg whites to a thick paste.
Boil the sugar and water to 118°C, meanwhile whip the other half of the whites to soft peaks, then pour in the syrup and whip to a glossy meringue (Italian method); add colour.
Fold the meringue into the almond paste until the batter flows like lava (macaronage), then pipe 3.5 cm rounds and leave 30 minutes until a skin forms.
Bake at 150°C for 12–14 minutes until the "feet" form and the tops don't wobble; cool before peeling off.
Make ganache by pouring hot cream over chocolate, cool until pipeable, sandwich the shells and mature them in the fridge 24 hours.

steps: Cook the butter over medium heat until it foams and smells nutty and the solids turn hazelnut brown (beurre noisette); strain and cool slightly.
Mix the icing sugar, almonds, flour and salt, then stir in the egg whites without whipping.
Stir in the warm brown butter and vanilla until smooth; rest 30 minutes if you can.
Fill buttered rectangular financier moulds three-quarters full and bake at 200°C for 12–15 minutes until golden at the edges and springy.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 500 ml water, 250 g sugar, 1 orange peel and 1 vanilla pod for syrup
steps: Mix flour, yeast, sugar, salt, eggs and milk and beat 10 minutes into a very elastic dough, then beat in the butter.
Pipe into buttered baba or savarin moulds half full and let rise 1 hour until the dough reaches the rims.
Bake at 180°C for 20–25 minutes until deep golden; unmould and let dry.
Boil the water, sugar, orange peel and vanilla, cool to warm, then soak the babas until heavy and saturated; drain.
Drizzle each with rum at the table and serve with Chantilly cream.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

steps: Line a 22 cm, 5 cm deep ring with the pastry and chill.
Bring the milk and vanilla to a boil, whisk the eggs, sugar, cornflour and salt, pour on the hot milk, return to the pan and whisk over medium heat until it thickens and boils for 1 minute.
Pour the hot custard into the pastry case and smooth the top.
Bake at 180°C for 50–60 minutes until the top is spotted dark brown and the custard barely wobbles.
Cool completely and chill at least 4 hours before slicing.

ingredients: 6 poached pear halves (or canned pears in syrup), drained
1 tbsp plain flour and 1 tbsp rum (optional)
2 tbsp apricot jam and 20 g flaked almonds
steps: Line a 24 cm tart tin with pastry, prick and chill 20 minutes.
Cream the butter and sugar, beat in the eggs, then the almonds, flour and rum to make frangipane.
Spread frangipane in the case, slice the pears thinly crosswise, fan them out and press them into the cream like spokes.
Scatter with flaked almonds and bake at 180°C for 40–45 minutes until the frangipane is puffed and golden.
Brush with warmed apricot jam while warm; serve at room temperature.

ingredients: 60 g caster sugar, plus 40 g for caramelising
steps: Roll the pastry 3 mm thick, cut six 9 cm discs and line small tartlet moulds, or make vol-au-vent cases with a raised rim; brush with egg.
Bake blind at 200°C for 15–20 minutes until puffed and golden; cool.
Make vanilla crème pâtissière with the milk, yolks, sugar and cornflour, and cool slightly.
Fill the cases with the cream, smooth, sprinkle with sugar and caramelise with a blowtorch or under a very hot grill for 1 minute.

ingredients: 400 g sweetened chestnut cream (crème de marrons)
300 ml double cream and 30 g icing sugar
steps: Whip the egg whites to stiff peaks, adding the sugar gradually, then pipe six 8 cm meringue discs and bake at 100°C for 90 minutes until dry; cool.
Beat the chestnut cream, chestnut purée, butter and rum until smooth and pipeable.
Whip the cream with icing sugar to firm peaks and pipe a dome on each meringue.
Pipe the chestnut mixture over the cream through a vermicelli nozzle, covering it in a tangle of strands like a snowy mountain, and dust with icing sugar.

steps: Pull a single espresso (about 30–40 ml) into a large cup.
Heat and froth the milk with a steam wand or whisk to about 65°C until silky with a little foam.
Pour the milk over the coffee to fill the cup and serve with sugar on the side, as in Paris cafés, often with a croissant.

ingredients: 2 kg mixed Mediterranean fish, cleaned and cut in pieces (rascasse/scorpion fish, gurnard, John Dory, monkfish, conger); substitute any firm white fish
500 g small rockfish or fish frames for the stock
2 onions, 1 leek and 1 fennel bulb, sliced
4 tomatoes, chopped, and 4 garlic cloves, crushed
1 pinch saffron threads and 1 strip dried orange peel
2 sprigs thyme, 1 bay leaf and 1 tbsp pastis (optional)
12 toasted baguette slices rubbed with garlic, and rouille to serve
steps: Heat the oil in a large pot, soften the onions, leek and fennel 8 minutes, then add the tomatoes, garlic, herbs, orange peel and the small rockfish and cook 5 minutes.
Cover with 2.5 l boiling water, boil hard 20 minutes so the oil emulsifies (the name means "boil, then lower"), then press everything through a sieve or food mill.
Return the broth to the pot with the saffron, pastis and potatoes and simmer 10 minutes.
Add the firm fish first, then the delicate fish 3–4 minutes later, and simmer gently 6–10 minutes until all the fish is opaque and flakes easily; season.
Serve in the traditional two courses: first the broth over garlic toasts spread with rouille, then the fish and potatoes on a platter.

ingredients: 1.5 kg small whole rockfish (poissons de roche), gutted and scaled; substitute fish heads and frames of white fish
3 tomatoes, chopped, and 1 tbsp tomato paste
1 large pinch saffron and 1 strip orange peel
croutons, grated Gruyère and rouille, to serve
steps: Heat the oil in a large pot and cook the onions, leek and fennel 10 minutes until soft.
Add the garlic, tomatoes, tomato paste and fish and stir over high heat 10 minutes until the fish falls apart.
Add 2.5 l water, thyme, bay, orange peel and saffron and simmer 30–40 minutes.
Pass everything through a food mill, pressing hard, then through a sieve; season with salt and cayenne and reheat.
Serve with croutons spread with rouille and grated cheese floating on top.

ingredients: 200 g fresh white beans (coco blancs) and 200 g fresh red-speckled beans (borlotti), or 1 can each, drained
200 g green beans, cut in short lengths
80 g small pasta (coquillettes) or broken spaghetti
1 batch pistou (basil, garlic, olive oil, grated Parmesan or aged Gruyère)
steps: Heat the oil in a large pot and soften the leek 5 minutes, then add the tomatoes and fresh beans and cover with 2.5 l water; simmer 30 minutes.
Add the carrots and potatoes and cook 10 minutes, then the green beans, courgettes and canned beans if using, and cook 10 minutes more.
Add the pasta and cook until tender, about 8–10 minutes; season.
Off the heat stir in most of the pistou and serve with the rest at the table; it is even better reheated the next day.

ingredients: 1.2 kg firm white fish (monkfish/baudroie, sea bass, John Dory), cut in thick pieces
1 strip orange peel, 1 bay leaf and 1 sprig thyme
steps: Simmer the onion, leek, fennel, orange peel, herbs, wine and stock 15 minutes.
Add the fish and poach gently 8–10 minutes until just opaque and flaking; lift it out and keep warm.
Whisk half the aïoli with the egg yolks in a bowl, then gradually whisk in 750 ml strained hot broth.
Return to a low heat and stir constantly until it thickens to a creamy custard that coats a spoon; do not let it boil.
Pour over the fish and toasts in deep plates and serve the remaining aïoli on the side.

ingredients: 2 red and 1 yellow peppers, cut in squares
1 bouquet of thyme, bay and basil (herbes de Provence)
steps: Fry each vegetable separately in olive oil over medium-high heat until lightly browned: aubergines 8 minutes, courgettes 6 minutes, peppers 8 minutes; season each and set aside.
Soften the onions in more oil 10 minutes, add the garlic and tomatoes and cook 10 minutes into a sauce.
Return all the vegetables to the pot with the herbs and simmer gently, covered, 30–40 minutes until soft but still holding their shape.
Remove the herbs, adjust seasoning and serve hot, warm or cold with crusty bread or rice.

ingredients: 1.5 kg beef chuck or cheek, cut in 6 cm pieces
750 ml robust red wine (Côtes de Provence or Côtes du Rhône)
2 tbsp olive oil and 2 tbsp plain flour
steps: Marinate the beef with the wine, onions, carrots, garlic, orange peel and herbs overnight (8 hours) in the fridge.
Drain the meat, keeping the marinade, pat dry, and brown it with the pork in the oil in a heavy pot (daubière) over high heat; sprinkle with flour and stir 2 minutes.
Bring the marinade to a boil, pour it over the meat with the vegetables and herbs, season and cover tightly.
Cook at 150°C or on the lowest heat for 3–3.5 hours until the beef is spoon-tender, adding the olives for the last 30 minutes.
Skim the fat and serve with macaroni tossed in the sauce, polenta or potatoes.

ingredients: 800 g small potatoes in their skins
500 g carrots, 300 g green beans and 3 small courgettes
steps: Soak the salt cod in cold water in the fridge for 1–2 days, changing the water 3–4 times a day, until pleasantly salted.
Boil each vegetable separately in salted water until just tender: potatoes 20 minutes, carrots 15, artichokes 20, green beans and courgettes 6–8; hard-boil the eggs 9 minutes.
Put the cod in cold water with the bay and thyme, bring just to a simmer and poach 8–10 minutes until it flakes; drain.
Arrange the fish, eggs and vegetables on a large platter, warm or at room temperature.
Serve with a big bowl of aïoli in the centre; traditionally eaten on Fridays and Ash Wednesday.

ingredients: 6 small round courgettes or 3 long ones
3 small red onions and 3 small aubergines or peppers
400 g minced veal or pork, or leftover daube
100 g stale bread soaked in milk and squeezed
2 garlic cloves and 2 tbsp parsley, chopped
4 tbsp olive oil and 2 tbsp breadcrumbs
steps: Halve or cap the vegetables and scoop out the flesh; blanch the courgettes, onions and aubergines 5 minutes, and salt and drain the tomatoes upside down.
Chop the scooped flesh and cook it in 2 tbsp olive oil with the garlic for 10 minutes.
Mix the meat with the cooked flesh, bread, eggs, Parmesan, parsley, salt and pepper and fill the vegetables generously.
Arrange in an oiled dish, sprinkle with breadcrumbs, drizzle with the rest of the oil and bake at 180°C for 45–50 minutes until golden and the filling reaches 72°C.
Serve warm or at room temperature, as they are eaten in Nice.

ingredients: 1 kg cleaned lamb tripe (panse), from a butcher
150 g salt pork or pancetta, finely chopped
6 garlic cloves and 1 bunch parsley, chopped
4 tomatoes, chopped, and 2 tbsp tomato paste
3 tbsp olive oil, 1 bouquet garni, salt and pepper
steps: Cut the tripe into 10 cm squares, make a slit in one corner of each, place a spoonful of mixed pork, garlic and parsley in the centre, fold into a parcel (paquet) and thread the corner through the slit to close.
Brown the onions and carrots in the oil in a heavy casserole, add the tomatoes and tomato paste and cook 5 minutes.
Add the parcels and trotters, the wine, bouquet garni and water to cover, season and bring to a simmer.
Cover tightly and cook in the oven at 140°C for 6–7 hours until the tripe is meltingly tender and the sauce is thick and sticky.
Serve hot with steamed potatoes; this Marseille dish improves when reheated the next day.

ingredients: 1.5 kg Camargue bull meat (taureau AOP) shoulder or cheek; substitute beef chuck
750 ml Costières de Nîmes or other full red wine
1 strip orange peel and 1 bouquet garni
3 tbsp olive oil and 2 tbsp flour
300 g Camargue red or white rice, to serve
steps: Marinate the meat in the wine with onions, garlic, carrots, orange peel and herbs for 8–24 hours in the fridge.
Drain and dry the meat, brown it with the lardons in hot oil, sprinkle with flour and stir 2 minutes.
Add the marinade and vegetables, bring to a boil, cover and simmer on very low heat for 2.5–3 hours until very tender.
Add the olives for the last 30 minutes and season.
Serve with boiled Camargue rice to soak up the dark sauce.

ingredients: 1 tbsp herbes de Provence (thyme, rosemary, savory)
steps: Season the chicken and brown it in the oil over medium-high heat 10 minutes until golden on all sides.
Add the onion and garlic and cook 5 minutes, then pour in the wine and let it bubble 2 minutes.
Add the tomatoes and herbs, cover and simmer 25–30 minutes until the chicken juices run clear (74°C at the thickest point).
Add the olives, uncover and reduce the sauce 5 minutes; season, scatter with basil and serve with rice or crusty bread.

ingredients: 2 whole sea bass (loup de mer), about 700 g each, cleaned and scaled
1 bunch dried fennel stalks or fresh fennel fronds
1 tsp coarse salt and black pepper
steps: Slash the fish twice on each side, season inside and out and stuff the cavities with fennel fronds, lemon and garlic.
Brush with olive oil and lay in an oiled fish grill.
Grill over medium-hot embers or a hot grill 10–12 minutes per side until the flesh is opaque at the bone; toss fennel stalks on the coals for aromatic smoke.
If you like, warm the pastis, pour it over the fish and flame it carefully, then serve with olive oil and lemon.

ingredients: 1 kg dried stockfish (estocafic), sawn into pieces
1 kg ripe tomatoes, peeled and chopped
200 ml dry white wine and 2 tbsp marc or brandy
1 bouquet garni, salt, pepper and a pinch of chilli
steps: Soak the stockfish in cold water for 4–6 days, changing the water every day, until supple; skin and bone it, then cut in pieces.
Soften the onions, leek, garlic and peppers in the oil 10 minutes, add the fish and stir 5 minutes, then flame with the marc.
Add the tomatoes, wine, bouquet garni, chilli and water barely to cover and simmer gently, covered, for 1.5–2 hours until the fish is very soft.
Add the potatoes and cook 25 minutes, then the olives for the last 10 minutes; season and serve hot.

ingredients: 1 small cucumber, sliced, and 1 green pepper, sliced
6 small purple artichokes or 100 g young broad beans (fèves), raw
200 g good tuna in olive oil, drained, or 8 anchovy fillets
6 tbsp olive oil, 1 garlic clove, basil leaves, salt and pepper
steps: Hard-boil the eggs 9 minutes, cool and quarter them.
Rub a large bowl with the garlic and arrange the tomatoes, cucumber, pepper, thinly sliced artichokes or beans and spring onions.
Add the tuna or anchovies, eggs and olives on top.
Dress only with olive oil, salt, pepper and torn basil (no boiled potatoes or green beans in the Niçois tradition) and serve at once.
