ingredients: 200 g mixed young leaves: rocket, dandelion, chervil, lamb's lettuce, purslane, oak-leaf lettuce
steps: Wash the leaves gently and spin completely dry.
Rub a salad bowl with the cut garlic, then whisk in the vinegar, salt, pepper, mustard and olive oil.
Add the leaves and toss just before serving so they stay crisp.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 6 tbsp olive oil and 1 tbsp red wine vinegar
1 green pepper and 1 small red onion, thinly sliced
150 g tuna in olive oil or 8 anchovy fillets
50 g black Nice olives, pitted, and basil leaves
steps: Split the rolls, rub the insides with garlic and soak both halves well with olive oil and vinegar ("bagnat" means bathed).
Layer the tomatoes, pepper, onion, egg, tuna or anchovies, olives and basil, and season.
Close the rolls, wrap tightly and press under a weight for at least 1 hour so the juices soak in.
Eat at room temperature, the classic beach lunch in Nice.

ingredients: 250 g chickpea flour (farine de pois chiches)
steps: Whisk the flour, water, 3 tbsp oil and salt into a smooth thin batter and rest at least 2 hours.
Heat the oven to its maximum (250–280°C) with a large round copper or cast-iron pan inside for 10 minutes.
Oil the hot pan with the remaining oil, pour in the batter 3 mm deep and bake 8–10 minutes on the top shelf, finishing under the grill until blistered and charred in spots.
Cut into rough pieces with a spatula, grind lots of black pepper over and eat hot with your fingers.

ingredients: 300 g bread dough (250 g flour, 150 ml water, 3 g yeast, 1 tbsp olive oil, 5 g salt)
2 tbsp pissalat (anchovy purée) or 4 mashed anchovies
steps: Make the dough, knead 8 minutes and let rise 1 hour.
Cook the onions in the olive oil with garlic, thyme and a pinch of salt over low heat, covered, for 45–60 minutes until meltingly soft and pale golden, not browned.
Stretch the dough into an oiled 30 x 40 cm tray, spread with pissalat and cover thickly with the onions.
Arrange the anchovies in a lattice and dot each diamond with an olive.
Bake at 220°C for 20–25 minutes until the crust is golden underneath; serve warm or at room temperature in squares.

ingredients: 5 tbsp olive oil, plus extra for brushing
1 tbsp herbes de Provence and coarse salt
steps: Mix the flour, water, yeast, salt and 3 tbsp oil and knead 10 minutes until smooth; knead in the olives if using.
Let rise, covered, 1–1.5 hours until doubled.
Divide in two, flatten each into a 1.5 cm thick leaf shape on oiled paper, then cut a central slash and several diagonal side slashes and pull them wide open like a leaf's veins.
Proof 20 minutes, brush with oil and sprinkle with herbs and coarse salt.
Bake at 230°C for 15–20 minutes until golden and crisp at the edges.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 2 tbsp olive oil, plus oil for frying
steps: Bring the water, oil and salt to a boil, then whisk in the chickpea flour in a stream.
Stir constantly with a wooden spoon over medium heat 10–12 minutes until very thick and pulling from the pan.
Pour into oiled saucers or a tray 1.5 cm deep and leave to set at least 2 hours.
Cut into thick fingers and fry in 1 cm olive oil at 180°C for 3–4 minutes per side until golden and crisp; season and serve hot, as in L'Estaque near Marseille.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 1 l sunflower or olive oil for frying
steps: Whisk the flour, egg yolk, olive oil, salt and sparkling water into a smooth batter and rest 15 minutes.
Whip the egg white to soft peaks and fold it in just before frying.
Heat the oil to 180°C, dip each flower in the batter, letting the excess drip off, and fry a few at a time 2 minutes until puffed and pale golden.
Drain on paper, sprinkle with salt and serve immediately.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 1 tbsp fresh thyme leaves and 1 sprig rosemary
steps: Soften the onions and garlic in 2 tbsp oil for 10 minutes and spread them in an earthenware dish (tian).
Arrange the courgette, aubergine and tomato slices on top in tight alternating rows standing on edge.
Season, scatter with thyme, tuck in the rosemary and drizzle with the remaining oil.
Bake at 180°C for 60 minutes, covering with foil for the first 30, until soft and caramelised on top; serve warm or at room temperature.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

steps: Salt the cut tomatoes and turn them upside down for 10 minutes to drain.
Mix the garlic, parsley, breadcrumbs and thyme with 2 tbsp oil (this is the persillade).
Sear the tomatoes cut side down in 2 tbsp oil over high heat for 3 minutes, then turn and arrange in a baking dish.
Pile the persillade on top, drizzle with the remaining oil and bake at 200°C for 20–25 minutes until soft and the crumbs are crisp.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 1 bouquet of thyme, bay and savory
steps: Snap off the tough outer leaves, trim the base and tips and halve the artichokes, scraping out any choke; drop them into lemon water.
Heat the oil in a wide pan and soften the onion, carrots and garlic 5 minutes.
Add the drained artichokes and stir 3 minutes, then pour in the wine and let it bubble 2 minutes.
Add the water, herbs, salt and pepper, cover and simmer 25–30 minutes until tender and the liquid is reduced to a light sauce; serve warm or cold.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 1/2 tsp thyme leaves and black pepper
steps: Put the olives, capers, anchovies, garlic, thyme and lemon juice in a mortar or food processor.
Pound or pulse to a coarse paste, then work in the olive oil gradually.
Season with pepper (it is already salty) and serve on toasted bread or with raw vegetables.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 100 g salted anchovies or anchovy fillets in oil
raw vegetables (celery, fennel, peppers, radish, artichokes) to serve
steps: If using salted anchovies, rinse and fillet them.
Warm the anchovies and garlic in 3 tbsp olive oil over very low heat 3–4 minutes until the anchovies melt.
Pound or blend to a paste, then whisk in the remaining oil and the vinegar to an emulsified sauce; season with pepper.
Serve warm with raw vegetables for dipping and grilled bread.

ingredients: 4 garlic cloves (Provence purple garlic if possible)
steps: Pound the garlic with the salt in a mortar to a smooth paste, removing any green germ.
Add the egg yolk and stir with the pestle in one direction.
Add the oil drop by drop, then in a thin stream, stirring constantly until the sauce is very thick and stands up.
Finish with lemon juice and keep refrigerated; use within a day as it contains raw egg.

ingredients: 1 pinch saffron threads soaked in 1 tbsp hot fish broth
1 small boiled potato (about 80 g), mashed, or 30 g bread soaked in broth
1/2 tsp cayenne pepper or piment d'Espelette
steps: Pound the garlic and salt in a mortar to a paste, then add the saffron with its liquid and the potato.
Work in the egg yolk and cayenne.
Add the oil gradually, stirring constantly, until thick and rust-coloured.
Serve with bouillabaisse or fish soup on garlic toasts.

ingredients: 60 g aged Gruyère, Mimolette or Parmesan, grated
steps: Pound the garlic and salt in a mortar to a paste.
Add the basil a handful at a time and pound to a bright green purée.
Work in the cheese, then the olive oil little by little (unlike Italian pesto there are no pine nuts).
Use the same day, stirred into soupe au pistou or pasta.

ingredients: 1 tsp thyme leaves or chopped basil
steps: Prick the aubergines, halve them and roast cut side down on an oiled tray at 200°C for 40–45 minutes until collapsed and very soft.
Scoop out the flesh, drain it in a sieve 10 minutes and chop it with a knife.
Mix with the garlic, olive oil, lemon, herbs, salt and pepper.
Chill 30 minutes and serve with toasted bread or raw vegetables.

ingredients: 800 g Swiss chard leaves (blettes), green parts only
80 g golden raisins soaked in 2 tbsp rum or warm water
steps: Wash and finely shred the chard, salt it, squeeze out all moisture with your hands and dry well.
Mix the chard with eggs, sugar, Parmesan, drained raisins and pine nuts.
Line a 26 cm tin with two-thirds of the pastry, fill with the chard mixture and cover with apple slices.
Cover with the remaining pastry, seal the edges, prick the top and bake at 180°C for 40–45 minutes until golden.
Cool and dust with icing sugar; this sweet chard tart is a Niçois classic served at room temperature.

ingredients: 250 g blanched almonds, ground very fine
200 g candied melon (melon confit); substitute candied orange or apricot
1 tbsp lemon juice and 1 tbsp water for the glaze
steps: Blend the candied melon and orange peel to a smooth paste, then work in the almonds and orange-flower water.
Warm the paste gently in a pan over low heat for 10–15 minutes, stirring, until it no longer sticks to your fingers.
Spread it 1 cm thick on wafer paper and let it dry overnight.
Mix the icing sugar with lemon juice and water to a thick white glaze (an egg-free version of the traditional royal icing) and spread thinly over the top.
Cut into small almond-shaped diamonds and dry 1 hour at 50°C or overnight at room temperature.

ingredients: 80 ml olive oil or 80 g soft butter
steps: Mix the flour, sugar and salt, then add the oil or butter, orange-flower water, zest and enough water to make a firm, smooth dough.
Rest the dough 1 hour, wrapped.
Roll into 10 cm logs as thick as a finger, taper the ends and cut a deep slit along the top so they look like little boats.
Brush with milk and bake at 180°C for 18–20 minutes until pale golden; they keep for weeks in a tin and are eaten at Candlemas.

ingredients: 300 ml whole milk, 3 egg yolks, 70 g sugar, 25 g cornflour and 1 tbsp orange-flower water
steps: Knead the flour, yeast, sugar, salt, eggs and warm milk 8 minutes, then knead in the butter until a smooth brioche dough; let rise 1.5 hours.
Shape into a 24 cm disc in a ring, proof 45 minutes, brush with egg and sprinkle with pearl sugar; bake at 180°C for 20–25 minutes and cool.
Make crème pâtissière with the milk, yolks, sugar and cornflour, flavour with orange-flower water and chill.
Whip the cream to soft peaks and fold into the cold crème pâtissière (crème diplomate).
Split the brioche horizontally, pipe a thick layer of cream on the base, replace the top and chill 1 hour before serving.

ingredients: 1 tsp grated orange zest and 1 pinch salt
steps: Mix the flour, yeast, sugar, salt and zest, then add the oil, orange-flower water and water and knead 10 minutes into a soft, supple dough.
Let rise, covered, 2 hours until doubled.
Roll into a flat 1 cm oval, place on a lined tray and cut several slits through it, opening them out like a fougasse.
Proof 30 minutes, brush with olive oil and bake at 180°C for 20–25 minutes until golden.
Tear it by hand rather than cutting (tradition says cutting brings bad luck) as part of the Christmas thirteen desserts.

ingredients: 1 tsp grated lemon zest and 1 pinch salt
steps: Mix the flour, sugar, salt and zest, add the eggs, butter and orange-flower water and knead into a smooth dough; rest 1 hour.
Roll out as thinly as possible, almost transparent, and cut into rectangles about 8 x 12 cm with a fluted wheel, making a slit in the centre of each.
Fry a few at a time in oil at 175°C for 30–60 seconds per side until they puff and turn pale gold.
Drain on paper and dust generously with icing sugar.

ingredients: 150 g black nougat (made with honey and almonds only)
150 g each dried figs, raisins, almonds and walnuts (the "four beggars")
4 oranges or mandarins and 4 winter pears or apples
1 small winter melon or a bunch of grapes
steps: Lay a table with three white tablecloths, as is the Provençal Christmas custom.

Arrange thirteen sweets, representing Christ and the twelve apostles, on small plates: the pompe, nougat, the four beggars, dates, fresh fruit, candied fruit, quince paste, calissons, navettes and melon or grapes; vary by family tradition to reach thirteen.
Serve after midnight mass at the end of the Gros Souper on Christmas Eve and leave them out for three days, letting everyone taste each one.

steps: Line a 20 cm square tin with wafer paper and keep the nuts warm in a low oven.
Heat the honey to 120°C; separately boil the sugar and water to 145°C.
Whip the egg whites to stiff peaks, pour in the hot honey in a stream while whisking, then the sugar syrup, and keep whisking 5–8 minutes until thick and glossy; add vanilla.
Quickly fold in the warm almonds and pistachios (Montélimar nougat must contain at least 28% almonds), press into the tin and cover with the second sheet of wafer paper.
Weight it and leave to set overnight, then cut into bars with a large oiled knife.

ingredients: 1 kg firm fruit: apricots, clementines, cherries, pears or melon pieces
steps: Prick or halve the fruit, blanch it 2–5 minutes in boiling water until just tender, then drain.
Boil the sugar, water, glucose and lemon to a syrup, pour it over the fruit and leave 24 hours.
Each day for 5–7 days, drain the syrup, bring it back to a boil to concentrate it, and pour it back over the fruit, until the fruit is translucent and fully saturated.
Drain the fruit on a rack and dry at 50°C for 2 hours, or in the air for 2 days, until no longer sticky.
Store in a tin; Apt in the Luberon is the capital of candied fruit, eaten at Christmas and in calissons and cakes.

ingredients: 20 ml pastis (anise and liquorice spirit, bought from licensed producers)
steps: Pastis is a Marseille aniseed spirit flavoured with star anise and liquorice, about 45% alcohol, drunk as an apéritif; buy it from licensed producers.
Pour the pastis into a tall glass, then add cold water (about 1 part pastis to 5 parts water) and watch it turn cloudy yellow.
Add ice last, if using, and serve with olives and tapenade; drink responsibly and only if of legal age.

ingredients: 300 g pike (brochet) fillet, skinless and boneless, chilled (substitute: hake or whiting)
125 g butter, plus 30 g for the sauce
1/4 tsp grated nutmeg, plus salt and white pepper
12 cooked crayfish tails with shells (écrevisses), or cooked prawns
steps: Bring the milk and 125 g butter to a boil, tip in the flour all at once and stir over medium heat for 2–3 minutes until the panade comes away from the pan; cool, then beat in the eggs one at a time.
Blitz the pike in a food processor until very smooth, add the panade, nutmeg, 1 tsp salt and pepper, and process to a glossy paste; chill for at least 1 hour.
For the Nantua sauce, sauté the crayfish shells in 30 g butter for 5 minutes, flame with Cognac, add tomato purée and cream, simmer 15 minutes, strain and stir in the peeled tails.
Shape the quenelle mix into large ovals with two wet spoons and poach in barely simmering salted water for 10–12 minutes until they float and feel firm.
Drain the quenelles into a buttered gratin dish, cover with the sauce and bake at 200°C for 15–20 minutes until they puff up and the sauce bubbles; serve with rice.

ingredients: 1 saucisson à cuire (Lyon cooking sausage, about 500 g), pistachio or truffled if available (substitute: cotechino)
steps: Mix flour, yeast, sugar, salt, milk and 3 eggs and knead 10 minutes until elastic, then work in the butter in pieces until the dough is smooth and shiny; let rise covered for 1 hour, then chill 1 hour.
Prick the sausage and poach it in water kept just below a simmer for 40 minutes; cool slightly, peel off the skin and pat dry.
Roll the dough into a rectangle, dust the sausage lightly with flour, place it on the dough and wrap it, sealing the seam.
Set it seam-down in a buttered loaf tin, prove for 45 minutes until risen, then brush with the beaten yolk.
Bake at 190°C for 30–35 minutes until deep golden; rest 10 minutes, slice thickly and serve warm with a green salad.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 1 saucisson à cuire (Lyon cooking sausage, about 500 g) (substitute: cotechino or a large smoked pork sausage)
steps: Prick the sausage, put it in cold water with the bay leaf and bring to just below a simmer; poach for 40 minutes without boiling so it does not split.
Meanwhile boil the potatoes in their skins in salted water for 20–25 minutes until a knife slides in easily.
Whisk mustard, vinegar, salt and pepper, then whisk in the oil and add the shallot.
Peel the potatoes while hot, slice them thickly and toss with the dressing and parsley so they soak it up warm.
Slice the hot sausage into thick rounds and serve over the potatoes, bouchon style, with extra mustard.

ingredients: 1 kg honeycomb beef tripe (gras-double), cleaned and blanched
150 ml mayonnaise mixed with capers and gherkins (sauce gribiche or tartare), to serve
steps: Simmer the tripe with onion, carrot, bouquet garni and salted water for 3 hours until very tender; cool and cut into 10 cm squares.
Marinate the squares overnight in the wine, mustard and lemon juice in the fridge.
Drain and pat dry, dip each piece in beaten egg and press into the breadcrumbs on both sides.
Fry in clarified butter over medium heat for 4–5 minutes per side until crisp and golden and hot through.
Serve immediately with sauce gribiche or tartare and steamed potatoes.

ingredients: 4 andouillettes (pork chitterling sausages, AAAAA label if possible)
steps: Score the andouillettes lightly in a few places so they don't burst.
Fry them in oil and 1 tbsp butter over medium heat for 15–20 minutes, turning, until browned all over and piping hot in the middle (75°C).
Remove and keep warm; add remaining butter and onions to the pan and cook 10 minutes until soft and golden.
Deglaze with the wine and vinegar, scrape up the sediment, stir in 1 tbsp mustard and reduce for 2 minutes.
Spoon the onions over the sausages, scatter parsley and serve with the remaining mustard, gratin dauphinois or fries.

ingredients: 1 onion and 1 carrot, for the poaching liquid
steps: Simmer the tripe with the whole onion, carrot, bouquet garni and salted water for 3 hours until tender; drain and cut into thin strips 1 cm wide.
Cook the sliced onions in half the butter over medium-low heat for 15 minutes until soft and golden.
In another large pan heat the oil and remaining butter until foaming and fry the tripe strips over high heat for 8–10 minutes until crisp at the edges.
Add the onions, season well and toss together for 2 minutes.
Deglaze with the vinegar, let it sizzle off for 30 seconds, scatter with parsley and serve at once with boiled potatoes.

ingredients: 4 slices calf's liver, 1.5 cm thick (about 600 g)
steps: Cook the onions in 30 g butter over medium-low heat for 15–20 minutes, stirring, until soft and caramel coloured; season and set aside.
Season the liver and dust lightly with flour, shaking off the excess.
Heat the oil and remaining butter until foaming and sear the liver over medium-high heat for 2–3 minutes per side until browned outside and just pink inside.
Move the liver to warm plates, return the onions to the pan, deglaze with the vinegar and bubble for 30 seconds.
Spoon the onions over the liver, sprinkle with parsley and serve with mashed potatoes.

steps: Season the chicken and brown it skin-side down in the butter and oil over medium-high heat for 10 minutes, turning until golden all over.
Add shallots and garlic and cook 2 minutes, then pour in the vinegar and let it bubble hard for 3 minutes to soften its sharpness.
Add the wine and tomato purée, cover and simmer gently for 25–30 minutes until the juices run clear at the thigh (75°C).
Lift out the chicken, reduce the sauce by half, then whisk in the crème fraîche and simmer 2 minutes until glossy.
Return the chicken to coat it, sprinkle with parsley and serve with rice or fresh pasta.

dishes.name: Poulet de Bresse à la Crème

ingredients: 1 Bresse chicken or free-range chicken (about 1.8 kg), cut into 8 pieces
200 ml dry white wine (Mâcon or Savoie)
steps: Season the chicken and colour it gently in the butter over medium heat for 8 minutes without browning too much (the dish should stay pale).
Add onions and mushrooms and sweat 5 minutes, then pour in the wine and simmer to reduce by half.
Stir in 300 ml of the crème fraîche, cover and simmer gently for 35–40 minutes until the chicken is cooked through (juices clear, 75°C).
Remove the chicken, whisk the remaining cream with the yolk and stir into the sauce off the heat, then warm gently without boiling until it coats a spoon; add lemon juice.
Pour the sauce over the chicken and serve with pilaf rice.

ingredients: 1 Bresse poularde or large free-range chicken (about 2 kg)
1 cleaned pig's bladder (vessie), soaked in vinegared water (substitute: a large oven-safe cooking bag)
1 black truffle, sliced (or 2 tbsp truffle paste)
steps: Slip the truffle slices under the breast and thigh skin of the bird and season inside and out.
Place the bird inside the bladder with the Madeira, Cognac and a little salt, squeeze out the air and tie the opening tightly with string.
Lower into barely simmering stock and poach very gently for 1 hour 45 minutes, ladling stock over the top, until the bird is cooked through (75°C at the thigh).
Bring it to the table in the inflated bladder, then cut it open and pour the juices into a pan; whisk in the crème fraîche and reduce for 3 minutes.
Carve the bird and serve with the sauce and poached leeks and carrots from the stock.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 400 ml tomato coulis or crayfish sauce, to serve
steps: Heat the oven to 160°C and butter 6 ramekins or one charlotte mould.
Blend the livers with garlic and parsley until smooth, then add eggs, flour, milk, nutmeg, 1 tsp salt and pepper and blend again; pass through a sieve.
Pour into the moulds and set them in a roasting tin filled with hot water halfway up.
Bake for 35–40 minutes (60 minutes for one large mould) until just set and a knife comes out clean; the centre must reach 72°C.
Rest 5 minutes, turn out onto plates and coat with warm tomato coulis or sauce Nantua.

ingredients: 1 kg cardoons (cardons), stalks only (substitute: celery hearts or salsify)
4 marrow bones, cut 5 cm long (about 150 g marrow)
steps: Strip the strings from the cardoon stalks, cut into 6 cm lengths and drop into water with lemon juice to stop browning.
Whisk the flour into 2 litres of salted water (a "blanc"), bring to a boil and simmer the cardoons for 45 minutes until tender; drain.
Soak the marrow bones in salted water for 15 minutes, push out the marrow, slice it into rounds and poach in simmering stock for 2 minutes.
Make a light sauce by melting the butter, stirring in a spoon of flour and whisking in the stock; simmer 5 minutes.
Toss the cardoons in a gratin dish with the sauce, top with marrow slices and cheese and bake at 200°C for 20 minutes until golden; serve with roast beef or alone.

steps: Boil the potatoes in their skins for 15 minutes until just tender, cool, peel and slice 5 mm thick.
Cook the onions in 20 g butter over medium-low heat for 15 minutes until golden and soft.
Fry the potato slices in the oil and remaining butter in a wide pan over medium-high heat for 15 minutes, turning occasionally, until crisp and brown.
Add the onions, season well and toss together for 3 minutes; add a dash of vinegar if you like.
Sprinkle with parsley and serve hot alongside roast meats or sausages.

ingredients: 1 head frisée (curly endive), pale inner leaves torn
3 tbsp red wine vinegar, plus 1 tbsp for poaching
steps: Rub a salad bowl with the garlic, whisk in mustard, 2 tbsp vinegar, salt and pepper, then the oil.
Fry the lardons in a dry pan over medium heat for 6–8 minutes until crisp; fry the bread cubes in the fat until golden, then deglaze the pan with the last tbsp vinegar.
Poach the eggs one at a time in simmering water with 1 tbsp vinegar for 3 minutes until the white is set and the yolk runny.
Toss the frisée with the dressing, the warm lardons, croutons and pan juices.
Top each plate with a poached egg and plenty of black pepper and serve immediately.

ingredients: 500 g fromage blanc (faisselle), well drained (substitute: strained quark or thick Greek yogurt)
3 tbsp chopped chives, parsley and chervil
steps: Beat the drained fromage blanc with a whisk until smooth, then whisk in the crème fraîche.
Stir in shallots, garlic, herbs, vinegar and oil and season generously with salt and pepper.
Chill for at least 1 hour so the flavours blend.
Serve cold as a dip with country bread and radishes, or alongside boiled potatoes, as in Lyon's bouchons.

ingredients: 1 kg pork belly fat with some meat and skin, cut into 2 cm cubes
1/2 tsp quatre-épices (or a pinch each of nutmeg, clove, ginger)
steps: Melt the lard in a heavy pot and add the pork cubes; cook over low heat for 2 hours, stirring occasionally, so the fat renders slowly.
Raise the heat to medium for the last 15–20 minutes and stir until the cubes turn golden brown and crisp.
Lift out with a slotted spoon, drain well on paper (keep the fat for cooking).
Toss while warm with salt, pepper and spices and leave to cool.
Serve at room temperature with apéritif drinks, bread and a glass of Beaujolais.

ingredients: 1 rosette de Lyon (cured dry pork sausage, about 400 g), bought from a charcutier
steps: Buy a ready-cured rosette from a charcutier; it is a large air-dried pork saucisson matured for several weeks, so it is not something to cure at home without proper facilities.
Peel off the casing and slice the rosette on the diagonal, very thinly, at room temperature.
Arrange on a board with cornichons, pickled onions, butter and sliced bread.
Serve as a starter or apéritif, Lyon bouchon style, with a jug of Beaujolais or Côtes du Rhône.

ingredients: 2 apples, thinly sliced (optional sweet version) or 60 g grated Comté (savoury)
steps: Whisk flour and salt with the eggs, then gradually whisk in the milk to a thick, smooth batter; rest 30 minutes.
Melt a quarter of the butter in a 24 cm frying pan over medium heat and pour in a quarter of the batter, a thicker pancake than a crêpe.
Scatter with apple slices or cheese and cook for 3–4 minutes until the base is golden and the top almost set.
Flip and cook 2–3 minutes more until golden on both sides; sprinkle with sugar if sweet.
Repeat with the remaining batter and serve hot, the hearty "hunger-killer" of Lyon and Savoie.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 200 g pralines roses (pink sugar-coated almonds from Lyon) (substitute: pink sugared almonds)
steps: Rub the butter into the flour and salt, add just enough cold water to bring the dough together, wrap and chill 30 minutes.
Roll out and line a 24 cm tart tin, prick, line with paper and beans and blind-bake at 180°C for 15 minutes; remove the beans.
Crush the pralines roses coarsely in a bag with a rolling pin, put them in a pan with the cream and simmer gently, stirring, for 10–15 minutes until thick and coating the spoon.
Pour the pink filling into the case and bake for 10 minutes until bubbling.
Cool completely for at least 2 hours until set, then slice and serve.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

steps: Mix flour, baking powder, sugar and salt, add eggs, butter, zest and orange-blossom water and knead to a smooth, soft dough; wrap and rest in the fridge for 2 hours.
Roll the dough very thinly (2 mm) and cut into rectangles of about 10 x 5 cm; make a slit in the centre and pull one end through to form a knot.
Heat the oil to 175°C and fry the bugnes a few at a time for 1 minute per side until puffed and golden.
Drain on paper and dust generously with icing sugar; eat warm, especially around Mardi Gras.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 1 tsp green food colouring (natural spirulina or matcha works)
steps: Make the ganache: heat the cream to a simmer, pour over the chopped chocolate, stir smooth with the curaçao and chill until firm, about 30 minutes.
Knead almonds, icing sugar and glucose into a pliable marzipan, tinting it a soft green with the colouring.
Roll the marzipan 4 mm thick and cut into 3 cm squares.
Pipe a small dot of ganache onto half the squares, top with the remaining squares and pinch the edges to seal into little cushions.
Roll in caster sugar, then press a crisscross pattern on top with the back of a knife; store in an airtight box.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 250 g pralines roses (pink sugared almonds), roughly crushed
steps: Mix flour, yeast, sugar, salt, milk and eggs and knead 10 minutes until elastic, then knead in the butter bit by bit until the dough is smooth and glossy.
Work in 200 g of the crushed pralines evenly, cover and leave to rise 1 hour, then chill for 2 hours (or overnight) to firm.
Shape into a round loaf, place on a lined tray and prove 1 hour until puffy.
Brush with the yolk, press the remaining pralines over the top and bake at 180°C for 30–35 minutes until deep golden and hollow-sounding.
Cool on a rack before slicing; the pink sugar melts into crimson streaks in the crumb.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 100 g sugar, plus 2 tbsp pearl sugar for topping
steps: Mix flour, yeast, sugar, salt, milk, eggs, orange-blossom water and rum, then knead 10 minutes and work in the butter until smooth and elastic.
Leave to rise covered for 2 hours at room temperature, then knock back and rest 1 hour in the fridge.
Shape into a ball, push a hole through the centre with your thumbs and stretch it into a large crown about 25 cm wide.
Prove 1 hour on a lined tray, brush with beaten egg, scatter with pearl sugar and bake at 180°C for 30–35 minutes until well browned.
Cool before serving with coffee; in the Drôme it is traditionally eaten at Easter.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 200 g Emmental de Savoie or Abondance, grated
350 ml dry Savoie white wine (Apremont or Jacquère)
1 large stale baguette, cut into cubes with crust on each
steps: Rub the inside of a caquelon (fondue pot) with the cut garlic, then add the wine and heat until steaming.
Add the cheese a handful at a time over medium-low heat, stirring in a figure-of-eight with a wooden spoon until each lot melts.
Mix the cornflour with the kirsch (or a little wine), stir it in and keep stirring for 2–3 minutes until smooth, creamy and just simmering; season with nutmeg and pepper.
Set the pot over its burner at the table, keeping it barely bubbling, and dip bread cubes on long forks, stirring as you go.
Serve with cornichons and a green salad; for strict vegetarians choose cheeses made with microbial rennet.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 1 whole Reblochon cheese (about 450 g) (substitute: Taleggio or another washed-rind cheese)
steps: Boil the potatoes in their skins for 15–20 minutes until just tender, then peel and slice thickly.
Fry the lardons in a dry pan for 5 minutes, add onions and butter and cook 10 minutes until golden; deglaze with the wine and let it reduce by half.
Rub a gratin dish with garlic and layer potatoes with the onion-lardon mix, seasoning lightly, then spoon over the crème fraîche.
Cut the Reblochon in half horizontally and lay both halves rind-side up on top.
Bake at 200°C for 25–30 minutes until the cheese has melted and is bubbling and golden; serve with green salad and charcuterie.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 800 g raclette de Savoie cheese, sliced 4 mm thick
200 g jambon cru (air-dried ham, e.g. jambon de Savoie)
150 g rosette or other dried saucisson
100 g viande des Grisons or bresaola
steps: Boil the potatoes in their skins in salted water for 20 minutes until tender, then keep them warm in a covered basket or dish.
Arrange the cheese slices, charcuterie and pickles on platters and switch on the raclette grill to heat for 10 minutes.
Each diner places a slice of cheese in a coupelle under the grill and melts it for 2–3 minutes until bubbling and lightly browned.
Scrape the melted cheese over halved potatoes, season with pepper or paprika and eat with the charcuterie and pickles.
Serve with dry Savoie white wine or herbal tea, and keep cooking a slice at a time.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 400 g crozets de Savoie (small square buckwheat or wheat pasta) (substitute: orecchiette or small pasta squares)
steps: Cook the crozets in plenty of salted boiling water for 15–20 minutes until tender, then drain.
Fry the lardons for 5 minutes, add onions and butter and cook 10 minutes until golden; deglaze with the wine and reduce for 2 minutes.
Mix the crozets with the lardons, onions and crème fraîche, season and spread in a gratin dish.
Cut the Reblochon in half horizontally and lay it rind-side up on top.
Bake at 200°C for 20 minutes until the cheese has melted and browned; serve with green salad.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 8 diots de Savoie (pork sausages) (substitute: fresh Toulouse sausages)
steps: Prick the diots and brown them in the butter and oil over medium heat for 8 minutes, turning, then remove.
Cook the onions in the same pan for 8–10 minutes until golden, then sprinkle with flour and stir 1 minute.
Pour in the wine, add bay and thyme, return the sausages and bring to a simmer.
Cover and cook gently for 30 minutes until the sausages are cooked through (no pink inside) and the sauce has thickened.
Serve with polenta or crozets and a spoon of the onion-wine sauce.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 1 kg waxy potatoes, peeled and sliced thinly
steps: Heat butter and oil in a large, heavy pan (the long-handled "pelle" or a 28 cm frying pan) and brown the lardons for 4 minutes.
Add onions and potato slices, season and cook over medium heat for 30 minutes, turning regularly, until the potatoes are tender and golden in places.
Press the potatoes flat, cut the Reblochon into slices and lay them on top.
Cover with a lid and cook on low heat for 10 minutes until the cheese has melted completely.
Bring the pan to the table and serve straight from it with salad and charcuterie.

ingredients: 1.5 kg floury potatoes, peeled and grated
10 thin slices smoked bacon or jambon cru, to line the mould
steps: Squeeze the grated potatoes in a cloth to remove excess water.
Brown the lardons for 5 minutes, then mix with potatoes, prunes, raisins, eggs, crème fraîche, flour, 1 tsp salt, pepper and nutmeg.
Line a buttered farçon mould or 1.5 litre bundt tin with the bacon slices and fill with the mixture, folding the overhang on top.
Cover with foil and cook in a bain-marie in a 160°C oven for 3 hours until firm and golden at the edges.
Rest 10 minutes, turn out, slice and serve with a green salad or as a side to roast pork.

ingredients: 400 g Abondance cheese, rind removed, cut into thin slices (substitute: Beaufort or Raclette)
2 tbsp Madeira or dry white port
black pepper and a pinch of nutmeg
600 g small potatoes, boiled in their skins
steps: Rub four small individual gratin dishes (berthoud dishes) with the garlic.
Divide the cheese slices among them, then pour over the wine and Madeira and season with pepper and nutmeg.
Bake at 220°C for 10–12 minutes until the cheese melts and is bubbling with a golden top.
Sprinkle with parsley and serve straight away with hot potatoes and green salad; choose vegetarian-rennet cheese for strict vegetarians.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 4 slices cooked ham or jambon de Savoie
300 g Beaufort or Comté, grated or sliced
steps: Rub the bread with garlic, arrange in a buttered baking dish and drizzle with the wine so it soaks in.
Lay a slice of ham over each pair of bread slices and cover thickly with cheese.
Bake at 220°C for 10–12 minutes until the cheese bubbles and turns golden.
If using, fry the eggs in butter until the whites are set and slide one on top of each croûte.
Grind over pepper and serve hot with salad and a glass of local white wine.

ingredients: 600 g small perch fillets from Lake Geneva (perche du Léman), skin on (substitute: small fillets of walleye or yellow perch)
600 g French fries or boiled potatoes, to serve
steps: Pat the fillets dry, season and dust lightly with flour.
Heat the oil and 20 g butter in a large pan over medium-high heat and fry the fillets for 1–2 minutes per side until golden and opaque all the way through.
Arrange on warm plates; wipe the pan and melt the remaining butter until it foams and turns nut brown (beurre noisette).
Add a squeeze of lemon and the parsley and pour the sizzling butter over the fish.
Serve immediately with lemon wedges, fries and a glass of Savoie or Swiss Chasselas.

ingredients: 2 murçons (Savoie caraway-flavoured smoked pork sausages, about 400 g each) (substitute: smoked Morteau sausage)
steps: Prick the murçons, put them in a pan of cold water with onion, bay and caraway, and bring slowly to just below a simmer.
Poach very gently for 40 minutes without boiling so they don't split.
After 15 minutes add the peeled potatoes and carrots to the same pot and cook until tender, about 25 minutes.
Slice the sausages thickly and serve with the potatoes, carrots and mustard; leftovers are also used in a "murçon gratin" with Tomme.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 1.2 kg floury or all-purpose potatoes (Bintje), peeled
steps: Slice the potatoes 3 mm thick; do not rinse, as the starch thickens the cream.
Bring milk, cream, crushed garlic, nutmeg, 1.5 tsp salt and pepper to a simmer, add the potatoes and cook gently for 10 minutes, stirring carefully.
Rub a gratin dish with the halved garlic and plenty of butter, then tip in the potatoes and liquid and level the top.
Dot with butter and bake at 160°C for 1 hour 15 minutes until the top is golden and a knife slides through easily (no cheese, by Dauphiné tradition).
Rest 10 minutes before serving with roast lamb or a green salad.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 1.2 kg waxy potatoes, peeled and thinly sliced
steps: Rub a gratin dish with garlic and butter it generously.
Layer the potato slices with grated cheese, small knobs of butter, nutmeg, salt and pepper, finishing with cheese.
Pour over the hot stock until it just comes up to the top layer.
Bake at 180°C for 1 hour 15 minutes until the stock is absorbed, the potatoes tender and the top deep golden.
Serve with roast meats or diots.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 150 g fromage blanc or ricotta, well drained
30 g butter and 2 tbsp cream, to serve
steps: Knead flour, salt, water and oil into a smooth, firm dough; wrap and rest 30 minutes.
Mix Comté, fromage blanc, parsley and pepper into a thick filling.

Roll the dough as thinly as possible in two equal sheets, dot one with half-teaspoons of filling 3 cm apart, cover with the second sheet and press around each mound; cut into small 3 cm squares (ready-made Ravioles de Romans are sold in plaques).
Drop the ravioles into gently simmering salted water and cook for 1–2 minutes until they float.
Lift out and toss with melted butter and cream, or bake under more Comté for 5 minutes as a gratin.

ingredients: 1 tbsp vanilla sugar or 1 tsp vanilla extract
15 g butter and 1 tbsp sugar, for the tin
steps: Heat the oven to 160°C; butter a tall savarin or brioche mould and dust with sugar.
Whisk the yolks with sugar, vanilla and zest for 5 minutes until pale and thick, then fold in the sifted flour and starch.
Whisk the whites with salt to firm peaks and fold them into the yolk mixture in three goes, keeping as much air as possible.
Pour into the mould and bake for 35–40 minutes until risen, golden and a skewer comes out clean.
Unmould onto a rack while warm, cool and dust with icing sugar; serve with fruit compote or crème anglaise.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 1 egg plus 1 egg for the custard
80 g sugar, plus 2 tbsp for the fruit
steps: Rub the butter into flour and 50 g sugar, add 1 egg and a spoon of cold water and bring to a dough; chill 30 minutes.
Roll out to line a 26 cm tin, prick the base and sprinkle with the cornflour to absorb juices.
Pack the bilberries in tightly and sprinkle with 2 tbsp sugar.
Bake at 190°C for 25 minutes, then whisk the remaining egg with crème fraîche and 30 g sugar, pour between the berries and bake 15 minutes more until just set.
Cool to room temperature before slicing.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 400 g pear jam or poached pear compote (confiture de poires)
steps: Mix the pear jam with cinnamon and lemon juice.
Roll the pastry 3 mm thick and cut into 12 cm rounds.
Spoon a tablespoon of filling on each round, fold into half-moons and press the edges firmly with a fork to seal.
Place on a lined tray, brush with milk, sprinkle with sugar and cut a small steam vent in each.
Bake at 200°C for 20–25 minutes until puffed and golden; serve warm or cold, as at Christmas in Savoie.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 200 g Grenoble walnuts (noix de Grenoble AOP), finely ground, plus 50 g halves to decorate
100 g dark chocolate and 50 ml cream for icing (optional)
steps: Heat the oven to 170°C and butter a 22 cm round tin.
Whisk eggs and sugar until pale and thick, then stir in the melted butter and rum.
Fold in the ground walnuts, flour and baking powder.
Pour into the tin and bake for 35–40 minutes until firm and a skewer comes out clean.
Cool, then glaze with melted chocolate and cream if desired and decorate with walnut halves.

ingredients: 30 ml Green or Yellow Chartreuse (herbal liqueur), bought from a licensed retailer
steps: Chartreuse is a herbal liqueur made by the Carthusian monks of the Grande Chartreuse near Grenoble from a secret recipe of some 130 plants; Green is 55% ABV and intensely herbal, Yellow is softer, sweeter and 40%.
Buy a bottle from licensed producers or retailers; it is not made at home.
Serve 30 ml neat at room temperature or slightly chilled as a digestif after a rich meal, or over ice; it is also used to flavour hot chocolate and in cocktails such as the Last Word.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 30 ml Génépi des Alpes (Alpine wormwood liqueur), bought from a licensed producer
steps: Génépi is a pale-green or golden liqueur from Savoie and the Aosta valley flavoured with Alpine artemisia plants (génépi), sweet and aromatic at about 35–40% ABV.
Buy it from licensed distilleries or wine shops; do not attempt to make it at home.
Serve 30 ml well chilled in a small glass after a fondue or raclette as a mountain digestif, or pour a dash into hot chocolate after skiing.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 400 g tomme fraîche de l'Aubrac or young Cantal, thinly sliced (substitute: half mozzarella, half young Cantal or Lancashire)
steps: Boil the potatoes in salted water for 20–25 minutes until very tender, drain well and pass through a ricer or mash until smooth.
Return to a heavy pan over low heat, beat in the butter, crème fraîche and garlic and season.
Add the tomme in handfuls, beating vigorously with a wooden spoon in a figure-of-eight and lifting high.
Keep beating for 8–10 minutes until the purée turns glossy, elastic and stretches in long ribbons from the spoon.
Serve at once with Toulouse sausage or grilled meat; for strict vegetarians check the cheese uses microbial rennet.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 1 kg waxy potatoes, peeled and thinly sliced
400 g tomme fraîche de Cantal or young Cantal/Salers, thinly sliced (substitute: young Cheddar)
steps: Melt the lard in a large heavy frying pan and brown the lardons for 4 minutes.
Add the potatoes, season and cook over medium heat for 25–30 minutes, turning often, until tender and golden in places.
Stir in the garlic and parsley, then lay the tomme over the potatoes.
Fold and stir gently for 3–5 minutes until the cheese melts and binds into a golden, stringy cake; let the base crisp for a minute.
Slide onto a plate and serve with green salad and jambon d'Auvergne.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 400 g stale country bread, crusts removed, torn into pieces
300 g tomme fraîche or young Cantal, thinly sliced
steps: Soak the bread in warm milk for 10 minutes, then squeeze out excess milk.
Melt the butter in a heavy frying pan over medium heat, add the garlic and the bread and mash with a spoon until it forms a thick paste.
Add the cheese and stir vigorously for 5–8 minutes until melted and stretchy.
Press flat and let the base turn golden and crisp for 3–4 minutes, then fold over like an omelette.
Serve hot with a green salad.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 800 g palette or shoulder of salt pork (demi-sel), soaked 2 hours
400 g smoked belly bacon (lard fumé) in one piece
1 saucisse d'Auvergne or smoked pork sausage (about 400 g)
1 onion studded with 2 cloves, 1 bouquet garni, peppercorns
steps: Put the salt pork and bacon in a large pot of cold water, bring to the boil, skim and add the onion, bouquet garni and peppercorns; simmer gently for 1 hour 30 minutes.
Blanch the cabbage quarters in boiling water for 5 minutes and drain.
Add cabbage, carrots, turnips and leeks to the pot and simmer 45 minutes more.
Add the sausage and potatoes and simmer 30 minutes until the potatoes are tender and the sausage cooked through.
Serve the broth first over toasted bread, then the meats sliced with the vegetables, mustard and cornichons.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 300 g smoked bacon or ham, finely chopped
250 g Swiss chard (blettes) leaves, finely chopped
steps: Heat the oven to 180°C and butter a 1.5 litre terrine or loaf tin.
Whisk the eggs, flour and milk into a thick batter and season with pepper and a little salt.
Mix in bacon, onion, chard and parsley thoroughly.
Pour half into the tin, lay the prunes in a line, then cover with the remaining batter.
Bake for 1 hour until puffed, golden and a knife comes out clean; serve warm or cold in slices with salad.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 1 kg petit salé (lightly salted pork belly and shoulder) (substitute: unsmoked bacon joint)
400 g green lentils from Le Puy (lentilles vertes du Puy AOP)
steps: Soak the salted pork in cold water for 2 hours to remove excess salt, then drain.
Cover the pork with fresh cold water, add the onion and bouquet garni, bring to a simmer, skim and cook gently for 1 hour 15 minutes.
Add the lentils (unsoaked), carrots, garlic and the sausage if using and simmer 30–40 minutes until the lentils are tender but hold their shape.
Lift out the meat and sausage, slice, and taste the lentils for seasoning (they rarely need salt).
Serve the lentils in deep plates topped with the pork and sausage, sprinkled with parsley, with strong mustard.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 100 g stale bread soaked in 100 ml milk, squeezed
4 thin slices barding fat or streaky bacon
steps: Remove 12 large outer leaves and blanch the whole cabbage and loose leaves in boiling salted water for 8 minutes; refresh and drain, then chop the heart finely.
Mix sausage meat, bacon, onion, garlic, bread, eggs, parsley, chopped cabbage heart, salt and pepper.
Line a large bowl with the leaves overlapping, fill with the stuffing, fold the leaves over to re-form a cabbage and tie with string.
Place in a casserole, cover with bacon slices, pour in stock and braise covered at 170°C for 1 hour 45 minutes until the centre reaches 75°C.
Rest 10 minutes, untie, cut into wedges and serve with the reduced cooking juices and potatoes.

ingredients: 1 kg lamb or veal tripe (panse), cleaned and blanched, cut into 12 squares
500 g lamb or calf's feet, blanched
200 g salt pork belly, finely chopped
3 garlic cloves and 1 bunch parsley, chopped
1 bouquet garni, 2 cloves, salt and pepper
steps: Simmer the feet in water for 2 hours, then pick the meat off and chop finely; mix with the pork belly, garlic, parsley, salt and pepper.
Put a spoonful of this filling on each square of tripe, fold into little parcels and tie with string.
Sweat onions and carrots in a casserole for 5 minutes, add tomato purée, wine, stock, bouquet garni and cloves, then lay in the parcels.
Cover tightly and cook in the oven at 140°C for 5 hours until meltingly tender.
Serve hot with boiled potatoes; in Aveyron and Cantal tripoux are traditionally eaten for a hearty late breakfast.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 2 tbsp sugar (for the sweet version, instead of herbs)
steps: Whisk the eggs with the flour, then slowly whisk in the milk to a thick, smooth batter; season and stir in the herbs.
Melt a quarter of the butter in a 24 cm pan over medium heat and pour in a quarter of the batter.
Cook for 3 minutes until set at the edges and golden underneath, then flip and cook 2 minutes more.
Repeat with the remaining batter and serve hot with salad, or sprinkled with sugar as a sweet farinette.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 250 g green lentils from Le Puy (lentilles vertes du Puy AOP) (substitute: French green or Castelluccio lentils)
1 red onion or 2 shallots, finely chopped
steps: Rinse the lentils, cover with cold water, add the carrot, bay and thyme and simmer for 20–25 minutes until tender but still holding their shape; salt at the end.
Whisk mustard, vinegar, salt and pepper, then whisk in the oil.
Drain the lentils, remove the herbs and toss while warm with the dressing and onion.
Leave 15 minutes to absorb, add parsley and serve warm or at room temperature, with walnuts or a little crumbled Bleu d'Auvergne if you like.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 8 slices stale country bread (pain de seigle or campagne)
steps: Cook the onions in butter over medium-low heat for 10 minutes until soft and golden.
Add cabbage, potatoes and stock and simmer for 30 minutes until all is tender; season.
Layer the bread and Cantal slices in a deep ovenproof tureen or individual bowls.
Ladle the soup over, let it soak for 2 minutes, then bake at 200°C for 10 minutes until the cheese bubbles.
Serve very hot; the soup should be thick enough for a spoon to stand up.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 250 g buckwheat flour (farine de sarrasin / blé noir)
steps: Whisk both flours with the salt and yeast, then gradually whisk in the warmed buttermilk and water to a thick batter.
Cover and leave to ferment in a warm place for 2 hours until bubbly.
Heat a heavy pan or griddle over medium heat and grease with butter.
Ladle in batter to make thick 18 cm pancakes and cook 3–4 minutes per side until set and speckled with holes.
Serve hot with butter and honey, or savoury with Cantal and salad, as Cantal farmhouses ate them as daily bread.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 4 apples or pears, peeled and sliced
30 g butter, melted, plus more for the dish
steps: Heat the oven to 190°C and butter a 26 cm baking dish.
Whisk the eggs and sugar, add the flour and salt, then whisk in the milk, melted butter and rum to a smooth batter.
Arrange the fruit in the dish and pour the batter over.
Bake for 35–40 minutes until puffed, golden and set in the centre.
Dust with icing sugar and serve lukewarm; it sinks as it cools, like a clafoutis.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

steps: Whisk the egg whites lightly with sugar, then stir in the melted butter, flour and vanilla to a smooth batter.
Spread tablespoons of batter into thin 12 cm circles on a lined baking tray and bake at 180°C for 6–8 minutes until golden at the edges.
While hot, immediately roll each round around a metal cone mould and leave to set; work quickly, 2–3 at a time.
Whip the cream with icing sugar and kirsch to firm peaks.
Just before serving, pipe the cream into the crisp cones so they stay crunchy.
