ingredients: 1 kg apples (Reinette or Canada), peeled and sliced
steps: Rub butter into the flour and salt, add cold water and bring together into a dough; chill 30 minutes.
Toss the apples with sugar and cinnamon.
Roll out two-thirds of the pastry to line a deep 26 cm tin and pack in the apples.
Roll out the rest for a lid, seal the edges, cut a steam hole and brush with milk.
Bake at 190°C for 40–45 minutes until golden and the apples are soft; serve warm or cold.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 1 kg pork shoulder or salt pork (demi-sel)
1 Limousin pork sausage or smoked sausage (about 400 g)
1 red cabbage, quartered (the Limousin hallmark; green cabbage also used)
1 onion studded with cloves, 1 bouquet garni
steps: Put the pork and bacon in a large pot of cold water, bring to a boil, skim, add onion and bouquet garni and simmer 1 hour 30 minutes.
Add the cabbage, carrots and turnips and simmer 45 minutes.
Add the chestnuts, potatoes and sausage and simmer 30 minutes until all is tender and the sausage cooked through.
Lift out the meats and slice; serve the broth first, then the meats with the vegetables and chestnuts, with mustard.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 1 kg waxy potatoes, peeled and very thinly sliced
steps: Line a buttered 26 cm pie dish with one pastry sheet, leaving an overhang.
Layer the potatoes with onions, garlic, parsley, salt, pepper and nutmeg.
Cover with the second sheet, seal and crimp the edges, brush with milk and cut a 2 cm chimney hole in the centre.
Bake at 190°C for 1 hour until the potatoes are tender when tested through the hole (cover with foil if browning too fast).
Spoon the crème fraîche into the pie through the chimney, return for 5–10 minutes, then serve warm with green salad.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 600 g boudin noir aux châtaignes (black pudding with chestnuts), from a charcutier
steps: Prick the boudin lightly and cut into 4 portions.
Fry the apple wedges and onion in half the butter over medium heat for 8–10 minutes until golden; add the chestnuts to warm through.
In another pan heat the oil and remaining butter and fry the boudin over medium-low heat for 10–12 minutes, turning gently, until browned and heated right through.
Serve the boudin with the apples, onions and chestnuts and mashed potatoes.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 400 g Creusois cheese or young Saint-Nectaire, rind removed and cubed (substitute: young Cantal or Gouda)
500 g country bread cubes and boiled potatoes, to serve
steps: Rub a heavy pot with garlic and melt the butter over low heat.
Add the cheese and milk and stir constantly until melted and smooth.
Mix the cornflour into the crème fraîche, stir it in and simmer gently for 2–3 minutes until thick and creamy; season.
Keep warm on a fondue burner and dip bread and potatoes into it.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 250 g salt pork belly or bacon with its rind (couenne)
steps: Bring the pork and rind to a boil in the water, skim and simmer for 1 hour.
Add all the vegetables and simmer for 1 hour more until very tender.
Lift out the pork, slice it and return it to the pot; taste for seasoning.
Put a slice of rye bread in each bowl and ladle the soup over; Limousin tradition is to finish with "chabrol", a splash of red wine in the last of the broth.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

steps: Whisk the flour and salt with the water to a smooth, pourable batter and rest for 1 hour.
Heat a cast-iron crêpe pan over medium-high heat and grease lightly.
Pour a ladle of batter and spread thinly; cook 2 minutes until the edges lift, flip and cook 1 minute.
Serve warm rolled with butter, or dipped in soup, as Limousin and Corrèze farmhouses did in place of bread.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 500 g black cherries, unpitted as tradition requires
steps: Heat the oven to 180°C and butter a 24 cm ceramic dish; scatter the cherries in a single layer (the pits give the classic almond flavour; warn guests).
Whisk eggs and sugar, add flour and salt, then whisk in milk, cream and vanilla to a smooth batter.
Pour the batter over the cherries.
Bake for 35–40 minutes until puffed, golden and set in the middle.
Cool to lukewarm, dust with icing sugar and serve.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 125 g butter, melted and lightly browned
steps: Heat the oven to 180°C and butter a 24 cm round tin.
Mix the hazelnut flour, plain flour and sugar.
Whisk the egg whites with salt to soft peaks and fold into the dry mixture, then fold in the cooled browned butter.
Pour into the tin and bake for 25–30 minutes until golden and firm with a soft centre.
Cool, dust with icing sugar and cut into wedges; it keeps well for several days.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 1 tsp bitter almond extract or orange-blossom water
steps: Heat the oven to 160°C and line a 22 cm square tin with baking paper.
Mix ground almonds and sugar, then stir in 2 egg whites and the almond extract to a thick paste.
Whisk the other 2 whites with salt to soft peaks and fold in gently.
Spread in the tin and bake for 25–30 minutes until pale golden with a crisp crust and a moist, chewy middle.
Cool, dust with icing sugar and cut into squares; this airy almond cake is a speciality of Saint-Léonard-de-Noblat.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 1.5 kg beef chuck (paleron) or Charolais shin, cut in 5 cm chunks
1 onion, chopped, plus 18 small pearl onions, peeled
250 g button mushrooms (champignons de Paris), quartered
steps: Marinate the beef overnight in the red wine with the carrots, chopped onion, garlic and bouquet garni, then drain, keeping the wine, and pat the meat dry.
In a heavy casserole brown the lardons in the oil over medium heat for 5 minutes, lift out, then sear the beef in batches over high heat until deeply browned on all sides.
Return the beef, sprinkle with flour and stir for 2 minutes, then add the marinade wine with its vegetables, the stock and lardons; bring to a simmer.
Cover and cook on the lowest heat or in a 150 °C oven for 3 hours until the beef is fork-tender.
Meanwhile brown the pearl onions and mushrooms in the butter for 10 minutes; stir them into the stew for the last 20 minutes and serve with boiled potatoes or fresh pasta.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 1 rooster or large free-range chicken (2.5 kg), cut in 8 pieces
2 tbsp cognac or marc de Bourgogne
steps: Marinate the chicken overnight in the wine with carrot, onion, garlic and bouquet garni, then drain and dry the pieces, keeping the wine.
Brown the lardons in a casserole, remove, then brown the chicken in the fat and butter over medium-high heat for 10 minutes until golden.
Pour in the cognac and flame it carefully, sprinkle with flour and stir 2 minutes, then add the wine and vegetables and bring to a simmer.
Cover and simmer gently for 2 hours for a rooster (1 hour for a chicken) until the meat pulls from the bone and reaches 75 °C.
Fry the pearl onions and mushrooms in a little butter, add them with the lardons for the last 15 minutes, reduce the sauce if thin and serve with steamed potatoes.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 24 prepared Burgundy snails (canned or frozen) with 24 cleaned shells
1/2 tsp salt and a pinch of black pepper
1 tbsp dry white wine (Chablis or Aligoté)
steps: Rinse and drain the snails; heat the oven to 220 °C.
Beat the butter with garlic, shallot, parsley, salt, pepper and wine into a smooth green "beurre d'escargot".
Push a little butter into each shell, insert a snail, then seal the opening generously with more butter.
Stand the shells opening-up in an escargot dish and bake for 10–12 minutes until the butter sizzles and bubbles.
Serve immediately with tongs, small forks and crusty baguette to mop the butter.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 30 g butter mashed with 1 tbsp flour (beurre manié)
4 slices country bread, toasted and rubbed with garlic
steps: Simmer the wine with shallot, onion, garlic and bouquet garni for 20 minutes until reduced by a third.
Lower to a bare simmer and poach the eggs two at a time for 3 minutes until the whites set; lift out onto a warm plate.
Strain the wine, return to the pan and whisk in the beurre manié a little at a time; simmer 5 minutes until glossy and coating a spoon. Season.
Fry the lardons until crisp.
Place two eggs on each toast, spoon over the meurette sauce, scatter with lardons and serve hot.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 1.5 kg unsmoked ham hock or cured ham shoulder, desalted overnight
1 calf's foot or 2 pig's trotters, split
750 ml dry white Burgundy (Aligoté or Chablis)
1 large bunch flat-leaf parsley, chopped (about 60 g)
steps: Soak the ham overnight in cold water, then drain.
Put the ham, calf's foot, wine, onion, carrots and bouquet garni in a pot, add water to cover and simmer gently for 3 hours until the ham falls apart.
Lift out the meat, strain the stock through a fine sieve and reduce it to about 500 ml; stir in the vinegar and pepper.
Shred the ham into chunks; mix the parsley, shallots and garlic.
Layer ham and parsley mixture in a terrine, pour over the warm stock to cover and chill at least 12 hours until set.
Slice and serve cold with Dijon mustard, cornichons and crusty bread.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 125 g Comté or Gruyère, finely grated
a pinch of nutmeg and black pepper
steps: Heat the oven to 200 °C; bring water, milk, butter and salt to a boil.
Tip in the flour at once and beat over medium heat for 2 minutes until the dough leaves the pan sides.
Off the heat beat in the eggs one by one until the dough is smooth and glossy, then stir in 100 g cheese, nutmeg and pepper.
Pipe walnut-sized mounds onto a lined tray, brush with yolk and top with the remaining cheese.
Bake 25–30 minutes without opening the oven until puffed, golden and hollow; serve warm with a glass of Chablis or Kir.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 1.5 kg mixed freshwater fish (pike, eel, perch, tench, carp), cleaned and cut in chunks
6 slices bread, toasted and rubbed with garlic
steps: Brown the lardons and pearl onions in half the butter in a wide pan for 8 minutes.
Add the fish, starting with the firmer eel and carp, then pour in the wine with garlic and bouquet garni; bring to a simmer.
Poach gently for 15–20 minutes until all the fish flakes easily and is opaque.
Lift out the fish, whisk the remaining butter mashed with flour into the liquid and simmer 5 minutes, then stir in the crème fraîche and season.
Return the fish to warm through and serve over garlic croutons.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

steps: Season the chicken and brown it in butter in an ovenproof dish over medium heat for 15 minutes, then cover and cook 20 minutes until the juices run clear.
Heat the oven grill. Lift out the chicken, deglaze with the wine and reduce by half.
Stir in the crème fraîche, mustard, paprika and 100 g Comté and simmer until the cheese melts into a smooth sauce.
Return the chicken, coat with sauce, scatter with the rest of the cheese and breadcrumbs.
Grill 5–8 minutes until bubbling and golden; serve with rice or tagliatelle.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 8 thick slices cooked ham (jambon blanc), about 600 g
250 ml Chablis or other dry white Burgundy
steps: Soften the shallots in butter for 3 minutes, stir in the flour and cook 1 minute.
Add the Chablis and thyme and reduce by half over medium heat, then whisk in the tomato paste and crème fraîche; simmer 5 minutes until creamy.
Lay the ham slices overlapping in a gratin dish and pour over the sauce.
Bake at 180 °C for 15 minutes until hot and lightly bubbling; serve with mashed potatoes or spinach.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 800 g salted pork shoulder (palette demi-sel), soaked 2 hours
1 smoked Burgundy sausage or Morteau sausage
steps: Put the pork shoulder and belly in a large pot with cold water, onion, bouquet garni and peppercorns; bring to a simmer and skim.
Simmer gently for 1 hour 30 minutes.
Blanch the cabbage for 5 minutes in a separate pan, then add it with the carrots, turnips and leeks to the pot.
After 20 minutes add the sausage and potatoes and cook 30–40 minutes more until all is tender.
Slice the meats, arrange over the vegetables with a little broth and serve with Dijon mustard and coarse salt.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 150 ml dry white wine (Aligoté) or verjuice
steps: Soak the mustard seeds in the wine and vinegar, covered, for 24 hours until plump.
Add salt, sugar and water and blend in a food processor for 3–5 minutes into a smooth paste, adding a little water if too thick.
Press through a fine sieve for a classic smooth Dijon texture, or leave grainy for moutarde à l'ancienne.
Pack into a clean jar and refrigerate 2–3 days to mellow; keeps for 2 months chilled.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 250 g dark honey (chestnut or forest honey)
1 tsp baking soda plus 1 tsp baking powder
2 tsp ground mixed spice (cinnamon, ginger, nutmeg, clove)
steps: Warm the honey and milk gently until runny but not hot.
Mix the flours, raising agents, spices, aniseed, salt, peel and zest in a bowl.
Pour in the honey mixture and beat to a smooth, thick batter.
Pour into a lined loaf tin and bake at 160 °C for 55–60 minutes until a skewer comes out clean.
Wrap when cool and rest 1–2 days before slicing; it gets moister and spicier.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 20 g butter, melted, plus extra for the dish
steps: Heat the oven to 190 °C and butter a shallow baking dish.
Whisk eggs and sugar, then add the flour and salt, then gradually the milk and melted butter to a smooth, crêpe-like batter.
Spread the apples in the dish and pour over the batter.
Bake 30–35 minutes until puffed, set and golden; sprinkle with vanilla sugar and serve warm.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

steps: Rub the butter into the flour and salt, then add the egg and water and bring together into a pastry; chill 30 minutes.
Beat the fromage blanc with 2 eggs, sugar, flour and lemon zest into a smooth filling.
Roll the pastry 3 mm thick and cut 12 cm rounds; spoon filling in the centre.
Fold up three sides and pinch to form tricorn hats, leaving the filling visible in the middle; brush pastry with yolk.
Bake at 190 °C for 25–30 minutes until golden and the filling is set.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 120 ml chilled dry white Burgundy Aligoté (bought from licensed producers)
15–20 ml crème de cassis de Dijon (blackcurrant liqueur)
steps: Pour the crème de cassis into a chilled wine glass.
Top with the cold Aligoté and stir gently once; garnish with lemon if liked.
Serve as an apéritif with gougères; with Champagne instead of Aligoté it becomes a Kir Royal.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 2 Morteau sausages (about 800 g), pricked (sub: any smoked pork sausage)
steps: Put the sausages in cold water, bring to a bare simmer (do not boil) and poach for 40 minutes.
Meanwhile sweat the onion, carrot and lardons in butter for 5 minutes, add the lentils, bouquet garni and water to cover by 3 cm.
Simmer the lentils 25–30 minutes until tender but whole; season with salt, pepper, vinegar and mustard.
Slice the sausages thickly and serve over the lentils with extra mustard.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 1 Mont d'Or (Vacherin du Haut-Doubs) cheese in its spruce box, 500 g (sub: Vacherin or ripe Camembert-style soft cheese)
60 ml dry white Jura wine (Savagnin or Chardonnay)
cornichons and pickled onions to serve
steps: Boil the potatoes in salted water for 20 minutes until tender.
Heat the oven to 200 °C; remove the lid and plastic from the cheese, wrap the box base in foil.
Cut a few slits in the rind, push in the garlic and pour over the wine; add pepper.
Bake 20–25 minutes until molten and bubbling; serve at the table spooned over the hot potatoes with pickles.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 800 g Comté (mix of young and aged), grated
a pinch of nutmeg and pepper
1 large baguette, cut in cubes a day ahead
steps: Rub the inside of a fondue pot (caquelon) with garlic.
Heat the wine until steaming, then add the cheese a handful at a time, stirring in a figure-eight over medium-low heat until melted.
Mix the cornflour with the kirsch, stir in and cook 2 minutes until smooth and creamy; season with nutmeg and pepper.
Set on a burner at the table and dip bread cubes on long forks, stirring as you dip.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 300 g fresh morels or 40 g dried morels, soaked 30 minutes
100 ml Vin Jaune or dry sherry
steps: Halve and rinse the morels well to remove grit; if dried, strain and keep the soaking liquid.
Fry the shallots in butter for 3 minutes, add the morels and cook 5 minutes over medium heat.
Add the Vin Jaune (and a little soaking liquid) and reduce by half, then stir in the cream and simmer until thick and coating. Season.
Toast the bread lightly, pile on the morels in cream, top with Comté and grill 3–4 minutes until golden.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

dishes.name: Poulet au Vin Jaune et aux Morilles

ingredients: 1 Bresse chicken or free-range chicken (1.8 kg), cut in 8 pieces
30 g dried morels, soaked in warm water 30 minutes
250 ml Vin Jaune (sub: dry fino sherry)
steps: Season and brown the chicken in butter over medium heat for 12 minutes until golden; add the shallots for the last 3 minutes.
Pour in 200 ml Vin Jaune, cover and simmer gently 35 minutes until the chicken is cooked through (75 °C).
Rinse the morels, sauté briefly in a little butter, and add with the crème fraîche and a splash of strained soaking water.
Simmer uncovered 10 minutes until the sauce coats the spoon, then stir in the last 50 ml of Vin Jaune off the heat; serve with rice or fresh pasta.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 250 g metton (dried skimmed-milk curd), or cancoillotte base; sub: 300 g fromage frais plus 50 g Comté
steps: Put the metton with the water in a heavy pan over low heat.
Stir constantly for 10 minutes until it melts into a smooth, runny, translucent yellow cream.
Beat in the butter, salt, garlic and wine until glossy.
Serve warm over boiled potatoes, sausage or bread, or chilled as a spread.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 300 g brési (smoked, salt-cured, air-dried beef from the Haut-Doubs), sub: bresaola
steps: Slice the brési paper-thin with a sharp knife or slicer.
Arrange overlapping on a board, drizzle lightly with walnut oil and sprinkle with chives and black pepper.
Serve as an apéritif with cornichons and bread.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 120 g gaudes flour (toasted cornmeal from Bresse/Jura); sub: fine cornmeal dry-toasted in a pan until nutty
1 litre milk (or half milk, half water)
2 tbsp cream or sugar to serve
steps: If using plain cornmeal, toast it in a dry pan over medium heat for 6–8 minutes, stirring, until golden and fragrant.
Whisk the flour into the cold milk with the salt, then bring slowly to a boil, whisking.
Simmer 10–15 minutes, stirring, until thick and smooth.
Serve hot in bowls with a knob of butter and cream, or sugared for children.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

steps: Boil water, butter, sugar and salt, tip in the flour and beat over heat 2 minutes to a smooth choux dough.
Off the heat beat in the eggs one by one, then the orange-flower water and zest.
Spread into a buttered 26 cm tart tin about 2 cm thick, brush with yolk, score a criss-cross pattern and sprinkle with pearl sugar.
Bake at 190 °C for 25–30 minutes until puffed and golden; eat warm.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 1.5 kg raw fermented sauerkraut (choucroute crue), rinsed and squeezed
300 ml dry Alsace Riesling or Sylvaner
10 juniper berries, 2 bay leaves, 1 tsp coriander seed, 4 cloves
steps: Soften the onions in goose fat in a large casserole for 5 minutes without colouring.
Add half the sauerkraut, the spices tied in muslin, the pork shoulder and belly, cover with the remaining sauerkraut and pour in the wine plus 200 ml water.
Cover and simmer gently or bake at 160 °C for 2 hours.
Add the Montbéliard sausages and potatoes for the last 40 minutes, and warm the Strasbourg sausages in hot (not boiling) water for 10 minutes.
Pile the sauerkraut on a platter with sliced meats, sausages and potatoes; serve with mustard and horseradish.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 3 g dried yeast (optional, traditional dough is unleavened)
200 g crème fraîche épaisse mixed with 100 g fromage blanc
a pinch of nutmeg, salt and pepper
steps: Knead flour, water, oil, salt and yeast into a smooth dough and rest 1 hour.
Heat the oven as hot as it goes (250–300 °C) with a baking stone or tray inside.
Roll the dough paper-thin into two rectangles; spread with the seasoned cream mixture, scatter with onions and lardons.
Bake 7–10 minutes until the edges are blistered and crisp and the lardons cooked; cut in squares and eat with fingers.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 500 g pork shoulder, 500 g lamb shoulder, 500 g beef chuck, cut in chunks
750 ml dry Alsace Riesling or Sylvaner
200 g flour plus 120 ml water for a sealing dough
steps: Marinate the meats overnight in the wine with onions, garlic, cloves, juniper and bouquet garni.
Heat the oven to 180 °C. In a terrine layer a third of the potatoes, then half the meat with leeks and carrots, seasoning each layer; repeat, ending with potatoes.
Pour in the marinade to just cover.
Mix flour and water to a dough, roll into a rope and press around the lid to seal it hermetically.
Bake 3 to 3 1/2 hours; break the crust at the table and serve straight from the dish with a green salad.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 1 large chicken (2 kg), cut in 8 pieces
1/2 tsp salt and pepper, pinch of nutmeg
steps: Brown the chicken in butter over medium heat for 12 minutes until golden; add shallots and cook 2 minutes.
Flame with cognac, pour in the Riesling, cover and simmer 45 minutes until cooked through.
Add the mushrooms for the last 15 minutes.
Lift out the chicken, reduce the liquid by a third, then stir in the cream (and yolk off the heat) and season with nutmeg.
Return the chicken to the sauce and serve with buttered spaetzle.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 200 ml crème fraîche and 100 ml milk
steps: Line a 26 cm tart tin with pastry and chill; heat the oven to 200 °C.
Cook the onions slowly in butter, covered, over low heat for 30 minutes until soft and pale gold, not browned.
Fry the lardons briefly and add to the onions.
Whisk eggs, cream, milk, flour, salt, pepper and nutmeg, combine with the cooled onions and pour into the case.
Bake 35–40 minutes until set and golden; serve warm with new wine (vin nouveau) in autumn.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 500 g leftover cooked beef (from pot-au-feu), minced
1 onion and 2 tbsp parsley, finely chopped
1 egg plus 1 stale bread roll soaked in milk and squeezed
steps: Knead flour, 3 eggs and salt into a firm noodle dough, wrap and rest 30 minutes.
Sweat the onion in butter, mix with the minced beef, parsley, soaked bread and egg; season well.
Roll the dough very thin into a rectangle, spread with filling, roll up tightly and cut into 3 cm "snails".
Brown the spirals cut-side down in butter for 3 minutes per side, then pour in the stock, cover and simmer 15 minutes until absorbed.
Serve with a green salad and the pan juices.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 1 tsp salt plus salt for the water
steps: Beat flour, eggs, milk, salt and nutmeg into a thick, sticky batter until it bubbles; rest 10 minutes.
Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil.
Press the batter through a spaetzle maker or scrape thin strips off a wet board into the water.
Once they float, cook 1 minute more, then lift out and drain.
Toss in foaming butter over medium heat for 3–4 minutes until lightly golden; serve with game, coq au Riesling or gravy.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

steps: Beat flour, eggs, milk, salt and nutmeg into a thick, elastic batter that holds on a spoon.
Dip a teaspoon in boiling salted water, scoop small quenelles of batter and drop them in.
Simmer 8–10 minutes until they float and are cooked through; drain.
Brown the breadcrumbs in butter until nutty and toss with the knepfle; serve as a side or in soup.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 100 g fresh pork belly or lard
2 stale bread rolls soaked in milk and squeezed
1 tsp salt, pepper, pinch of nutmeg
40 g butter and 1 sliced onion to serve
steps: Mince the liver, pork belly, onion and bread finely together, or pulse in a food processor.
Beat in eggs, flour, parsley and seasoning to a soft paste that holds on a spoon.
Drop spoonfuls into simmering salted water and poach 10–12 minutes until firm and cooked through.
Fry the sliced onion in butter until golden, pour over the dumplings and serve with sauerkraut or potato salad.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 1.5 kg smoked pork shoulder (schiffala, palette fumée)
2 tbsp white wine vinegar and 4 tbsp oil
1 red onion, finely chopped, and 2 tbsp chives
steps: Cover the shoulder with cold water, add onion, carrot, leek, bay and peppercorns and bring slowly to a simmer.
Poach gently, never boiling, for 2 to 2 1/2 hours until tender.
Boil the potatoes in their skins 20 minutes, peel and slice while warm.
Dress the potatoes with vinegar, oil, mustard, red onion, chives and a ladle of hot broth.
Slice the pork and serve warm with the potato salad and horseradish.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 2 smoked or salted pork knuckles (about 1 kg each)
steps: Simmer the knuckles in water with vegetables and spices for 2 1/2 hours until the meat is very tender.
Heat the oven to 200 °C; drain the knuckles and score the skin.
Mix the beer, honey and mustard and brush over.
Roast 25–30 minutes, basting, until the skin is crisp and lacquered; serve with sauerkraut, potatoes and mustard.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 1.5 kg mixed river fish (pike, perch, trout, eel, tench), filleted and cut in pieces
steps: Sweat the shallots in half the butter for 3 minutes, add the mushrooms and cook 5 minutes.
Pour in the Riesling and stock, bring to a simmer and poach the fish, eel first, for 10–12 minutes until just opaque and flaking.
Lift out the fish; thicken the liquid with the remaining butter mashed with flour and simmer 5 minutes.
Off the heat whisk in the cream mixed with yolks without boiling; return the fish, sprinkle with parsley and serve with buttered noodles.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 1 pig's head (or 1 kg pork cheeks plus 2 trotters)
steps: Soak the meat in cold water overnight, then put in a large pot with vegetables, spices, wine and water to cover.
Simmer gently for 3 hours until the meat falls from the bone.
Lift out, strip the meat and cut in small pieces; strain the broth and reduce to about 600 ml with the vinegar.
Mix the meat with shallots, gherkins and parsley, pack into a terrine and pour over the broth.
Chill 12 hours until firm; slice and serve with vinaigrette, onions and bread.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 150 g Emmental or Gruyère, in thin strips
steps: Halve the cervelas lengthwise, score the rounded side and slice, or cut into strips.
Whisk oil, vinegar, mustard, salt and pepper into a vinaigrette.
Toss cervelas, cheese, onion and gherkins with the dressing (this version is the "cervelas-gruyère").
Rest 15 minutes, sprinkle with herbs and serve with buttered bread or potato salad.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 500 g full-fat fromage blanc, well drained
3 tbsp chives, parsley and chervil, chopped
steps: Boil or roast the potatoes in their skins for 25 minutes until tender (sautéed potatoes are also common).
Beat the fromage blanc with the crème fraîche until smooth.
Stir in shallots, garlic, herbs, salt and pepper; chill.
Serve the cool herb cheese with the hot potatoes, traditionally with Munster on the side.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 1 tsp salt and pepper, pinch of nutmeg
100 ml oil or lard for frying
apple sauce or green salad to serve
steps: Grate the potatoes and onion coarsely and squeeze out as much liquid as possible in a cloth.
Mix with eggs, flour, parsley, salt, pepper and nutmeg.
Heat 5 mm of oil in a frying pan over medium-high heat, drop in spoonfuls and flatten.
Fry 3–4 minutes per side until deep golden and crisp; drain and serve hot with apple sauce or salad.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 1 litre water plus 3 tbsp baking soda (traditional lye bath is safer replaced by baking soda at home)
steps: Knead flour, water, yeast, sugar, salt and butter for 10 minutes into a firm dough; rise 45 minutes.
Divide into 8, roll each into a 60 cm rope thicker in the middle, and twist into the pretzel knot; chill 20 minutes uncovered.
Bring the water and baking soda to a simmer and dip each pretzel for 30 seconds; drain.
Sprinkle with coarse salt, slash the thick part and bake at 220 °C for 12–15 minutes until deep brown and shiny.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: raisins and pearl sugar to decorate
steps: Knead flour, milk, yeast, sugar, salt, egg, zest and butter into a soft, smooth brioche dough; rise 1 hour.
Divide into 8 oblong pieces and shape little men: snip the arms and legs with scissors and pinch a head.
Add raisins for eyes and buttons, rise 30 minutes, brush with yolk and sprinkle with pearl sugar.
Bake at 180 °C for 15–20 minutes until golden; eat for Saint Nicholas (6 December) with hot chocolate.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 15 g fresh yeast or 7 g dried
100 g raisins soaked in 2 tbsp kirsch or rum
steps: Dissolve the yeast in the milk with a little flour and leave 20 minutes until foamy.
Knead with the rest of the flour, sugar, salt and eggs for 10 minutes, then work in the butter until the dough is elastic; fold in the raisins.
Rise covered for 1 1/2 hours, then refrigerate overnight for flavour.
Butter a kougelhopf mould, place an almond in each groove, press in the dough and rise 2 hours until near the rim.
Bake at 180 °C for 40–45 minutes until deep golden; unmould, cool and dust with icing sugar.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

steps: Cream the butter and sugar, add the egg, vanilla and zest, then the flour and salt to form a soft dough (this is the classic butter "Butterbredele").
Wrap and chill 1 hour.
Roll 4 mm thick and cut stars, hearts and moons; brush with yolk.
Bake at 180 °C for 10–12 minutes until just golden at the edges; store in tins through Advent.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 1 kg quetsches (Damson-like Alsace plums), halved and stoned (sub: Italian prune plums)
steps: Line a 28 cm tin with the pastry and sprinkle with semolina to absorb juices.
Stand the plum halves upright in tight concentric circles, cut-side up.
Bake at 200 °C for 25 minutes.
Whisk egg, cream and 30 g sugar, pour between the plums and bake 15 minutes more until set.
Sprinkle with remaining sugar mixed with cinnamon while warm.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

steps: Line a deep 24 cm springform tin with the pastry.
Beat fromage blanc, yolks, 80 g sugar, cream, cornflour, zest and vanilla until smooth.
Whisk the whites to soft peaks with the remaining sugar and fold in gently.
Pour into the case and bake at 180 °C for 50–60 minutes until risen and golden.
Turn out upside down onto a rack as it cools to keep it from sinking; serve at room temperature.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 500 g dried pears, 250 g dried figs, 250 g prunes, chopped
100 g walnuts and 100 g hazelnuts, roughly chopped
100 g candied orange and lemon peel
2 tsp cinnamon plus 1/2 tsp clove and star anise, ground
500 g bread dough (flour, water, yeast, salt), proved once
1 tbsp honey diluted in water to glaze
steps: Simmer the dried pears 10 minutes to soften, drain, then mix with all the fruit, nuts, peel, spices and kirsch; macerate overnight.
Work the fruit mixture into two-thirds of the bread dough so it is mostly fruit held together by dough.
Shape into 3 loaves and wrap each in a thin layer of the remaining dough.
Bake at 180 °C for 50–60 minutes until browned, brushing with honey water at the end.
Wrap and rest a few days before slicing thinly at Christmas.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 1/2 tsp salt, pepper and a pinch of nutmeg
steps: Line a 26 cm tart tin with the pastry, prick and chill 20 minutes, then blind-bake at 200 °C for 12 minutes.
Fry the lardons in butter for 5 minutes until lightly coloured, drain and scatter over the case.
Whisk the eggs, yolk, cream, milk and seasoning (the authentic version has no cheese).
Pour into the case and bake at 180 °C for 30 minutes until puffed, golden and just set in the centre.
Rest 10 minutes and serve warm with a green salad.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 800 g salted pork shoulder (palette demi-sel), soaked 2 hours
200 g dried white beans, soaked overnight and part-cooked (optional)
1 onion stuck with cloves, 1 bouquet garni
steps: Put the pork shoulder and belly in cold water with onion and bouquet garni, bring to a simmer and skim.
Simmer 1 hour 15 minutes.
Add the blanched cabbage, carrots, turnips, leeks and beans and cook 30 minutes.
Add the sausages and potatoes and cook 30 minutes more until everything is tender.
Serve the broth first over bread, then the sliced meats and vegetables with mustard and gherkins.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 400 g pork loin or shoulder, cut in thin strips
300 g veal shoulder, cut in thin strips
250 ml dry white wine (Côtes de Toul gris or Riesling)
steps: Marinate the meats overnight with wine, shallots, garlic, herbs and seasoning; drain well.
Lay one pastry sheet on a lined tray, pile the meat along the centre leaving a 3 cm border.
Cover with the second sheet, seal the edges, cut a chimney hole and brush with egg; score a pattern.
Bake at 200 °C for 15 minutes, then 180 °C for 35 minutes until deep golden and the meat is cooked through (75 °C at the centre).
Serve warm or cold with salad.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 300 g pork shoulder and 300 g veal, diced small
2 sheets puff pastry or shortcrust (500 g)
steps: Marinate the meats overnight in wine with shallots, garlic, parsley and seasoning; drain.
Line a deep 24 cm pie tin with one pastry sheet and fill with the meat.
Cover with the second sheet, seal, cut a chimney and brush with beaten egg.
Bake at 190 °C for 45 minutes.
Whisk 2 eggs with the cream, pour through the chimney with a funnel and bake 15 minutes more until set and the meat is cooked through.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 2 eggs plus 1 hard-boiled egg per person to garnish
steps: Knead flour, eggs, salt and water into a firm pasta dough and rest 30 minutes.
Roll thin and cut into 4–5 cm squares or diamonds; dry 15 minutes.
Boil in salted water 4–5 minutes until tender and drain.
Toss the warm pasta with a dressing of oil, vinegar, shallots, crème fraîche and herbs.
Serve warm or tepid topped with quartered hard-boiled eggs.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 4 andouillettes de Troyes (pork chitterling sausages, AAAAA quality)
150 ml dry white wine (Chablis or Champagne still wine)
2 tbsp Dijon or Chaource-style mustard sauce: 2 tbsp mustard plus 150 ml cream
steps: Prick the andouillettes lightly and score the skin.
Brown them in butter in a pan over medium heat for 15–20 minutes, turning, until heated through to the centre (or grill them).
Remove, soften the shallots in the pan, deglaze with the wine and reduce by half.
Stir in the mustard and cream and simmer until thick; season with pepper.
Serve the andouillettes with the sauce and frites or sautéed potatoes.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 300 g smoked bacon in one piece
1 onion stuck with cloves and 1 bouquet garni
steps: Put the pork shoulder and bacon in a large pot of cold water with onion, bouquet garni and peppercorns; bring to a simmer and skim.
Simmer 1 1/2 hours.
Add the cabbage, carrots, turnips and leeks and cook 30 minutes.
Add the sausage and potatoes for the final 30 minutes until all is tender.
Serve the meats sliced over vegetables with mustard; the Champagne version is often finished with a little smoked ham from the Ardennes.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

dishes.name: Pied de Cochon à la Sainte-Menehould

steps: Soak the trotters overnight, then tie each pair tightly in muslin or bandage to keep the shape.
Simmer very gently with the vegetables, spices, wine and water to cover for 4 hours until the bones are soft; cool in the liquid.
Unwrap, brush with mustard and melted butter and roll in breadcrumbs.
Grill or bake at 220 °C for 20 minutes, turning, until golden and crisp and hot through.
Serve with mustard and mashed potatoes; the softened small bones are traditionally eaten too.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 8 boudins blancs de Rethel (white pork sausages, no starch), sub: any good French boudin blanc
steps: Prick the boudins lightly so they don't burst.
Cook them in butter over medium-low heat for 12–15 minutes, turning, until golden and heated through.
Meanwhile caramelize the apple wedges in a pan with a little butter and the sugar for 8 minutes.
Serve the boudins with the apples, or with mashed potatoes moistened with cream.

ingredients: 1.5 kg cured pork shoulder (salted), soaked overnight
750 ml still white wine (Coteaux Champenois or dry white)
steps: Soak the shoulder overnight, then simmer gently in the wine and water with vegetables, herbs and peppercorns for 3 hours until very tender.
Lift out and flake the meat; reduce and strain the stock to about 400 ml.
Mix the meat with parsley and shallots, press into a mould, pour over the stock and chill 12 hours until set.
Unmould and roll the outside in breadcrumbs (the signature crust); slice and serve cold with mustard and bread.

ingredients: 125 g butter, melted and cooled, plus extra for the mould
steps: Whisk eggs and sugar 3 minutes until pale and thick.
Fold in flour, baking powder, salt, zest and vanilla, then the melted butter.
Cover and chill the batter at least 1 hour (this gives the signature hump).
Heat the oven to 220 °C; butter and flour a madeleine tray and fill each shell three-quarters full.
Bake 4 minutes, lower to 180 °C and bake 6–8 minutes more until humped and golden; unmould at once.

ingredients: 1 kg mirabelles de Lorraine (small golden plums), halved and stoned; sub: yellow plums
steps: Line a 28 cm tart tin with the pastry and sprinkle with ground almonds.
Arrange the mirabelles closely, cut-side up.
Bake at 200 °C for 20 minutes.
Whisk eggs, 50 g sugar, cream and eau-de-vie, pour over and bake 20 minutes more until set.
Sprinkle with the remaining sugar and serve lukewarm.

steps: Mix ground almonds and sugar, then add the unbeaten egg whites and vanilla and work into a soft, sticky paste.
Pipe or spoon walnut-sized mounds onto baking paper, spaced well.
Dampen the tops with a wet finger, dust with icing sugar to get the crackled surface.
Bake at 180 °C for 15–20 minutes until lightly golden and cracked; cool on the paper, then peel off (traditionally sold stuck to the paper).

steps: Melt chocolate and butter gently over a water bath.
Beat yolks with sugar until pale, then stir in the chocolate, almonds and flour.
Whisk whites with salt to firm peaks and fold in gently.
Bake in a buttered 24 cm tin at 170 °C for 25–30 minutes until just set with a moist centre.
Cool, unmould and dust with icing sugar; serve with custard (crème anglaise).

ingredients: 1/2 tsp natural bergamot essential oil (food grade) or 1 tsp bergamot extract
steps: Dissolve sugar, water and glucose in a heavy pan and boil without stirring to the hard-crack stage (150 °C).
Off the heat add the bergamot oil and lemon juice, swirling (take care, it steams).
Pour onto an oiled tray or marble and, when barely firm, mark into 2 cm squares with an oiled knife.
Cool completely, break into squares and store airtight; the translucent golden candies are a Nancy speciality.

ingredients: 1 tbsp gum arabic powder dissolved in 2 tbsp water
steps: Toast the almonds at 150 °C for 15 minutes and cool.
Boil the sugar and water to a syrup (110 °C) and add vanilla; keep warm.
Toss the almonds in a bowl with a little gum arabic, then add the syrup a spoonful at a time, tossing continuously and letting each layer dry with a fan or hair-dryer on cool.
Repeat 10–15 times until a smooth, thick white shell forms; tint the last layers if liked.
Dry overnight on a tray; serve at baptisms and weddings as Verdun has since the 13th century.

ingredients: a few drops of natural red food colouring (carmine or beet)
steps: Whisk the whites to soft peaks, add the sugar gradually, then the yolks, vanilla and colouring.
Fold in the sifted flour, cornflour and baking powder.
Pipe 8 cm fingers onto lined trays, dust generously with icing sugar twice and rest 10 minutes.
Bake at 160 °C for 12–15 minutes until firm and dry but still pink; cool and store airtight.
Dip them into a glass of Champagne in the Reims tradition.

ingredients: 1 bottle (750 ml) Champagne AOC (buy from licensed producers or merchants)
ice bucket with ice and water
Biscuits Roses de Reims to accompany
steps: Champagne is the sparkling wine of the Champagne region, made from Chardonnay, Pinot Noir and Pinot Meunier grapes by the traditional method; buy it from licensed producers.
Chill the bottle in an ice bucket for 20–30 minutes to 8–10 °C.
Remove the foil and cage, hold the cork and turn the bottle gently so it opens with a sigh rather than a pop.
Pour slowly in two stages into tulip glasses and serve as an apéritif or with oysters, gougères or biscuits roses.

ingredients: 1.2 kg beef chuck (paleron), cut in 5 cm chunks
750 ml Flemish brown ale or bière brune
2 slices pain d'épices (spiced gingerbread), spread with 2 tbsp Dijon mustard
2 tbsp brown sugar (cassonade) and 1 tbsp cider vinegar
1 tsp salt and 1/2 tsp black pepper
steps: Pat the beef dry, season with salt and pepper and brown it in batches in hot butter in a heavy casserole over high heat, 3-4 minutes per side; set aside.
Lower the heat to medium, add the onions and cook 15 minutes until soft and golden, then stir in the flour for 1 minute.
Return the beef, pour in the beer, add the brown sugar, vinegar, bay and thyme, and lay the mustard-spread pain d'épices on top, mustard side down.
Cover and simmer very gently, or bake at 160°C, for 2 1/2-3 hours, stirring occasionally, until the beef breaks with a spoon and the bread has melted into a glossy sauce.
Taste for sweet-sour balance and serve with frites or boiled potatoes and a glass of the same beer.

ingredients: 2 thick slices country bread (pain de campagne)
250 ml blonde beer or bière de garde
steps: Heat the oven grill to high; toast the bread lightly, place each slice in an individual gratin dish, drizzle with 2 tbsp beer, spread with mustard and top with a slice of ham.
Melt the Cheddar in a saucepan over low heat with the remaining beer, stirring constantly, until smooth and creamy, about 5 minutes; season with pepper.
Pour the cheese over the bread to cover it completely and grill for 5-7 minutes until bubbling and spotted brown.
Top each with a fried egg if you like and serve at once with frites and a green salad.

ingredients: 500 g skinless chicken thighs, boned and cut in pieces
500 g rabbit, boned and cut in pieces
500 g pork shoulder, cut in pieces
500 g veal shoulder, cut in pieces
3 onions, thinly sliced, and 3 garlic cloves, sliced
400 ml dry white wine and 100 ml white wine vinegar
4 sheets gelatine (or 2 pig's trotters for a traditional set)
2 bay leaves, 6 sprigs thyme, 10 juniper berries
1 1/2 tsp salt and 1 tsp black pepper
steps: Mix the meats with onion, garlic, herbs, juniper, salt, pepper, wine and vinegar, cover and marinate in the fridge overnight (8 hours).
Soak the gelatine in cold water for 5 minutes, squeeze, and layer the meats in a terrine dish, tucking the gelatine between layers; pour the marinade over.
Cover tightly with a lid or foil and bake at 150°C for 3 hours, until the meat is meltingly tender and the juices run clear.
Cool, then chill for at least 12 hours until the juices set into a clear jelly.
Slice cold and serve with hot frites, cornichons and a green salad.

ingredients: 2 kg live mussels (moules de bouchot), scrubbed and debearded
1 large onion or 3 shallots, finely chopped
200 ml dry white wine or blonde beer
1.2 kg floury potatoes (Bintje), cut in 1 cm batons
2 litres beef dripping (blanc de boeuf) or neutral oil, for frying
steps: Discard any mussels that are broken or do not close when tapped; keep the rest cold.
Fry the potatoes in dripping at 150°C for 6-7 minutes until soft but pale, drain, then fry again at 180°C for 2-3 minutes until crisp and golden; salt them.
Meanwhile melt the butter in a large pot over medium heat and soften the onion and celery for 5 minutes.
Add the mussels and wine, cover and cook over high heat for 5-6 minutes, shaking the pot, until all shells are open; discard any that stay closed.
Season with pepper, scatter with parsley and serve in the pot alongside the frites and mayonnaise.

ingredients: 600 g pork belly in one piece
4 carrots, 2 leeks and 2 turnips, cut in large pieces
steps: Put the meats in a large pot, cover with cold water, bring to the boil and skim the scum for 10 minutes.
Add the clove-studded onion, bouquet garni, salt and peppercorns and simmer gently for 2 hours.
Blanch the cabbage quarters in boiling water for 5 minutes, drain, then add them to the pot with the carrots, leeks and turnips and simmer 45 minutes more.
Add the potatoes and cook 25 minutes until tender and the meats are very soft.
Serve the broth first, then the sliced meats and vegetables with coarse salt, mustard and cornichons.

ingredients: 500 ml blonde beer or bière de garde
2 sprigs thyme, 1 bay leaf, 1 tsp salt, 1/2 tsp pepper
steps: Season the chicken and brown it in butter in a casserole over medium-high heat, 8-10 minutes, until golden; flame with the genièvre if using and remove.
Fry the lardons and shallots in the same pot for 5 minutes, add the mushrooms for 5 minutes, then sprinkle with flour and stir 1 minute.
Return the chicken, pour in the beer, add thyme and bay, cover and simmer gently for 50-60 minutes until the thigh juices run clear (75°C inside).
Stir in the crème fraîche and simmer uncovered 5 minutes to thicken; adjust seasoning.
Serve with buttered tagliatelle or steamed potatoes.

ingredients: 1 tbsp cider vinegar and 1 tbsp brown sugar
2 sprigs thyme, 1 bay leaf, 1 tsp salt, 1/2 tsp pepper
steps: Marinate the rabbit with the beer, half the onion, thyme and bay in the fridge overnight; soak the prunes and raisins in warm water for 1 hour.
Drain the rabbit, keeping the marinade, pat dry and brown in butter over medium-high heat for 8 minutes; add the remaining onion and cook 5 minutes.
Sprinkle with flour, stir, then pour in the strained marinade, vinegar and sugar, season, cover and simmer gently for 50 minutes.
Add the drained prunes and raisins and cook 20 minutes more until the rabbit is tender and the sauce glossy.
Serve with steamed potatoes or crusty bread.

ingredients: 40 g butter and 40 g plain flour, for béchamel
1 pinch nutmeg, 1 tsp salt, 1/2 tsp white pepper
steps: Braise the endives in 30 g butter with the sugar and a pinch of salt, covered, over low heat for 25 minutes until tender, then drain well and squeeze out excess water.
Make a béchamel: melt 40 g butter, stir in the flour for 1 minute, whisk in the milk and simmer 5 minutes until thick; season with nutmeg, salt, pepper and half the cheese.
Heat the oven to 200°C; roll each endive in a slice of ham and lay them in a buttered gratin dish.
Pour the béchamel over, scatter with the rest of the cheese and bake 20-25 minutes until bubbling and golden.
Serve hot with boiled or mashed potatoes.

ingredients: 125 g plain flour, 2 eggs and 250 ml milk, for crêpes
20 g butter, plus extra for the pan
1 tsp salt, 1/2 tsp pepper, 1 pinch nutmeg
steps: Whisk the flour, eggs, milk and a pinch of salt into a smooth batter, rest 15 minutes, then cook 4 thin crêpes in a buttered pan over medium heat, 1 minute per side.
Sauté the shallots in butter for 3 minutes, add the mushrooms and cook 8-10 minutes until their liquid evaporates; stir in 100 ml crème fraîche and season.
Lay a slice of ham on each crêpe, spread with the mushroom duxelles and roll up; place in a buttered gratin dish.
Season the remaining crème fraîche with salt, pepper and nutmeg, pour over, scatter with Gruyère and bake at 200°C for 15-20 minutes until golden and bubbling.
Serve hot as a main with a green salad.

ingredients: 2 duck breasts (magrets), skinned, cut in strips
400 g duck leg meat or pork shoulder, minced
1 tsp quatre-épices, 2 tsp salt, 1 tsp pepper
500 g shortcrust or puff pastry (pâte brisée)
steps: Marinate the duck strips with the Calvados, shallots, spices, salt and pepper in the fridge overnight.
Mix the minced meats with the marinade liquid to make the farce, keeping the duck strips separate.

Line a buttered raised pie mould with two-thirds of the pastry, fill with alternating layers of farce and duck strips, cover with the remaining pastry, seal the edges and cut a chimney hole; brush with egg yolk.
Bake at 200°C for 20 minutes, then at 170°C for about 1 1/2 hours until the filling reaches 72°C in the centre.
Cool completely and chill overnight; serve sliced cold with cornichons and salad.

ingredients: 500 ml whole milk, for soaking (optional, to soften the salt)
1 tsp coriander seeds, 1 bay leaf, 1 sprig thyme
1 tbsp cider vinegar and 1 tbsp chopped chives
steps: Soak the herring fillets in milk for 1 hour if they are very salty, then drain and pat dry.
Layer them in a glass dish with the carrots, onion rings, coriander, bay and thyme, cover completely with oil and refrigerate for at least 24 hours.
Boil the potatoes in salted water for 18-20 minutes until a knife slips in easily; peel while warm.
Slice the potatoes, dress with the vinegar, 3 tbsp of the herring oil and chives.
Serve the herring and its carrots and onions on the warm potato salad.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 300 g puff pastry or pâte brisée (2 sheets)
1 kg leeks, white and pale green, sliced
steps: Sweat the leeks in butter with a pinch of salt, covered, over low heat for 20-25 minutes until very soft but not coloured; cool slightly.
Whisk the eggs with the crème fraîche, nutmeg, salt and pepper, and stir in the leeks.
Line a 26 cm tart tin with one sheet of pastry, pour in the filling, cover with the second sheet, seal the edges, cut a small vent and brush with egg yolk.
Bake at 200°C for 35 minutes until deep golden and the filling is set.
Rest 10 minutes and serve warm with a green salad.

ingredients: 7 g dried yeast and 150 ml warm milk
30 g soft butter and 1/2 tsp salt
1 Maroilles cheese (about 400 g), rind lightly scraped, sliced (substitute: Livarot or Époisses)
steps: Dissolve the yeast in the warm milk, then knead with the flour, butter and salt for 8 minutes into a soft dough; cover and leave to rise for 1 hour.
Roll the dough out to line a buttered 28 cm tart tin and leave to rise 15 minutes more.
Heat the oven to 220°C; spread the crème fraîche over the dough, arrange the Maroilles slices on top and grind over plenty of pepper.
Bake 20-25 minutes until the crust is golden and the cheese is melted and bubbling.
Serve hot with a green salad and a blonde beer.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

steps: Melt the butter in a heavy pot over medium heat and soften the onion for 5 minutes.
Add the cabbage, apples, sugar, vinegar, cloves, bay, salt and pepper and stir well to coat.
Cover and cook very gently for 1 1/2 hours, stirring now and then and adding a splash of water if it catches, until soft and glossy.
Adjust the sweet-sour balance with more sugar or vinegar and serve with pork, sausages or game.

ingredients: 80 g caster sugar and 1 tsp salt
200 g raisins, soaked in warm water 30 minutes
steps: Dissolve the yeast in the warm milk, then mix with the flour, sugar, salt and eggs and knead 10 minutes until elastic.
Work in the soft butter a piece at a time until smooth and shiny, then knead in the drained raisins.
Cover and leave to rise 1 1/2 hours until doubled; shape into a loaf, place in a buttered loaf tin and rise 45 minutes more.
Brush with egg yolk, scatter with pearl sugar and bake at 180°C for 30-35 minutes until deep golden and hollow-sounding underneath.
Cool on a rack and serve sliced with butter for breakfast.

ingredients: 10 g dried yeast and 100 ml warm milk
50 g caster sugar and 1 pinch salt
150 g vergeoise brune (Flemish soft brown beet sugar; substitute dark muscovado)
100 g soft butter, for the filling
1 tsp vanilla extract or 1 tbsp rum
steps: Dissolve the yeast in the milk, mix with flour, eggs, sugar, salt and 150 g butter, knead into a soft dough and leave to rise 1 hour.
Divide into walnut-sized balls, flatten each and cook in a hot thin-waffle iron (gaufrier) for 1-2 minutes until golden; split each waffle in half horizontally while still hot.
Beat the vergeoise with 100 g butter and the vanilla or rum until creamy.
Spread the filling on one half and close with the other; press lightly and leave to set before serving.

ingredients: 7 g dried yeast and 80 ml warm milk
2 eggs, 1 for the dough and 1 for the topping
60 g soft butter, plus 40 g in small pieces
30 g caster sugar and 1 pinch salt
150 g vergeoise blonde or brune (substitute light muscovado)
steps: Dissolve the yeast in the milk, then knead with flour, 1 egg, 60 g butter, sugar and salt for 8 minutes; cover and rise 1 hour.
Roll out to line a buttered 28 cm tart tin, leaving the dough fairly thick, and rise 20 minutes more.
Scatter the vergeoise evenly over the dough and dot with the butter pieces; whisk the second egg with the crème fraîche and spoon it over.
Bake at 190°C for 20-25 minutes until the edges are golden and the sugar has formed a soft caramel; serve warm or cool.

ingredients: 150 g caster sugar (half fine, half icing sugar)
150 g dark chocolate, finely shaved into curls
steps: Whisk the egg whites to soft peaks, then add the caster sugar gradually until stiff and glossy; fold in the icing sugar.
Pipe 12 discs of 6 cm onto a lined tray and bake at 100°C for 1 1/2-2 hours until dry and crisp; cool completely.
Whip the cream with icing sugar and vanilla to firm peaks.
Sandwich pairs of meringues with whipped cream, then coat the outsides in cream and roll in the chocolate shavings.
Chill 1 hour and eat the same day.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 10 g dried yeast and 30 ml warm milk
60 g caster sugar and 1 tsp salt
1 tsp vanilla extract or zest of 1 lemon
steps: Dissolve the yeast in the milk, then mix with the flour, yolks, whole egg, sugar, salt and vanilla.
Beat the dough vigorously by hand or with a stand mixer for 15 minutes ("battu" means beaten) until very elastic, then beat in the butter until smooth.
Pour into a buttered fluted cylindrical mould, filling it one-third, cover and leave to rise in a warm place for 2-3 hours until it reaches the rim.
Bake at 180°C for 30-35 minutes until deep golden; a skewer should come out dry.
Unmould onto a rack and serve with coffee or with fresh fruit and cream.

steps: Mix the almonds, sugar, honey, jam, extract and egg white into a firm, slightly sticky paste; chill 1 hour.
Roll into a 4 cm log, wrap and chill again, then cut into 1.5 cm slices and place on a lined tray.
Brush with egg yolk and bake at 180°C for 12-15 minutes until golden on top but still soft inside.
Cool completely; they keep a week in an airtight tin.

ingredients: 1 tsp neutral oil, for the slab
steps: Heat the sugar, glucose and water in a heavy pan, stirring until dissolved, then boil without stirring to 150°C (hard-crack stage) on a sugar thermometer.

Pour onto an oiled marble slab or silicone mat, add the peppermint and colour, and when cool enough to handle (wear food-safe gloves) fold and pull the sugar repeatedly until it turns satiny and opaque.
Pull a thin strip of the sugar aside, twist it along the top of the main rope to make the characteristic yellow stripe.
Snip the rope into 2-3 cm pillows with oiled scissors before it hardens, cool completely and store airtight.

ingredients: 1/2 tsp each ground ginger, cloves and nutmeg
1/2 tsp baking soda and 1 pinch salt
steps: Cream the butter and vergeoise, add the milk, then work in the flour, spices, baking soda and salt to a firm dough.
Wrap and rest in the fridge overnight so the spices develop.
Roll to 4 mm (or press into floured carved wooden spéculoos moulds), cut into rectangles and place on a lined tray.
Bake at 180°C for 12-15 minutes until deep golden-brown and fragrant; cool on a rack to crisp.
Serve with coffee or crush to use in desserts.

ingredients: 40 ml genièvre (juniper spirit of the Nord, e.g. from Houlle, Wambrechies or Loos), bought from a licensed distillery
1 small cup black coffee (optional, for a bistouille)
steps: Genièvre is a grain spirit flavoured with juniper berries, the ancestor of gin, made in the Flanders and Artois distilleries; buy it from licensed producers.
Serve it well chilled in a small tulip glass as a digestif, or add a dash to a hot black coffee to make a bistouille, the traditional miners' and market-goers' drink of the Nord.

ingredients: 330 ml bière de garde (e.g. Jenlain, Ch'ti, Trois Monts), bought from a licensed brewery
50 g Mimolette or Maroilles cheese, to accompany (optional)
steps: Bière de garde is the amber, malty "keeping beer" of French Flanders and Hainaut, once brewed by farms in winter and stored for drinking in summer; buy it from licensed brewers.
Serve lightly cool (8-10°C) in a stemmed glass, poured slowly to leave a fine head.
It pairs naturally with carbonade, welsh, Maroilles and other dishes of the Nord, and is also used as a cooking liquid in them.

ingredients: 2 kg live mussels (moules de bouchot), scrubbed and debearded
steps: Discard any mussels that are broken or stay open when tapped.
Soften the shallots (and mushrooms, if using) in butter in a large pot over medium heat for 5 minutes.
Add the mussels and cider, cover and cook over high heat 5-6 minutes, shaking the pot, until all are open; discard any that stay closed.
Lift the mussels into bowls, boil the juices 2 minutes, stir in the crème fraîche and pepper and bubble 1 minute.
Pour the sauce over the mussels, scatter with parsley and serve with frites or crusty bread.

dishes.name: Tripes à la Mode de Caen

ingredients: 2 kg cleaned, blanched beef tripe (all four stomachs if possible), cut in 5 cm squares
4 carrots, sliced, and 4 onions, each studded with 2 cloves
200 g beef fat (graisse de rognon), sliced (optional)
250 g flour mixed with water to a paste, to seal the lid
steps: Lay the foot in a heavy earthenware tripière or casserole, then layer the tripe with the vegetables, bouquet garni, salt and pepper, ending with the beef fat.
Pour in the cider and Calvados and add water to just cover.
Put the lid on and seal it with the flour paste so no steam escapes.
Bake at 120°C for 10 hours, until the tripe is meltingly soft and the sauce gelatinous.
Break the seal, discard the bones and bouquet, skim off fat and serve piping hot on warmed plates with steamed potatoes and a glass of cider.

ingredients: 4 sole fillets (about 150 g each), or 2 whole soles filleted
300 g live mussels and 12 peeled raw prawns
200 ml dry cider or white wine, plus 200 ml fish stock
200 ml crème fraîche and 2 egg yolks
steps: Steam open the mussels with half the cider in a covered pan for 4 minutes, shell them and strain the juices.

Fold the sole fillets, lay them in a buttered dish on the shallots, add the remaining cider, the stock and mussel juices, cover and poach at 180°C for 10-12 minutes until opaque and flaking; keep warm and reserve the liquid.
Sauté the mushrooms in 20 g butter for 5 minutes and cook the prawns in the same pan 2-3 minutes until pink.
Make a roux with 40 g butter and the flour, whisk in the poaching liquid and simmer 5 minutes; off the heat whisk in the cream and yolks, then reheat gently without boiling until it coats a spoon.
Arrange the sole with mussels, prawns and mushrooms, nap with the sauce and serve with steamed potatoes.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 1 free-range chicken (about 1.6 kg), cut in 8 pieces
2 tart apples, cut in wedges and fried in butter, to garnish
steps: Season the chicken and brown it in half the butter in a sauté pan over medium-high heat for 10 minutes until golden.
Warm the Calvados, pour it over and flame carefully, standing back; when the flames die add the shallots and cider.
Cover and simmer gently 35-40 minutes until the juices run clear (75°C at the thigh).
Meanwhile sauté the mushrooms in the remaining butter 6 minutes; add them and the crème fraîche to the chicken and simmer uncovered 5 minutes until the sauce coats a spoon.
Serve with the buttered apple wedges and rice or steamed potatoes.

ingredients: 1 Rouen duck (or Barbary duck, about 2 kg), with its liver
200 ml good red wine (Bordeaux or Burgundy)
200 ml rich duck or veal stock
1 tsp salt and 1/2 tsp black pepper
steps: Season the duck inside and out and roast at 220°C for 25-30 minutes so the breast is pink; rest 10 minutes.
Meanwhile boil the shallots in the red wine until reduced by two-thirds, add the stock and reduce by half.
Remove the legs and return them to the oven 15 minutes more until cooked through; carve the breasts into fine slices.
Push the raw liver through a sieve, whisk into the hot sauce with the Cognac and butter over low heat and let it simmer for 2 minutes until the liver is cooked and the sauce thickens.
Serve the breast slices with the sauce and the crisp legs, with soufflé or sautéed potatoes.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

dishes.name: Escalope de Veau à la Normande

ingredients: 4 veal escalopes (about 150 g each), beaten thin
steps: Season the escalopes, dust lightly with flour and fry in butter over medium-high heat 2-3 minutes per side until golden and cooked through; keep warm.
Sauté the mushrooms in the same pan 5 minutes until browned.
Pour in the Calvados and flame carefully, then stir in the crème fraîche and simmer 3 minutes to a coating sauce.
Return the veal and its juices to the pan for 1 minute and serve with rice or sautéed apples.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 1 leg of salt-marsh lamb (agneau de pré-salé from Mont-Saint-Michel bay, about 2 kg; substitute any good leg of lamb)
1 kg flageolet beans or waxy potatoes, cooked, to serve
2 tsp coarse sea salt and 1 tsp pepper
steps: Bring the lamb to room temperature for 1 hour; make small incisions and push in the garlic slivers.
Rub with butter, salt, pepper and herbs and roast at 220°C for 15 minutes, then at 180°C for 45-55 minutes for pink meat (60°C inside).
Rest the gigot loosely covered for 15 minutes; deglaze the roasting pan with the water, scraping up the juices, and simmer 3 minutes.
Carve and serve with the jus and flageolets or potatoes; the lamb's naturally salty, herby flavour needs little else.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 800 g firm white fish fillets (sole, turbot, monkfish, brill), cut in large pieces
2 leeks (white part) and 2 shallots, finely chopped
250 ml dry cider and 500 ml fish stock
1 tsp salt, 1/2 tsp pepper, chopped parsley
steps: Steam the mussels open with half the cider in a covered pot, 5 minutes; shell them, discard any closed ones and strain the juice.
Soften the leeks and shallots in butter 8 minutes, add mushrooms for 5 minutes, then pour in the rest of the cider, the stock and the mussel juices and simmer 10 minutes.
Add the fish and simmer very gently 5 minutes, then the scallops and prawns for 2-3 minutes until just opaque and cooked through.
Stir in the crème fraîche and mussels, warm through without boiling and season.

ingredients: 1 kg pork shoulder, cut into 5 cm cubes

steps: Melt the lard in a heavy cast-iron pot over low heat, add all the pork, salt, pepper, bay and thyme, and let the meat colour lightly for 15 minutes, stirring now and then; Tours rillettes are browned a little, which gives them their darker colour.

ingredients: 500 g dried mogettes (Vendée white beans; substitute cannellini or lingot beans)
6 thick slices jambon de Vendée (dry-cured ham; substitute prosciutto or Bayonne ham)
steps: Soak the beans overnight in plenty of cold water, then drain.
Cover with fresh water, add the clove-studded onion, carrot, bouquet garni and 2 garlic cloves, bring to a boil, then simmer gently for 1 hour 30 minutes, salting only in the last 20 minutes.
Drain the beans, keeping a little liquid, and stir in half the butter until glossy.
Fry the ham slices quickly in the remaining butter for 1 minute per side and toast the bread, rubbing it with the last garlic clove.
Serve the mogettes on or beside the buttered toast with the ham on top, as a Vendée Sunday lunch.
