ingredients: 1 kg pig's offal (lungs, heart, spleen), cleaned and cut into small dice
300 g pork head meat or cheek, diced
300 ml pork blood (from the butcher) or omit and thicken with 2 tbsp flour
steps: Blanch the offal and head meat in boiling water for 5 minutes, drain and rinse.
Put the meats, onions, garlic, wine, bouquet garni, spices, salt and pepper into a heavy pot, bring to a simmer and cook covered on low heat for 2 hours 30 minutes, stirring often.

Take off the heat and whisk in the blood a little at a time (or the flour slaked in a little cold wine), then return to a very low heat for 10 minutes, stirring constantly, until thick and dark; do not boil.
Serve hot with boiled potatoes, as a traditional pig-killing day stew of the Vendée, or cold sliced the next day.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

dishes.name: Galette aux Pommes de Terre du Berry

ingredients: 500 g floury potatoes, boiled in their skins
1 egg yolk beaten with 1 tbsp milk, for glazing
steps: Peel the potatoes while still warm and mash or pass them through a ricer.
Rub the butter into the flour, baking powder, salt and pepper, then knead in the potatoes to form a soft dough.
Roll to a 3 cm thick round, fold in three, roll again and repeat twice like puff pastry; finally shape into a 3 cm thick disc.
Place on a lined tray, brush with egg yolk and score a lattice with a knife.
Bake at 200°C for 35 to 40 minutes until golden and puffed; serve warm with a green salad or alongside roasts.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 10 g fresh yeast or 5 g dried yeast
steps: Dissolve the yeast in the warm water, add to the flour and salt and knead for 10 minutes into a smooth, supple dough.
Cover and leave to rise in a warm place for 1 hour 30 minutes until doubled.
Knock back, divide into 12 balls, rest 15 minutes, then roll each into a 12 cm disc about 4 mm thick.
Bake on a very hot stone or tray at 260°C for 3 to 5 minutes until puffed like a balloon and lightly spotted.
Split open while hot and fill with salted butter, mogettes or goat cheese, as in the troglodyte restaurants of the Saumur area.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 400 g bread dough (flour, water, yeast, salt) or 1 baguette-sized dough
6 garlic cloves, crushed to a paste
steps: Shape the risen dough into a long flat loaf and leave to rise for 45 minutes.
Bake at 230°C for 15 minutes until just set but pale, then cool slightly.
Mash the butter with the garlic, parsley and salt.
Slice the loaf along its length, spread generously with the garlic butter, close and bake again for 5 minutes until the butter melts in.
Cut into fingers and serve warm with an aperitif, as in the Vendée.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 1.2 kg firm apples (Reine des Reinettes, Golden or Pink Lady), peeled, cored and halved
250 g pâte brisée or puff pastry
steps: In a 26 cm ovenproof pan, cook the sugar over medium heat without stirring until amber, then whisk in the butter.
Pack the apple halves upright, tightly, rounded side down, into the caramel, add the vanilla and cook on the hob for 20 minutes until the apples soften and the caramel darkens.
Roll the pastry 3 mm thick, drape it over the apples and tuck the edges down inside the pan; prick a few holes.
Bake at 200°C for 30 minutes until the pastry is golden and crisp.
Rest 10 minutes, then invert onto a plate in one swift move and serve warm with crème fraîche, as the Tatin sisters did in Lamotte-Beuvron.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

steps: Cream the butter and sugar, beat in the eggs one at a time, then fold in the almonds, flour and rum to make frangipane; chill 30 minutes.
Roll the pastry into two 26 cm rounds, one slightly thicker; place the thinner on a lined tray.
Spread the frangipane in a dome leaving a 3 cm border, wet the border, cover with the second round and seal, scalloping the edge.
Glaze with yolk, score curved rays from the centre outwards without cutting through, and chill 20 minutes.
Bake at 200°C for 35 to 40 minutes, dust with icing sugar for the last 3 minutes to glaze, and serve warm or at room temperature.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 150 g mixed candied fruit (glacé fruit), diced
steps: Line a 24 cm tart tin with the pastry, prick it and chill for 15 minutes.
Spread the apricot jam over the base and scatter the candied fruit evenly.
Whisk the egg whites to firm peaks, then gently fold in the ground almonds and caster sugar to make a macaron-like batter.
Spread the almond mixture over the fruit, smooth and dust heavily with icing sugar.
Bake at 170°C for 40 to 45 minutes until crisp and pale gold on top; cool completely before slicing.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

steps: Cream the butter and sugar until pale, add the almonds, then beat in the eggs one at a time.
Fold in the flour and 2 tbsp rum, and pour into a buttered 22 cm round tin.
Bake at 180°C for 35 to 40 minutes until golden and a skewer comes out clean.
While warm, brush with 1 tbsp rum; once cool, mix the icing sugar with the last tbsp of rum to a thin glaze and pour over the top.
Leave the icing to set before slicing; it keeps well for several days, a legacy of the Nantes rum and sugar trade.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 15 g fresh yeast or 7 g dried yeast
steps: Dissolve the yeast in the milk, then mix with the flour, sugar, salt, eggs, orange-blossom water and rum; knead 10 minutes.
Work in the butter a little at a time until the dough is smooth and elastic, then cover and leave to rise 2 hours.
Knock back, divide into three and roll into ropes, then braid into a long plait.
Prove on a lined tray for 1 hour 30 minutes until well risen, then brush with yolk.
Bake at 170°C for 30 to 35 minutes until deep golden and hollow-sounding; it is the traditional wedding and Easter brioche of the Vendée.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 1/2 tsp natural flavouring (mint, lemon or raspberry)
1 tsp neutral oil for the slab
steps: Heat the sugar, water and glucose in a heavy pan, stirring until dissolved, then boil without stirring to 150°C (hard crack) on a sugar thermometer.
Remove from the heat, add the lemon juice and flavouring, and pour onto an oiled marble slab or silicone mat.
Divide the mass, colour one part, and when cool enough to handle with gloves, pull the plain part until it turns satiny and opaque.
Lay coloured strips on the pulled sugar, roll into a long rope and cut with oiled scissors, turning the rope a quarter turn between cuts to make the classic tetrahedron shapes.
Cool completely and store airtight in a tin.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 150 g chopped almonds or hazelnuts, toasted
steps: Cook the sugar and glucose to a deep blond caramel, then stir in the butter and nuts and mix well.
Pour onto a baking mat, cover with a second mat and roll quickly to 5 mm thick nougatine.
While still warm, cut into small 2 cm squares with an oiled knife and let harden.
Melt the white chocolate gently to 45°C, cool to 28°C while stirring, tint with blue colouring until slate-blue, and warm back to 29°C.
Dip each square in the chocolate, set on parchment and leave to harden; they mimic the slate roofs of Angers.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 1.5 kg ripe quinces, washed and cut into pieces (keep skins and cores)
steps: Simmer the quinces with skins and cores in the water for 1 hour until very soft.
Strain through a jelly bag without pressing, measure the clear juice and add 750 g sugar per litre of juice.
Boil with the lemon juice, skimming, until it reaches 105°C and a drop sets on a cold plate.
Add colour if you like, then pour into small round shallow wooden boxes or moulds and leave to set for 24 hours.
Serve as a translucent jelly sweet, eaten straight from its box with a small spoon, as in Orléans since the Middle Ages.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

steps: Mix the almonds and sugar, then work in the unwhipped egg whites and vanilla to a thick, sticky paste.
Pipe or spoon into small rings (the traditional Cormery shape has a hole in the centre, like a navel) on a lined tray.
Dust with icing sugar and leave to dry for 15 minutes.
Bake at 170°C for 18 to 20 minutes until pale gold and crackled; cool on the tray before lifting off.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

steps: Cointreau is a clear triple-sec orange liqueur created in Angers in 1875 from sweet and bitter orange peels; it is made commercially and should be bought, not made at home.
Serve it neat or over ice in a small tumbler with a slice of orange as a digestif, or use it in cocktails and to flavour crêpes, soufflés and fruit salads.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 3 green peppers (piment doux des Landes or Anglet peppers; substitute green bell peppers), sliced
800 g ripe tomatoes, peeled and chopped
1 tsp piment d'Espelette (substitute mild chilli flakes)
4 eggs, beaten (optional, for the scrambled version)
steps: Warm the olive oil in a wide pan over medium heat and soften the onions for 10 minutes without browning.
Add the peppers and garlic and cook 10 minutes more until soft.
Add the tomatoes, salt and piment d'Espelette and simmer uncovered for 15 minutes until thick and jammy.
If using eggs, pour them in and stir gently over low heat for 2 to 3 minutes until just creamy and set.
Serve hot with crusty bread as a side, or with eggs as a light meal.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 800 g veal shoulder, finely diced by hand (or coarsely minced)
4 green peppers (Espelette or Anglet; substitute green bell peppers), diced
steps: Heat the oil in a casserole over medium-high heat and brown the veal for 6 to 8 minutes, then remove.
In the same pot soften the onions, peppers and garlic for 10 minutes over medium heat.
Return the meat, add the piment d'Espelette, salt and stock, cover and simmer gently for 40 minutes until the veal is tender and the sauce reduced.
Serve hot with boiled potatoes or rice; it is the market-day dish of Espelette.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 1 chicken, about 1.6 kg, jointed into 8 pieces
2 green peppers and 2 red peppers, sliced
4 slices jambon de Bayonne (substitute prosciutto), cut into strips
600 g ripe tomatoes, peeled and chopped
steps: Season the chicken with salt and brown it in the olive oil in a casserole over medium-high heat for 10 minutes; set aside.
Add the ham, onions, peppers and garlic and cook gently for 10 minutes until softened.
Deglaze with the wine, add the tomatoes and piment d'Espelette, then return the chicken.
Cover and simmer for 35 to 40 minutes until the chicken is cooked through (thigh juices clear, 75°C).
Serve with rice or boiled potatoes.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 1 kg small squid (chipirons), cleaned, tentacles and ink sacs reserved
2 sachets (8 g) squid ink, if the ink sacs are few
steps: Sear the squid bodies and tentacles in hot olive oil for 2 minutes, then remove.
In the same pan soften the onions, garlic and pepper for 10 minutes over medium heat, then add the tomatoes and cook 5 minutes.
Crush the ink sacs into the wine with the bought ink, pour into the pan and add the piment d'Espelette and salt.
Return the squid and simmer gently, covered, for 25 minutes until tender and the sauce is glossy and black.
Serve with white rice, as in Saint-Jean-de-Luz.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 2 m natural casings, soaked and rinsed
500 ml fresh lamb or pork blood (from the butcher), kept cold
300 g lamb tripe and offal, cooked and finely chopped
steps: Soften the onions in the fat over low heat for 15 minutes until very tender; cool slightly.
Mix the onions, chopped offal, spices, salt and pepper into the cold blood.
Fill the casings loosely using a funnel and tie off into 15 cm links.
Poach in water held at 80°C for 30 to 40 minutes, pricking any that float, until a pricked sausage releases no blood.
Drain and serve hot, sliced and pan-fried, with piperade, as a Basque festival dish.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 200 g stale bread soaked in 100 ml milk, squeezed
the hen's liver and gizzard, chopped
3 garlic cloves and 2 tbsp parsley, chopped
4 carrots, 3 leeks, 3 turnips and 1 celery stick
steps: Mix the bread, ham, liver, gizzard, eggs, garlic, parsley and a pinch of salt and pepper, stuff into the hen and sew it closed.
Put the hen in a large pot, cover with cold water, add the onion, bouquet garni, salt and peppercorns and bring slowly to a simmer, skimming.
Simmer very gently for 2 hours, then add the carrots, leeks, turnips and celery and cook 45 minutes more until the hen is very tender and the stuffing reaches 75°C.
Serve the broth first with toasted bread, then the sliced hen, stuffing and vegetables with coarse salt and cornichons, in the tradition of Henri IV of Béarn.

ingredients: 1.5 kg mixed fish (hake, monkfish, gurnard, conger), cleaned and cut into pieces, heads and bones reserved
steps: Make a stock: soften the onions, leek and carrot in 2 tbsp oil, add the fish heads and bones, tomatoes, wine and 1.5 litres water, simmer 30 minutes and strain, pressing well.
Season the fish pieces with salt, dust lightly with flour and fry in the remaining oil with the garlic for 2 minutes per side.
Arrange the fish in a wide pot, add the mussels and langoustines, pour over the hot stock and add the piment d'Espelette.
Simmer gently for 8 to 10 minutes until the fish flakes and the mussels open (discard any that stay shut).
Serve in deep bowls over slices of garlic-rubbed toast, as the fishermen of Saint-Jean-de-Luz do.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 600 g fresh albacore or bonito tuna (thon germon), cut into 3 cm cubes
2 tbsp choricero pepper paste or 1 tsp piment d'Espelette
800 g potatoes, peeled and broken into chunks (cascadas)
steps: Soften the onion, peppers and garlic in the olive oil over medium heat for 10 minutes.
Add the pepper paste and tomatoes and cook 5 minutes, then add the potatoes and stir to coat.
Pour in the stock, add salt, and simmer 20 to 25 minutes until the potatoes are tender and release starch.
Season the tuna, add it off the heat, cover and leave 5 minutes so it just cooks through without drying.
Serve straight from the pot with bread.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 300 g dried white beans (haricots tarbais; substitute cannellini), soaked overnight
2 confit duck legs plus 2 tbsp of their fat
300 g ventrèche or unsmoked bacon, in one piece
1 ham bone or 200 g jambon de Bayonne heel
1 tsp salt and pepper to taste
steps: Put the drained beans, ventrèche, ham bone and bouquet garni into a large pot with 3 litres water and simmer 1 hour, skimming.
Soften the carrots, turnips, leeks and garlic in the duck fat for 10 minutes, then add to the pot with the potatoes and cabbage.
Simmer 1 hour 30 minutes more, then add the confit legs for the last 20 minutes to heat through.
Season, remove the meats, slice them and return to the soup, which should be thick enough for a ladle to stand in.
Serve over slices of country bread; at the end, Béarnais tradition is to add a splash of red wine to the last of the broth in the bowl (faire chabrot).
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 300 g jambon de Bayonne IGP (dry-cured ham, bought whole slice or from the bone; substitute prosciutto di Parma)
200 g black cherry jam (confiture de cerises d'Itxassou)
steps: Jambon de Bayonne is a salt-cured, air-dried ham from the Adour basin, rubbed with Salies-de-Béarn salt and sometimes piment d'Espelette and aged at least 9 months; buy it from a charcutier rather than making it at home.
Slice it very thinly by hand or machine just before serving and let it come to room temperature for 15 minutes so the fat turns translucent.
Arrange on a board with slices of Ossau-Iraty, cherry jam, buttered bread and a pinch of piment d'Espelette, and serve as an aperitif.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 1 m thin natural sheep casings, soaked
steps: Mix the pork, fat, garlic, piment d'Espelette, salt and pepper thoroughly, cover and chill for 12 hours to let the flavours develop.
Stuff into the casings and twist into small links about 5 cm long.
Leave to dry in the fridge, uncovered, for 24 hours.
Fry or grill over medium heat for 10 to 12 minutes, turning, until browned and cooked through to 71°C.
Serve hot with an aperitif, traditionally with oysters in Bayonne at Christmas.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 250 g fine yellow cornmeal (masa harina or fine polenta flour)
1 tsp butter or sunflower oil for the pan
steps: Mix the cornmeal and salt, then gradually add warm water and knead to a soft dough that does not crack.
Divide into 6 balls and press each by hand or between sheets of baking paper into thin rounds about 15 cm across.
Cook on a hot, lightly greased cast-iron griddle over medium-high heat for 2 minutes per side until speckled and puffed.
Serve warm, folded around Ossau-Iraty cheese or eaten with piperade, as at Basque fairs.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 3 eggs (2 for the dough, 1 for the cream) plus 1 yolk for glazing
1 tbsp dark rum or 1 tsp vanilla
200 g black cherry jam (Itxassou; optional instead of cream)
steps: Make the pastry: cream the butter with 150 g sugar, beat in 2 eggs, then mix in the flour, almonds and baking powder; chill 1 hour.
Make the cream: whisk 1 egg, 50 g sugar and the cornflour, pour on hot milk, return to the pan and cook, whisking, for 2 minutes until thick; add rum and cool.
Line a buttered 24 cm tin with two-thirds of the dough, fill with pastry cream (or cherry jam), and cover with the remaining dough, sealing the edges.
Brush with yolk and score a lattice or the Basque cross (lauburu) with a fork.
Bake at 180°C for 40 to 45 minutes until deep golden; cool completely before slicing.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 1 tsp bitter almond extract or vanilla
steps: Mix the almonds and sugar, add the egg whites, honey and extract, and work into a firm, sticky paste.
Roll into walnut-sized balls with damp hands and flatten slightly on a tray lined with paper.
Leave to dry for 30 minutes so a skin forms.
Bake at 180°C for 15 to 18 minutes until pale gold, crackled on top and soft within; this is the recipe made famous by Maison Adam since 1660.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 4 duck legs (Moulard or Barbary), about 300 g each
steps: Rub the legs with the salt, pepper, garlic, thyme and bay, cover and refrigerate for 12 hours.
Rinse off the salt and pat the legs completely dry.

Melt the duck fat in a heavy casserole, submerge the legs fully and cook at a bare simmer (about 90°C) on the hob or in a 140°C oven for 2 hours 30 minutes to 3 hours, until the meat almost falls from the bone.
Store the legs covered in their fat in the fridge for up to 3 weeks, or use at once.
To serve, crisp the legs skin side down in a dry pan over medium heat for 10 minutes, then flip and heat through; serve with pommes sarladaises fried in some of the fat.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 100 ml red Bordeaux or Madiran wine
steps: Score the fat of each breast in a fine crisscross without cutting the meat, and season both sides.
Lay the breasts fat side down in a cold heavy pan, then cook over medium heat for 10 to 12 minutes, pouring off the fat as it renders, until the skin is deep golden and crisp.
Turn and cook the flesh side 3 to 4 minutes for pink (55°C in the centre), then rest on a warm plate for 8 minutes.
Pour off most of the fat, soften the shallots, add the wine, stock and honey and reduce by half; whisk in the cold butter.
Slice the magrets thinly on the diagonal and serve with the sauce and potatoes fried in duck fat.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 1 raw duck foie gras, about 500 g, extra grade, at room temperature
toasted brioche or pain de campagne and fleur de sel, to serve
steps: Gently separate the two lobes and, with the back of a small knife, remove the main veins, keeping the lobes as whole as possible.
Season all over with the salt, pepper and sugar, sprinkle with the Armagnac, and press firmly into a terrine; cover and marinate in the fridge for 12 hours.
Bring to room temperature, then cook in a bain-marie in a 100°C oven for 40 to 45 minutes until the core reaches 55 to 58°C.
Cool, place a weighted board on top, pour off excess fat (keep it to seal the top) and refrigerate for 48 hours before serving.
Slice with a hot knife and serve chilled with toasted brioche, fleur de sel and a glass of Sauternes or Jurançon.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 2 goose necks, skin removed whole like a sleeve (ask the butcher)
200 g goose or duck liver, diced
1 small black truffle, chopped (optional; substitute 2 tbsp truffle paste)
1 tsp salt, 1/2 tsp pepper and 1 pinch quatre-épices
steps: Pick any meat from the neck bones and mix it with the pork, liver, egg, truffle, Armagnac, salt, pepper and spice.
Sew one end of each neck skin closed, fill with the stuffing without packing too tightly, and sew the other end.
Melt the goose fat in a pot, add the necks and poach gently at about 90°C for 1 hour 45 minutes to 2 hours until the stuffing reaches 75°C.
Cool in the fat; serve sliced cold as a starter with a green salad and walnuts, or reheated and browned with sautéed potatoes.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 1.5 kg boned pork loin (échine or filet), with some fat
steps: Make slits all over the pork and push in the garlic slivers and thyme leaves, season inside and out, then roll and tie firmly with string.
Brown the roast in the fat in a casserole over medium-high heat for 10 minutes.
Add the water or wine and the trotter, cover and cook in a 160°C oven for 2 hours 15 minutes, basting occasionally, until the internal temperature reaches 70°C and the meat is very tender.
Serve hot with pommes sarladaises, or chill overnight in its jellied juices and serve cold in slices, as is traditional in Périgord.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 1 black Périgord truffle (Tuber melanosporum), about 20 g, brushed clean (substitute a little truffle butter)
steps: Put the whole eggs in an airtight jar with the truffle and refrigerate for 24 hours so the eggs absorb its aroma through their shells.
Grate or finely chop half of the truffle and slice the rest very thinly.
Beat the eggs lightly with the chopped truffle, salt and pepper.
Melt the butter in a pan over medium heat until foaming, pour in the eggs and stir gently with a fork for 1 to 2 minutes until just set but still soft (baveuse).
Fold onto a warm plate, top with the truffle slices and serve at once.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 60 g beef bone marrow, soaked and sliced (ask the butcher)
1 tsp fleur de sel and cracked pepper
steps: Simmer the shallots in the wine over medium heat until reduced by three quarters, add the stock and reduce by half.
Poach the marrow slices in simmering salted water for 2 minutes and drain.
Season the steak and sear in a very hot pan (or over vine-cutting embers, the Bordeaux way) for 3 to 4 minutes per side for medium-rare, then rest 5 minutes.
Whisk the cold butter into the sauce off the heat, add the marrow and parsley.
Slice the steak, spoon over the sauce and serve with frites or sautéed potatoes.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 1 river lamprey, about 1.5 kg, cleaned, blood reserved, cut into 5 cm pieces (ask the fishmonger; substitute eel)
1 tsp salt and pepper to taste
steps: Blanch the lamprey pieces briefly in boiling water and scrape off the slime from the skin.
Sweat the leeks, ham, shallots and garlic in duck fat for 15 minutes, sprinkle with the flour and stir 2 minutes.
Pour in the wine, add the bouquet garni, salt and pepper and simmer 1 hour.
Add the lamprey and simmer gently 1 hour 30 minutes until tender, then stir in the blood off the heat and warm gently without boiling until the sauce thickens.
Serve hot with garlic croutons and leeks; it tastes even better reheated the next day.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 2 kg mussels (moules de bouchot), scrubbed and debearded
150 ml dry white wine (or Pineau des Charentes)
steps: Soften the shallots and garlic in butter in a large pot for 3 minutes, add the wine and mussels, cover and steam on high heat for 5 to 6 minutes, shaking, until all open; discard any that stay closed.
Strain the cooking liquid into a pan, remove the top shell of each mussel and keep them warm in a dish.
Add the curry and saffron to the liquid and reduce by half.
Whisk the yolks with the crème fraîche, stir into the liquid and heat gently without boiling until creamy.
Pour the sauce over the mussels, scatter with parsley and serve with bread, as in La Rochelle.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 48 cleaned, pre-cooked snails (petits-gris, called cagouilles locally; tinned are fine)
2 tbsp goose fat or olive oil
100 g jambon de Bayonne or unsmoked bacon, diced
1/2 tsp piment d'Espelette and 1 tsp salt
steps: Brown the sausage meat and ham in the fat over medium heat for 8 minutes, add the onion and garlic and soften 5 minutes.
Sprinkle with flour and stir 1 minute, then add the wine, stock, bouquet garni, chilli and salt.
Add the drained snails and simmer gently, covered, for 1 hour 30 minutes until the sauce is thick and the sausage cooked through.
Serve hot in bowls with bread for dunking and a glass of the same white wine.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 1.5 kg mixed small fish and cuttlefish (sole, small rays, eels, seiches), cleaned and cut into pieces
steps: Soften the onions and garlic in the butter for 10 minutes over medium heat.
Add the potatoes, wine, water, bouquet garni, salt and pepper and simmer 15 minutes.
Add the cuttlefish first and simmer 10 minutes, then the firmer fish for 5 minutes and the delicate fish for the last 3 to 4 minutes until all flakes easily.
Serve in bowls over toasted bread, as made by the fishermen of Fouras and the Île d'Oléron.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

steps: Melt the fat in a pot over low heat and cook the garlic gently for 5 minutes without colouring.
Stir in the flour, then gradually add the water, season and simmer 20 minutes.
Drizzle the egg whites into the simmering soup while stirring gently so they set in threads.
Off the heat, whisk the yolks with the vinegar, temper with a ladle of soup and stir back in without boiling.
Pour over the bread in bowls; in Périgord this soup was served to newlyweds on their wedding night (tourin blanchi).
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 15 g fresh yeast or 7 g dried yeast
2 litres petit salé broth with its cabbage and carrots
600 g petit salé (salted pork belly), cooked in the broth
steps: Dissolve the yeast in the milk, mix with the flour, salt, eggs and duck fat and knead 10 minutes into a smooth dough.
Shape into a large ball, cover and leave to rise 1 hour 30 minutes until doubled.
Lower the ball into the gently simmering broth around the pork and vegetables, cover and cook 40 to 45 minutes, turning once halfway, until firm and cooked through.
Lift out, cut into thick slices, and serve with the petit salé and vegetables, as in Sarlat.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 1 kg waxy potatoes, peeled and sliced 3 mm thick
steps: Rinse the potato slices and dry them thoroughly in a cloth.
Heat the duck fat in a large heavy pan over medium-high heat, add the potatoes and cook 10 minutes, turning, until they start to colour.
Lower the heat, cover and cook 10 minutes until tender, then uncover and cook 5 to 10 minutes more until golden and crisp at the edges.
Toss in the garlic and parsley for the last 2 minutes, season and serve at once alongside confit or magret.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 500 g Swiss chard, spinach and sorrel leaves, chopped
200 g unsmoked bacon or ventrèche, finely chopped
150 g stale bread soaked in 150 ml milk
steps: Blanch the cabbage whole for 5 minutes, then separate the large leaves and finely chop the heart.
